author: lodekeeper-z
subject: refactor: simplify supported block proposal fields (#9993)
body:
## Motivation

Live block production is supported from Fulu onward. The proposal path
still conditionally adds fields introduced before Fulu, making required
fields look optional and assembling complete objects through casts.

Use that existing support boundary to simplify proposal assembly. No new
API rejection or support-policy change is needed.

## Changes

- Return a complete common body, including BLS-to-execution changes and
the parent-slot sync aggregate, without conditional field attachment or
a return cast.
- Require builder commitments and execution requests directly, retaining
the existing missing-field errors.
- Construct payload attributes with withdrawals and the parent beacon
block root already present. Keep Gloas full/empty-parent withdrawal
selection, the applied-parent check, and Gloas/Heze additions intact.
- Exercise the assembly functions directly with Fulu/Gloas/Heze
fixtures. Move the engine fee-recipient test out of the API suite and
cover successful next-slot preparation with a Fulu state.

This replaces the earlier API-guard approach. Blob-proof/sidecar removal
is left to its separate workstream. Historical sync, serving, state
transitions, and API selection logic are unchanged.

> This PR was rewritten with assistance from Hermes Agent using Astra.

author: Nazar Hussain
subject: fix: fall back to finalized safe block (#10027)
body:
## Motivation

Range sync can fail a batch with
`FORKCHOICE_ERROR_MISSING_PROTO_ARRAY_BLOCK` when finality advances past
the FCR confirmed root before the next FCR slot tick.

## Description

If the confirmed block no longer resolves, `getSafeExecutionBlockHash()`
uses the finalized block and logs the fallback. This keeps block import
running whether FCR is paused or running, addressing the review feedback
about covering both states.

This is intentionally a shallow fix. #10048 moves confirmed-root
ownership and finality recovery into the FCR module. After this PR
merges, the fallback will be reverted in #10048 before that PR is
merged.

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter @lodestar/fork-choice check-types`
- `pnpm --filter @lodestar/fork-choice lint`
- Targeted safe-block and FCR pause tests: 16 passed

author: bing
subject: perf(state-transition): optimize slashing penalties (#676)
body:
**Motivation**

Problem:
For one penalty at validator index 200,000, Lodestar-z would:
- Allocate/resize slashing_penalties to about 200,001 entries.
- Clear the entire buffer with @memset.
- Use only one entry.

**Description**

Store penalties compactly alongside `indices_to_slash`, so one slashing
now uses one penalty entry, regardless of its validator index.

Closes #675

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

codex

author: Cayman
subject: refactor(ssz): share byte-list hashing with generic uint8 lists (#673)
body:
`ByteListType` duplicates the value and serialized hashing algorithms
for `FixedListType(UintType(8))`. Alias those two entry points to the
generic implementation, preserving the public signatures and keeping one
implementation of byte packing, padding, and length mixing. This can
merge independently; together with #672 it gives byte lists the bounded
hashing kernel without a second implementation.

This implementation was primarily authored by Codex.

author: Cayman
subject: perf(ssz): bound list hashing scratch with batched accumulation (#672)
body:
SSZ list value and serialized hashing currently allocate a chunk array
proportional to the input. Stream fixed and variable list contents
through a Merkle accumulator with 64-chunk batches and one root per
supported tree level, keeping list-level scratch around 4 KiB. The
accumulator hashes partial batches without expanding missing leaves and
uses cached roots for empty trees. Child hashers retain their own
allocation behavior, and existing allocator-taking entry points remain
available.

Follow-up to #158. This branches from main and composes independently
with #644, #647, and #671. Managed `Hasher`, bit-list, and progressive
hashing remain separate follow-ups.

This implementation was primarily authored by Codex.

author: Cayman
subject: perf(ssz): stream list tree reads into output values (#671)
body:
Reading an SSZ list tree into a value allocates a temporary node-ID
array even when the destination already has sufficient capacity. Use the
existing bounded depth iterator for plain, chunked, and variable-element
lists so allocations are limited to the output value and its children.
Packed decoding, zero-subtree handling, and partial-value cleanup retain
their existing behavior.

Follow-up to #158. This PR is independent of the open proof and hashing
work.

This implementation was primarily authored by Codex.

author: Chen Kai
subject: refactor: remove redundant epoch benchmark reward synchronization (#668)
body:
## Motivation

The epoch benchmarks redundantly synchronize reward and penalty buffer
lengths that `EpochTransitionCache.init()` already establishes. The
rewards benchmark clones the same baseline state for every iteration,
and the full-epoch benchmark initializes its cache immediately before
processing.

## Description

Remove the two redundant synchronization calls, the rewards benchmark's
unused `io` field, and the now-unused benchmark-only
`syncRewardPenaltyLengths` helper.

The implementation was primarily AI-authored.

author: Chen Kai
subject: fix: prevent duplicate Altair sync cache cleanup (#651)
body:
## Motivation

During the Phase0-to-Altair upgrade, an allocation failure after the
next sync cache transfers to its reference-counted wrapper can release
the same cache twice.

## Description

- Scope raw-cache cleanup to RC construction for both sync caches, so
each resource has one cleanup owner. Preserve allocation order and error
propagation.
- Add allocation-failure regression coverage for both RC allocations and
the first allocation after ownership transfer, checking unchanged
existing caches and successful subsequent setup.

author: Cayman
subject: refactor(pmt): bound lazy hashing and compact proof depth (#647)
body:
Lazy branch-root hashing used recursion, and compact-proof
reconstruction could create trees deeper than the supported limit. Use a
fixed `max_depth` postorder stack and a pool-capacity visit budget for
hashing, preserving cached roots, shared subtrees, chunked-leaf scratch,
and opaque callbacks.

Validate compact-proof shape, canonical padding, and depth before
allocating the decoded descriptor or tree nodes. Excessive depth returns
`InvalidProofDepth` at the fallible construction boundary.

`getRoot()` keeps its existing infallible signature. Its panic guards
invalid native graph construction; raw native callers must preserve
acyclicity and the supported depth. The implementation map records these
contracts.

Implementation primarily AI-authored, with independent AI review.

author: Cayman
subject: refactor(pmt): compute proof descriptors with integer paths (#644)
body:
Proof descriptors previously converted every generalized index and
sibling path into allocated binary strings, then assembled another
string before packing bytes. This also leaked a duplicated key when a
following map allocation failed.

Keep paths as integers, sort them in the same lexical path order, and
write descriptor bits directly into the final buffer. Bound map growth
and checked size arithmetic.

author: lodekeeper-z
subject: fix: stabilize ptc benchmark seeds (#674)
body:
**Motivation**

The PTC performance fixtures call `crypto.randomBytes` without importing
Node's crypto module. On Node 22, `crypto` is the Web Crypto global, so
benchmark collection fails:

```text
TypeError: crypto.randomBytes is not a function
```

`@chainsafe/benchmark` 2.0.1 still exits successfully and persists only
24 results, silently dropping the shuffle suite.

**Description**

Use `deterministicBenchmarkSeed` for the per-slot and full-epoch PTC
fixtures, with labels separated by operation and validator count. Two
complete benchmark executions now each produce all 49 results, including
the 25 shuffle cases. The measured implementations are unchanged.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The implementation and verification were primarily AI-authored.

subject: feat(metrics): record exported but unset state transition gauges (#662)

- `lodestar_stfn_state_cloned_count`
- `epoch_transition_commit_seconds`,
- `effective_balance_updates_count`
- `validators_in_{activation,exit}_queue`,
- `new_seen_attesters_per_block_total`,
- `new_seen_attesters_effective_balance_per_block_total` and
- `attestations_per_block_total`


Note that for epoch transition commit, we deviate slightly, since we do

author: Marko Lazic
subject: refactor(builder): builder identity polling (#10045)
body:
**Motivation**

`waitForBuilder` polled every 10s. With 12s slots that drifts against
slot boundaries, so every 6th poll lands in the same slot as the
previous one and emits an identical log line. Builder activation
(`pending` -> `active` / `exited`) only happens at epoch transitions, so
polling more often than that gives no new information.
Also polls on every slot until `pending` status is received as deposit
can be processed in any slot.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: batch verify payload attestation signatures in blocks (#10055)
body:
Since #9761 `processPayloadAttestation` honors `verifySignatures`, which
is false on the default block import path because signatures are
expected to be verified in batch. `getBlockSignatureSets` did not
include payload attestations, so PTC signatures in blocks were not
verified anywhere. A proposer could include a payload attestation with
an arbitrary signature and lodestar would import the block while every
other client rejects it, see
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9761#discussion_r3921309021.

- add payload attestation signature sets to `getBlockSignatureSets`
- add slot-based `getPayloadTimelinessCommittee` to the state view,
`getEpochPTCs` does not serve the previous epoch which is needed at
epoch boundaries

The native state view binding needs to implement the new getter. A spec
test harness that catches this class of regression will follow in a
separate PR.

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: feat(builder): add bid ledger (#9975)
body:
## Motivation

The Builder needs a local record of submitted bids, wins, unsettled
payment exposure, and reveal safety before bid construction and reveal
wiring are added.

Nico's `nflaig/builder` branch prototypes this boundary. This PR
extracts it as an independent, reviewable service and tightens its
safety and mutation boundaries.

## Changes

- Enforce one submitted bid for each slot, parent execution hash, and
parent beacon root tuple.
- Require the fork-specific SSZ root of the complete locally signed bid
when recording a win, in addition to the payload identity fields.
- Count each winning bid once until its payment is explicitly known to
be reflected in Builder balance.
- Expose an exact-identity settlement operation rather than assuming bid
age proves payment settlement.
- Retain old winning bids while their payments remain unsettled; prune
old losing or settled bid records after three epochs.
- Reserve one exact unsigned envelope root for each selecting Beacon
block root and reject conflicting envelope material.
- Track successful publication separately from reservation so an exact
envelope can be retried safely after a failed attempt.
- Reject invalid or unsafe numeric bid values with structured errors.
- Return defensive record snapshots so callers cannot mutate ledger
state.
- Prune reveal records deterministically after three epochs, including
reveal records without a retained win entry.

## Scope

This PR adds no Builder or CLI wiring. It does not implement bid pricing
policy, bid construction, signing, publication, payload storage,
persistence, selection observation, reveal publication, or the runtime
signal that confirms a payment is reflected in Builder balance.

[#9974](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9974) owns the
initial bid-policy implementation, so this PR deliberately excludes
policy behavior.

Tracking:
[LOD-60](https://linear.app/kriso/issue/LOD-60/bid-ledger-01-track-one-shot-bids-and-unsettled-reveal-obligations)

Reference implementation: `nflaig/builder` at `99fd8fa9ad`

Historical validation base: `f22c5ce63e`

Validated head: `48f5c0c9d4`

## Integration evidence

The temporary [combined integration
branch](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar/tree/krisoshea/builder-direct-engine-integration)
composes the source, orchestration, store, policy, preferences, bid,
selection, and reveal components at `6c1aff6c66`. This is deterministic
composition evidence, not final runtime wiring, and it predates the
explicit payment-settlement behavior added here.

## Testing

The latest review amendment only spells out the uniqueness tuple in the
class documentation; ledger behavior is unchanged.

Validated locally on 2026-09-10 at `48f5c0c9d4`, using Node 24.13.0:

- 19 focused bid-ledger tests, including signed-bid mismatch with no
win/liability side effect
- Builder package type-check
- Biome on the changed files
- Builder build and module import check
- `git diff --check`

These are local results, not a claim about GitHub CI or a live BN/EL
run.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used during codebase research, implementation,
drafting, testing, and review. The submitted code and PR text were
reviewed and revised by the author, including manual edits and technical
decisions.

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: feat(builder): observe beacon node blocks (#9931)
body:
## Motivation

The Lodestar Builder needs a source beacon node API path for learning
whether its bid was selected without joining libp2p. This PR implements
the standard `block` SSE topic plus `getBlockV2` as a bounded
compatibility path.

Beacon APIs #630 and merged Lodestar #9832 also forward the signed
winning block directly to the selected external Builder. The main
purpose of that flow is to let the Builder help disseminate the block,
with timely win notification as an additional benefit. Maintainer input
is requested on whether this observer should remain as a compatibility
fallback alongside direct delivery.

## Changes

- Subscribe only to the standard `block` SSE topic.
- Deduplicate roots before asynchronous work and retain a FIFO window of
256 roots.
- Skip locally pre-Gloas slots and retrieve each new post-Gloas block by
root with `getBlockV2`.
- Use the Builder abort signal for both the SSE stream and block
requests.
- Retry 404, server, timeout, and non-input transport failures for up to
six attempts with five 200 ms delays. Other 4xx responses, cancellation,
decoding failures, input fetch errors, and structural failures are
terminal.
- Treat response version metadata as fork authority, require a
Gloas-compatible body, and verify the returned slot against the event.
- Preserve the exact signed bid, including later-fork fields,
exact-width values, and `BUILDER_INDEX_SELF_BUILD`.
- Dispatch observations concurrently through isolated `runOnBlock`
callbacks.

The existing API-client request timeout is unchanged. This PR bounds
attempts and explicit retry delays, not total wall-clock or
slot-relative time. Selection and reveal code will own deadline policy.

The observer starts after the existing genesis, configuration,
readiness, Gloas, and Builder identity gates. It joins the clock and
`BuilderStatusTracker` as a long-lived Builder background service and
shares their abort controller.

This PR does not add p2p, `block_gossip`, canonical-chain filtering,
local-bid matching, reveal behavior, metrics, reconnect, replay, restart
recovery, multi-BN failover, or a new API endpoint.

The observer intentionally evaluates blocks before SELECT-01 registers
its first production consumer so this compatibility path remains active
and evidenced. Event-time `executionOptimistic` comes from the
triggering event, while the response metadata is authoritative for the
fork. Terminally failed roots remain consumed until FIFO eviction;
REL-01 owns controlled reconciliation. Aggregate retrieval concurrency,
observer-specific metrics, and block-root recomputation before financial
decisions are tracked in SEC-01, QA-01, and SELECT-01 respectively.

## API behavior and compatibility

The standard `block` event contains the slot, beacon block root, and
execution optimism. `getBlockV2` supplies the signed fork-correct block
and `Eth-Consensus-Version` metadata. Imported non-head blocks remain
valid observations, so `head` and `head_v2` are not substitutes.

Lodestar emits `block` after state transition and fork-choice import.
Root lookup checks fork choice for presence, then serves the block from
the seen-block input cache or database. This ordering provides no
expected Lodestar event-before-block window, but the Beacon API does not
require equivalent ordering across clients, so bounded 404 retry remains
a cross-client precaution.

The implementation audit is recorded in merged [Builder docs PR
#13](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar-eip-7732-builder-docs/pull/13).
The provisional direct-Engine planning reconciliation is recorded in
merged [Builder docs PR
#18](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar-eip-7732-builder-docs/pull/18),
the reproducible real-BN and shutdown evidence in merged [Builder docs
PR
#19](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar-eip-7732-builder-docs/pull/19),
and the recent upstream PR audit in merged [Builder docs PR
#20](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar-eip-7732-builder-docs/pull/20).
Implementation evidence was posted to [beacon-APIs
#599](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/issues/599#issuecomment-5257353985).
Marco's open Lodestar PoCs
[#9854](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9854),
[#9875](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9875),
[#9876](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9876), and
[#9896](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9896) explore
optional event improvements separately.

The API-02 diff is limited to five Builder files. The latest review
fixes build on Nico's updated branch at
`09ea035863a5712eb417949f71e31c9d0f97f0fb`; no additional `unstable`
merge was made for these fixes.

Historical validation base: `f22c5ce63e`.

Historical specification baseline: consensus-specs `v1.7.0-alpha.14`.

Project issue:
[krisoshea-eth/lodestar#12](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar/issues/12).

## Testing

Validated locally on 2026-09-10 at
`d74cf21de82d8ef4a8ad4b65627d2df131b42a16`, with Node 24.13.0 and pnpm
11.0.0:

- 58 targeted tests across the observer, Builder lifecycle, identity,
readiness and payload store.
- Ordinary Builder package type-check.
- Changed-file Biome.
- Builder package build and module import check.
- `git diff --check`.

Dependencies were installed from this branch's lockfile and the Builder
dependency packages were rebuilt in an isolated checkout. The new
startup-log and warning regressions failed before the source changes and
passed afterward.

Coverage includes SSE wiring, cancellation, Gloas and Heze output,
signed-bid preservation, slot consistency, duplicate suppression,
bounded retry, decoding failures, FIFO eviction, self-builds, stream
failures and callback isolation. These are local results, not a fresh CI
or real-BN/EL run. The earlier real-BN and shutdown evidence remains in
Builder docs PR #19.

## AI assistance disclosure

- [x] External Contributors: I have read the contributor guidelines and
disclosed my usage of AI below.

> AI assistance was used for codebase research, implementation, testing,
and review. I reviewed and revised the submitted code and PR text, made
manual edits and technical decisions, and take responsibility for the
final result.

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: feat(builder): track proposer preferences (#9976)
body:
## Motivation

The Builder needs to track validated proposer preferences from its
source Beacon Node using the exact `(proposal_slot, dependent_root)`
identity. Preferences from a different proposer-shuffling branch must
not be used for a bid.

## Changes

- Subscribe to the existing `proposer_preferences` event through the API
client.
- Start the tracker during Builder initialization with the shared abort
signal.
- Retain separate dependent-root entries per proposal slot and preserve
the first validated duplicate.
- Expose exact lookup and prune past slots through the Builder clock.
- Ignore events after shutdown and log subscription failures or
unexpected stream closure.

The tracker retains received preferences directly, without cloning.
Nested-map initialization uses the existing `MapDef` utility.

## Scope

The BN owns signature and gossip validation. This PR does not derive the
dependent root for a payload-build branch, produce payload attributes,
construct bids, or add a separate reconnect/replay mechanism. Those
input and lifecycle decisions remain separate from subscribing and
retaining preferences. Sharing one Builder event stream and retrieving
cached BN preferences at startup/reconnect are follow-ups raised in
review, not behavior implemented here.

## Testing

Validated locally on 2026-09-10 at
`0970b619e0a385a54534eebfbc4d5c0d7b109c8d` with Node.js 24.13.0:

- 11 tracker tests plus one Builder lifecycle test.
- Builder type-check, changed-file Biome, build/import and `git diff
--check`.

Coverage includes Gloas/Heze events, exact lookup, duplicate handling,
pruning, subscription rejection, unexpected close and shared-signal
shutdown. The lifecycle tests use the mocked API stream; this is not a
real BN/EL run. Hosted Tests and Sim passed at the preceding head
`a7f841000c`; those results do not establish CI success for this
documentation amendment.

## Tracking

- [LOD-61
PREF-01](https://linear.app/kriso/issue/LOD-61/pref-01-track-proposer-preferences-by-slot-and-dependent-root)
- Dependent-root derivation: [LOD-15
BN-01](https://linear.app/kriso/issue/LOD-15/bn-01-confirm-source-bn-input-validation-and-publication-surfaces)

author: Cayman
subject: fix: release benchmark hasher scratch (#688)
body:
**Motivation**

The attestation, block, and state benchmarks initialize `Hasher` scratch
without releasing it. Cold runs retain each iteration's allocations and
omit teardown from the measured cost; preallocated scratch also survives
until process exit. Found while investigating #158.

**Description**

Pair all six scratch initializations with `defer
scratch.deinit(allocator)`: cold runs release scratch within the timed
call, and preallocated runs release it when `main` exits.

Validation: all three ERA-backed benchmarks built and ran in
ReleaseSafe; formatting, tidy, and lint passed.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The changes were primarily AI-authored.

author: Cayman
subject: fix: release bitlist json scratch (#677)
body:
**Motivation**

Malformed BitList JSON or an allocation failure after hex decoding runs
both `defer` and `errdefer` on the same byte buffer. The new regressions
reproduce the double-free on main:

```text
Build Summary: 4/6 steps succeeded (1 failed); 25/27 tests passed (2 crashed)
```

Related to #158.

**Description**

Remove the duplicate cleanup in `BitListType.deserializeFromJson`. Cover
invalid hex, missing delimiters, length rejection, and every allocation
failure after scanner setup.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The changes were primarily AI-authored.

author: Cayman
subject: refactor: share bytelist tree conversion (#680)
body:
**Motivation**

ByteList retains a separate tree-to-value implementation with temporary
traversal allocation, while the generic uint8-list implementation
already streams its reads.

Related to #158.

**Description**

Alias `ByteListType.tree.toValue` to `GenericList.tree.toValue`. Add the
existing `canMemcpySsz` fast path to plain packed-list reads so
byte-compatible types copy each chunk once.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The changes were primarily AI-authored.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: refactor: derive gloas p2p max sizes from ssz types (#10053)
body:
Since #10042 the gloas progressive lists carry their limits in the ssz
types, so the max sizes of `SignedAggregateAndProof`,
`AttesterSlashing`, `DataColumnSidecar` and `SignedExecutionPayloadBid`
already equal the spec p2p bounds under both presets.

- bound gossip and reqresp objects by the ssz type max size or
`MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE`, whichever is smaller, dropping the gloas special
cases in `getGossipSSZMaxSize` and the reqresp size clamp
- remove the ssz type max size checks in gossip encoding, unreachable
now that the gossip bound never exceeds the type max size
- add a minimal preset test asserting the derived sizes match the preset
p2p bounds for gloas and heze

Follow-up to #10042

author: twoeths
subject: fix: dos protection for NetworkProcessor (#10039)
body:
**Motivation**

- NetworkProcessor holds unverified messages and was not designed with
DOS protection in mind

**Description**

- only support to buffer up to 5 roots per message slot, this is to
prevent OOM
  - cap it via `bufferedRootsBySlot = new MapDef<Slot, Set<RootHex>>`
- but support up to 32 searched roots per message slot. This is to make
sure the node is always synced by searching for all roots, and we will
penalize peers in UnknownBlockInput per `pruneFinalized()`
- cap it via `searchedRootsBySlot = new MapDef<Slot, MapDef<RootHex,
SearchedRootEntry>>`
- changed data structure
  - awaitingMessagesByBlockRoot is tracked per topic, same to envelope
- unite `unknownBlocksBySlot` and `unknownEnvelopesBySlot `to
`searchedRootsBySlot `so that we can cap roots per slot easier

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-bounty/lodestar/issues/19

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

- created with the help of Claude

---------

author: Chen Kai
subject: perf(state-transition): use native PTC sampling (#9903)
body:
**Motivation**

Reduce Gloas/Heze PTC processing overhead in historical accumulator
transitions. Related to #9771.

**Description**

- Use native whole-epoch PTC sampling via
`@chainsafe/lodestar-z/shuffle` (pinned to `1.1.0-dev.58a9fcbc13`).
- Reuse retained PTC window subtrees and cached hashes; build only the
new epoch.
- Verify parity with the TS sampler and re-enable Gloas/Heze historical
accumulator tests.

Gloas/Heze mainnet historical accumulator vectors pass at approximately
7 seconds locally (spec v1.7.0-beta.0, Node 25.2.1, default spec-test
hasher).

author: twoeths
subject: chore: persist invalid signed block with block root file name (#10060)
body:
**Motivation**

- when investigating #9925 I found it's a bit inconvenient: we loged
REJECTED block by block root, but stored it by the root of signed block
- for example:

```
-rw-r--r--  1 devops devops  1850 Aug 27 14:39 SignedBeaconBlock_0x1d1f49984de978d6f41dce95c69e528dcd163d2f00e215053c627c0839bf85c1.ssz
```

we never see this root in our log

**Description**

- still store the whole signed block, but use block root as file name

body:
**Motivation**

- when there are REJECTED block, the log was not detailed enough, and
some log missed block root.
- for example ` Gossip validation beacon_block rejected
peerId=16...mJKujG, clientAgent=Lighthouse,
clientVersion=Lighthouse/v8.1.3/x86_64-linux,
code=BLOCK_ERROR_UNKNOWN_PROPOSER, proposerIndex=2349064`

**Description**

- for REJECTED error code of block/column/payload, always include slot
and full root

part of #9925

author: Cayman
subject: feat: add flat file storage for data columns (#8899)
body:
**Motivation**

Keeping data column sidecars in LevelDB adds compaction and hot-to-cold
archival overhead. Flat files also allow requested columns to be read
without loading every column for a block.

**Description**

- Store newly persisted data columns in
`data_columns/<12-digit-slot>/0x<block-root>.dcol`.
- Use a versioned header, column bitmap, offset table, and independently
Snappy-compressed columns for targeted reads.
- Serialize writes per slot and commit them atomically.
- Rebuild the flat-file slot index on startup while retaining
unfinalized files, remove non-canonical files, and prune expired slot
directories.
- Keep existing LevelDB columns as a fallback, so no column-data
migration is required. Blob sidecar storage is unchanged.
- Add canonical range handling, Gloas payload handling, flat-file
metrics, and Grafana panels.
- Resolve canonical column-range roots from fork choice, recent
head-state roots, or the archive slot-to-root index without loading and
hashing full blocks.
- Populate the archive slot-to-root index atomically when blocks are
written, and remove entries when blocks are pruned.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: perf: replace snappyjs with snappy-wasm (#10062)
body:
**TLDR**

- Replace snappyjs with `@chainsafe/snappy-wasm@^0.5.2` for reqresp and
spec fixtures, sharing the library used by gossip. Update native
`snappy` to `^7.4.3` for compression and storage.
- Complete block-stream decoding is **2.74-3.04x as fast as snappyjs**
in local benchmarks. The 84 B case adds **0.77 µs**; short retention
runs show higher peak RSS.
- 562 targeted unit/spec tests passed, plus fixture-reader checks,
builds, type checks, lint, native portability and independent review.

Reqresp follows gossip's existing `Buffer.alloc`/`decompress_into`
pattern, preserving framing, checksums, size validation, offset input
views and output behavior. All compressed spec-fixture readers,
including gossip validation fixtures, use `decompress()` and return
independently owned Uint8Arrays. Remove snappyjs dependencies, ambient
declarations and obsolete benchmark cases.

Reqresp decoder measurements below are median microseconds per operation
across three fresh processes per case/backend; lower is better. They
execute the actual baseline decoder from `acdde443` and the final
decoder, including checksum verification and output handling. Complete
streams include frame parsing and assembly.

| Workload, Uint8Array input | snappyjs 0.7.0 | WASM 0.5.0 | WASM 0.5.2
|
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 84 B compressed frame | 1.665 | 2.233 | 2.430 |
| 1 KiB mixed compressed frame | 4.301 | 3.279 | 3.371 |
| 64 KiB mixed compressed frame | 194.870 | 54.696 | 54.528 |
| 64 KiB all-zero compressed frame | 225.466 | 102.350 | 105.439 |
| 64 KiB random, uncompressed-frame control | 5.476 | 5.416 | 5.455 |
| Goerli block, average frame | 151.173 | 41.717 | 38.413 |
| Goerli block, complete stream, 139,405 B decoded | 521.723 | 188.378 |
171.347 |
| Existing block fixture, complete stream, 146,755 B decoded | 565.225 |
252.961 | 206.296 |

Peak RSS in separate four-second retention runs, averaged across three
fresh processes:

| Workload | snappyjs 0.7.0, MiB | WASM 0.5.0, MiB | WASM 0.5.2, MiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Large frames, about 5.8 MiB retained | 140.2 | 153.1 | 156.7 |
| Small frames, about 2.2 MiB retained | 159.7 | 202.2 | 225.3 |

These runs use each decoder's maximum throughput with a fixed output
ring, so they process different amounts of data. Peak RSS includes
warmup. They do not establish long-term memory bounds or whole-node
performance.

Native Snappy 7.4.3 was approximately 9-14% slower on Goerli block
compression in these runs; its RSS results varied by workload. Full
native measurements are below.

<details>
<summary>Native compression and storage measurements</summary>

Each cell shows **snappy 7.2.2 / 7.4.3**, in synchronous µs per
operation, across four fresh processes per workload/version. These
execute the actual reqresp encoder and storage wrappers; storage timings
exclude filesystem I/O.

| Payload | Reqresp encoding | Storage compression | Storage
decompression |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 KiB mixed | 58.600 / 60.022 | 47.626 / 48.557 | 19.813 / 19.709 |
| 64 KiB all-zero | 24.748 / 25.414 | 15.508 / 16.566 | 57.754 / 57.186
|
| 64 KiB random | 26.770 / 26.634 | 13.169 / 13.353 | 10.783 / 11.040 |
| Goerli block, 139,405 B | 161.921 / 176.216 | 126.623 / 143.865 |
48.703 / 48.676 |
| 128 KiB synthetic column-like data | 53.853 / 54.969 | 23.010 / 22.631
| 18.737 / 18.741 |

Native timing uses identical GC segments outside the synchronous timer,
with event-loop turns every 32 operations. Compare versions within this
table; its GC schedule differs from the decoder measurements above.

Separate native memory probes perform up to 4,096 operations per
process, retaining eight outputs, without forced GC during work. Four
runs cover each version, both mixed 64 KiB and synthetic 128 KiB
payloads, and all three operations.

All 48 native memory runs completed the full workload. Mean RSS
increases from the initial snapshot are below; each cell is **7.2.2 /
7.4.3**, in MiB.

| Workload | Sampled peak increase | Increase after GC |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 128 KiB synthetic, reqresp encoding | 99.6 / 142.4 | 91.8 / 121.3 |
| 128 KiB synthetic, storage compression | 99.8 / 126.3 | 99.8 / 124.1 |
| 128 KiB synthetic, storage decompression | 98.9 / 94.5 | 98.9 / 62.6 |
| 64 KiB mixed, reqresp encoding | 74.9 / 83.8 | 74.6 / 82.8 |
| 64 KiB mixed, storage compression | 179.0 / 255.1 | 179.0 / 175.1 |
| 64 KiB mixed, storage decompression | 67.4 / 94.4 | 67.4 / 93.6 |

RSS was sampled after each 32-operation batch. Retained RSS includes
allocator effects and does not identify live output buffers. These
bounded probes do not establish production memory limits.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Method and validation</summary>

- Linux x86-64, Intel Core i7-1360P, Node v24.13.0, pinned to CPU 2. All
72 decoder timing, 18 decoder retention, 120 native timing and 48 native
memory processes ran sequentially. Version order is balanced for each
workload.
- Decoder timing warms up for at least 40 ms and collects nine samples
of at least 20 ms, including event-loop turns. No forced GC occurs
during those samples. Native timing collects eight samples targeting 50
ms of synchronous work with a fixed allocation/GC schedule.
- Production TypeScript is snapshotted with only import redirection and
type stripping. Correctness checks cover decoded bytes, checksums,
nonzero input offsets, input preservation, retained outputs and
cross-version native roundtrips.
- 292 unit tests passed across reqresp, gossip, existing flat-file
storage tests and era. The PR adds 12 reqresp/gossip compatibility
cases.
- 270 selected spec tests passed: 260 minimal BeaconBlock/BeaconState
static SSZ, four minimal merkle-proof and six mainnet Deneb
NewPayloadRequest cases.
- Fixture-reader checks cover bytes, SSZ roundtrips and ownership using
mainnet-preset fixtures, including 2.7 MB states. Static reader checks
use cached v1.7.0-alpha.8 fixtures; the gossip reader uses v1.7.0-beta.0
fixtures. The existing networking spec runner is disabled, so the latter
is a separate reader check.
- Type checks and builds passed for reqresp, spec-test-util and
beacon-node. Lint, native portability and `git diff --check` passed.
Independent review covered the code, dependency resolution, output
ownership and benchmark methodology.

</details>

Written with Codex and Claude Code. Separate agents reviewed the
implementation and benchmark methodology.

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: fix(api): respect cancellation during event stream setup (#10065)
body:
## Motivation

`eventstream()` loads EventSource asynchronously before attaching its
abort listener. If the signal is already aborted, or aborts during that
await, it still creates a connection and misses the abort event.

I reproduced this while checking Builder shutdown for #10064. It also
exists on `unstable`, so this fix is independent of that refactor.

## Description

Check the signal after loading EventSource and before constructing it.
Reject cancelled setup with the existing `ErrorAborted`, following the
HTTP client's cancellation convention. Established connections keep
their existing abort/close behavior.

No reconnect, replay or Builder runtime changes.

## Testing

Base `acdde443d29e59fdbb28f1762b7e2ae6e91faec0`.

- Both cancelled-setup regressions failed before the fix and pass
afterward.
- Seven focused tests pass across client cancellation and the existing
SSE server suite.
- A real loopback SSE connection confirms client abort releases the
server subscription. Existing malformed-event and throwing-consumer
tests still pass.
- API type-check, changed-file Biome, build/import and `git diff
--check` pass. API dependencies were built in an isolated checkout using
the pinned SSZ 1.7.0; the main checkout was untouched.

The setup race is tested deterministically with a mocked EventSource
constructor. The loopback test covers established-connection teardown,
not a measured live-network leak or the complete Builder lifecycle. Full
hosted CI is still pending.

Tracking [REL-01](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar/issues/22).
This addresses its transport setup cancellation item, not the broader
recovery scope.

> This PR was written with OpenAI Codex assistance and manually reviewed
and tested with Codex.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: refactor: compute payload attributes once in `prepareForNextSlot` (#10056)
body:
When we propose the next slot and a client is subscribed to
`payload_attributes`, `prepareForNextSlot` computes the payload
attributes twice: once for the SSE event and again in
`prepareExecutionPayload` for the `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` call, both
from the same state and fee recipient. The second run repeats
`getExpectedWithdrawals` (and the target gas limit lookup post-gloas)
for nothing.

- `prepareExecutionPayload` accepts precomputed attributes and only
builds them itself when none are passed, block production paths are
unchanged
- `prepareForNextSlot` passes the attributes of the emitted event to the
EL preparation

Cost of the second run, measured as one `getPayloadAttributesForSSE`
call on a 250k validator capella state with warm balance and validator
caches. The cases differ in how many validators the withdrawals sweep
probes before it fills the 16 slots:

| sweep case | probes | per run |
|---|---|---|
| best case, every probe is a withdrawal | 16 | 6.2 us |
| 10% eth1 credentials | 220 | 35 us |
| worst case, bounded sweep without candidates | 16384 | 2.8 ms |

Mainnet is close to the best case, so this saves microseconds per
proposal and only when a client is subscribed to the event. It is a
cleanup, not a performance improvement.

Follow-up to
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10037#pullrequestreview-5148972904

author: Lodekeeper
subject: test: stop gating CI on high-variance data-availability benchmarks (#10074)
body:
## Problem

`benchmark.yml` has been intermittently red on `unstable` for the last
~2 days. The failures are **false positives**, not real regressions —
the "failing" commits are unrelated dep bumps and refactors (#10063
builder rename, #10061 lodestar-z bump, #10066 libp2p-quic bump) that
cannot affect the benches that trip.

## Root cause

Two sets of benchmarks have run-to-run variance well above the hard
`threshold: 3` gate on the shared `warp-ubuntu-2204-x64-4x` runner:

1. **`dataColumnSidecarsByRange.test.ts`** (new in #8899) — reads real
LevelDB + flat-file data and, per its own header, relies on "warm
LevelDB and OS caches". Disk I/O on a shared virtualized runner is
highly variable. Its `archive index` / `head state` × `columns` ×
`{legacy, flat files}` benches are the main driver of the last-2-days
spike (observed 4-8.6×).
2. **`blobs.test.ts` KZG reconstruction** — CPU-heavy crypto with low
iteration counts. #9543 already reduced the workload to the smallest
blob count, but even the 6-blob reconstruct still trips the gate
(observed `x206.6`, 13 runs).

Every push to `unstable` persists a new rolling baseline to S3, so one
anomalously-fast run makes the next normal run look like a >3×
regression, and that run's slow numbers then become the baseline —
self-perpetuating reds. Examples from the last 2 days:

- unstable #10063: `archive index / 8 slots / 8 columns / legacy` x6.6,
`head state / 1 slots / 128 columns / legacy` x6.1, `reconstruct half
the blobs` x206.6
- unstable #10066 (libp2p-quic bump): `head state / 1 slots / 128
columns / legacy` x4.2, `Array.fill - length 1000000` x3.2
- unstable #10061 (lodestar-z bump): `send data - 1000 4096B messages`
x6.5, `head state / 8 slots / 8 columns / legacy` x8.2

A dep bump touching `Array.fill` timing or disk I/O is impossible —
clear variance signature.

## Fix

- **`dataColumnSidecarsByRange.test.ts`** (3 benches): raise the gate to
`threshold: 10`. Observed variance is 4-8.6×, so 10 clears it with
margin while still failing on a genuine >10× regression (per review
feedback from @nazarhussain).
- **`blobs.test.ts`** KZG reconstruction: mark **report-only** via
`noThreshold`. It hit x206 off a poisoned baseline, where no finite
threshold is meaningful; the bench still runs and posts to the
comparison comment so a real regression stays visible to a human
reviewer.

Narrowly scoped — only the benches proven high-variance are touched; the
rest of the suite stays gated as before.

🤖 Generated with AI assistance

---------

Co-authored-by: Nico Flaig <nflaig@protonmail.com>

subject: fix: align gloas external signer requests with remote signing api (#10071)
body:
Aligns the external signer client with the Glamsterdam additions to the
remote signing api (ethereum/remote-signing-api#28). All new gloas
payloads are `version`-wrapped like `BLOCK_V2` and
`AGGREGATE_AND_PROOF_V2`, and the PTC signing type is named after the
message the validator produces, consistent with `ATTESTATION` and
`SYNC_COMMITTEE_MESSAGE` which also carry only the signed data.

- rename `PAYLOAD_ATTESTATION` to `PAYLOAD_ATTESTATION_MESSAGE`, body
key `payload_attestation_message`
- wrap `execution_payload_envelope`, `payload_attestation_message`,
`proposer_preferences` and `builder_request_auth` in `{version, data}`,
version is the fork at the message slot
- add web3signer e2e cases for the four signing types, skipped until the
test image supports gloas

The same request shapes are implemented in
Consensys-Incorporated/web3signer#1192.

author: bing
subject: fix(network): actually dial QUIC before TCP when a peer advertises both (#10077)
body:
**Motivation**

Passing `[quic, tcp]` to the peer store does not mean quic was
prioritized. `js-lip2p` re-sorts peer addresses before dialing, using
its [default
sorter](https://github.com/libp2p/js-libp2p/blob/c484322727af01112c1f657a35239e910c413c08/packages/libp2p/src/connection-manager/address-sorter.ts#L23-L29)
which ranks TCP ahead of every other transport (see
[`reliableTransportsFirst`](https://github.com/libp2p/js-libp2p/blob/main/packages/utils/src/multiaddr/sorters.ts#L13)),
so we were still dialing TCP before QUIC even when QUIC was enabled.

Spec explicitly says to prefer QUIC > TCP
[p2p-interface.md#L155-L162](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/f21dac06e99743b1e98bb80297897b96520c942b/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L155-L162):

> All implementations MUST support the QUIC (UDP) libp2p transport and
the TCP libp2p transport. [...] QUIC is the primary transport. When a
peer is reachable over both TCP and QUIC, clients SHOULD prioritise
peer's QUIC addresses.

**Description**

Add a `connectionManager.addressSorter` that ranks quic-v1 addresses
first when the QUIC transport is enabled.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

found and fixed with fable.
Found while auditing our quic readiness in preparation for deprecating
mplex

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: reject gloas blocks with legacy deposits on deserialization (#10080)
body:
Gloas blocks still carry `deposits: ProgressiveList[Deposit]` even
though the list must be empty since Fulu, and it was the only block
operation list without a decode-time limit because ssz rejected `limit:
0`. A peer can send a 10 MiB block filled with legacy deposits which we
fully deserialize, hash and add to the seen caches before the unknown
parent IGNORE, well ahead of the nonzero deposits REJECT.

- bump `@chainsafe/ssz` to v1.8.0 which allows a zero limit on
progressive lists and validates list limits, `ArrayOf` now defaults to
`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` instead of `Infinity` which is no longer
accepted, the finite list type has identical serialization and JSON
- set `limit: 0` on the gloas `Deposits` list (inherited by heze), a
non-empty deposits range now fails at the ssz boundary before any
element is materialized, covering gossip, req/resp and JSON block
publishing, which also gives the early REJECT ordering of
ethereum/consensus-specs#5630 since decoding fails ahead of every IGNORE
- remove the gossip nonzero deposits check and the `NON_ZERO_DEPOSITS`
error code, a block with deposits can no longer reach gossip validation
so the check was unreachable, same as #10042 did for the other operation
lists, the state transition keeps enforcing the zero deposit count
- the gloas and heze `invalid_old_style_deposit_rejected` and
`invalid_too_many_deposits` sanity vectors now fail at decode, which the
spec runner already treats as the expected outcome for an ssz limit
violation

The gloas and heze ssz_static block vectors still carry legacy deposits,
see ethereum/consensus-specs#5640, they keep passing because the spec
runner does not propagate list limits.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-bounty/lodestar/issues/22

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix(network): declare @libp2p/utils as a runtime dependency of beacon-node (#10086)
body:
## Motivation

#10077 added a runtime import of `@libp2p/utils` in
`packages/beacon-node/src/network/libp2p/index.ts`:

```ts
import {loopbackAddressLast, publicAddressesFirst, reliableTransportsFirst} from "@libp2p/utils";
```

(used in the multiaddr sort comparator). However `@libp2p/utils` was
declared only under beacon-node's **`devDependencies`** — before #10077
it was used solely in tests.

The production Docker image runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prod`
(see `Dockerfile`), which prunes `devDependencies`. So the package is
absent at runtime and the beacon node crashes on startup:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@libp2p/utils' imported from /usr/app/packages/beacon-node/lib/network/libp2p/index.js
```

## Description

Move `@libp2p/utils` from `devDependencies` to `dependencies` in
`packages/beacon-node/package.json` (lockfile updated accordingly).
Version is unchanged (`^7.4.0`); the only change is the section move, so
it is now retained by the `--prod` install.

This matches how `packages/reqresp` already declares its runtime use of
the same package.

Fixes the startup regression introduced by #10077.

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: test: verify imported block in unknown-block sync simulation (#10054)
body:
## Motivation

The unknown-block sync simulation can fail when manual publication
succeeds because the target already arrived over gossip. The retained
API-02 failure logged an already-known target and returned HTTP 200.
This is a separate simulation race correction, not a Builder observer
change.

## Description

- Accept successful publication while preserving the existing
expected-error handling.
- After waiting for sync, query the target header by its exact block
root and require a successful response. A later head alone does not
prove that target arrived.
- Keep unexpected publication errors and missing/failed root lookups as
assertion failures.
- Follow Nazar's review by removing the redundant returned-root
comparison and the separate unit-test file for test utilities. The final
patch changes only the existing simulation helper.

## Validation

The simplified patch passed the complete local Docker multifork
simulation on 11 September, from 16:55:53 to 17:02:06 UTC, exit 0.
Ordinary CLI type-check, changed-file Biome and git diff --check also
passed. It used the existing pinned dependencies and Geth
v1.16.7/Lighthouse unstable-d235f2c images. Test containers and the
simulation network were cleaned up; existing Kurtosis resources were
untouched.

The earlier 10 focused regressions belonged to the pre-review patch and
were removed at review. They are not claimed as part of this head. No
new hosted CI success is claimed. This Electra simulation does not prove
the separate Gloas Builder bid/selection/reveal lifecycle.

## AI assistance

This change was reviewed and tested with OpenAI Codex assistance.

author: Cayman
subject: perf: stream compact proof generation (#683)
body:
**Motivation**

Compact-proof generation expands descriptor bits and recursively
allocates and concatenates arrays of leaves. Descriptor validation from
#647 already establishes the shape and depth needed for a bounded
traversal.

The descriptor is caller-controlled through
`BeaconStateView.createMultiProof`. Reserving its entire declared output
before navigating the source tree can amplify malformed input into a
large allocation, as reported in
[review](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/pull/683#discussion_r3979609729).

Related to #158.

**Description**

Traverse packed descriptor bits with a bounded pending-node stack and
grow the output as traversal reaches witnesses. Invalid source paths
release partial output; opaque materialization retains its existing
temporary ownership.

Add regressions for impossible paths before and after a valid witness,
output growth failures, and opaque-materialization failures. A
descriptor declaring roughly 128 KiB of output now reports the invalid
path with a 1 KiB output budget.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The changes were primarily AI-authored.

author: Cayman
subject: perf: stream bitlist tree reads (#679)
body:
**Motivation**

BitList tree-to-value conversion allocates a node-ID array even when the
destination already has enough capacity. Ordinary list conversion was
addressed in #671.

Related to #158.

**Description**

Read chunks with `Node.DepthIterator` directly into the resized BitList
output. Boundary and implicit-zero tests disable allocations after
reserving output capacity and verify that source roots remain unchanged.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The changes were primarily AI-authored.

author: Cayman
subject: docs: retire security implementation map (#696)
body:
**Motivation**

The [security-maintenance
rule](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/blob/02d61c2b9c9ca7361ea852b8f5458854f8522197/AGENTS.md#L20-L23)
requires routine implementation changes to update a central inventory:

```text
Update the normative threat model only when the security contract changes; otherwise update the implementation map.
```

This leaves contributors unsure which changes need an entry and makes
independent PRs conflict in the same table. Much of the inventory
duplicates code, tests, and existing API documentation.

**Description**

Retire the implementation map and make security documentation
maintenance depend on changes to the contract.

- Delete `docs/security/IMPLEMENTATION_MAP.md` and its references.
- Update `AGENTS.md` and `THREAT_MODEL.md` so changes that preserve
security objectives, trust assumptions, trust boundaries, and supported
caller obligations require no security-documentation update. Keep the
requirement to verify actual call paths before downgrading findings.
- Preserve the single-addon-version restriction in `THREAT_MODEL.md`.
Keep addon compatibility, `BeaconStateView.createFromBytes()`
provenance, and `EpochTransitionCache` lifetime requirements beside the
owning modules and APIs. Other enduring preconditions already have local
documentation.
- Use one-line public binding comments for STF concurrency and cache
teardown, including both teardown exports and phase0 checkpoint
computation. Preserve the requirement to coordinate across workers.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

This change was primarily AI-authored with Codex.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: test: fix finalized sync e2e cleanup (#10098)
body:
**Motivation**

Unstable e2e runs started failing/flaking in `finalizedSync.test.ts`
with an unhandled `QUEUE_ERROR_QUEUE_ABORTED` rejection while a
validator was still producing a Gloas block.

The test registers cleanup callbacks in a LIFO stack. It registered
`bn.close()`, then validator shutdown, then a second `bn.close()` with a
comment saying the beacon node should stop after validators. Because the
callbacks are popped, that second `bn.close()` actually ran before
validator shutdown, which can abort the state regenerator queue while
the validator is still producing.

**Description**

- Remove the duplicate Node A `bn.close()` so the existing LIFO order
shuts validators down before closing the beacon node they use.
- Remove the duplicate Node B `bn2.close()` registration.
- Add a short comment documenting the reverse cleanup order so future
edits preserve the dependency ordering.

**Verification**

- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm vitest run --project e2e
packages/beacon-node/test/e2e/sync/finalizedSync.test.ts` (passed twice,
including teardown)
- `git diff --check`

Observed in
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/35008064689.

guidelines](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/unstable/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-assistance-notice)

author: Cayman
subject: perf: bound bitlist hashing workspace (#678)
body:
**Motivation**

BitList value and byte hashing allocate a complete chunk buffer for
every hash. Ordinary lists already have bounded accumulation through
#672.

Related to #158.

**Description**

Use `MerkleAccumulator` in both BitList hashing paths, with workspace
independent of input length.

- `BitListType.hashTreeRoot` asserts the typed value's length and
storage invariants, passes full chunks directly to the accumulator, and
pads only a partial tail.
- `BitListType.serialized.hashTreeRoot` validates the bytes before
hashing and passes complete 256-bit chunks directly. A final chunk
containing the delimiter is copied and stripped before accumulation.
Both paths mix in the bit length.
- Extend allocation-disabled comparisons against tree roots around byte,
chunk, and 63/64/65-chunk boundaries.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The changes were primarily AI-authored.

author: Chen Kai
subject: fix: accept bigint proof indices (#699)
body:
**Motivation**

Addresses #621, item 35. `getSingleProof` is declared with a `bigint`
generalized index, and Lodestar's historical summaries API passes the
SSZ `getPathInfo()` result directly. The binding currently requires a JS
number and rejects that normal call:

```text
TypeError: Argument 1 must be a number
```

**Description**

Accept `js.BigInt` and convert directly to `u64` with the lossless flag
checked. Reject negative or oversized values with `InvalidGindex`
instead of truncating them. Keep the existing tree-level error handling
for zero and unavailable indices.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation was primarily AI-authored with Codex, with AI-assisted
review and validation.

author: Cayman
subject: refactor: bound variable vector hashing (#682)
body:
**Motivation**

Variable-element vectors keep every child root in a vector-sized stack
array while hashing values or serialized elements.

Related to #158.

**Description**

Keep the direct path for at most 64 elements and accumulate larger
vectors with bounded scratch. Serialized hashing continues to use the
fallible offset iterator. Child hashers retain their allocation
contracts. Tests cover empty and populated children across batch
boundaries, root equivalence, and malformed offsets.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The changes were primarily AI-authored.

author: Chen Kai
subject: fix: clean up inactivity scores (#702)
body:
**Motivation**

Addresses #621, item 46. Loading an Altair-or-later state with a Phase0
seed creates a new inactivity-scores subtree. Its block-scoped cleanup
expires before container decoding, while the container's early-error
cleanup excludes override nodes. A later decoding error therefore leaks
the scores subtree.

The new regression leaves 35 pool nodes allocated on the original code
on both presets. Mainnet reports:

```text
expected 168137, found 168172
```

**Description**

Override inactivity scores only when the seed already has a scores
subtree to reuse. For Phase0 seeds, let normal container deserialization
create and own the scores, so its existing field/root cleanup handles
failures. Borrowed seed subtrees keep their existing ownership. Fresh
scores now follow normal container field order; inputs with multiple
malformed fields can therefore report a different first decoding error.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation was primarily AI-authored with Codex, with independent
AI-assisted review and validation.

author: Nazar Hussain
subject: test: repair minimal preset state transition baseline (#704)
body:

The minimal preset test suite is unusable: 117 pass, 2 fail, 45 crash.
All 45 crashes come from one place. Minimal leaves Electra unscheduled
at `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH`, and the Electra test fixture multiplies that
epoch to build a slot, which overflows.

**Description**

Use genesis as the fork epoch when Electra is unscheduled. Take the
slot, proposer, parent root and payload timestamp from the state instead
of hardcoded mainnet values. Expect the preset's committee cap, and skip
the two mainnet weak-subjectivity tables on other presets.

Minimal now passes: 162 pass, 2 skipped. Mainnet is unchanged. Tests
only, no production code.

Refs #621, item 41.

author: Cayman
subject: refactor: extract bit array module (#693)
body:
**Motivation**

Packed-bit values live inside SSZ schema modules, coupling ordinary bit
operations to SSZ. Bounded and progressive bitlists also duplicate the
same growable storage and mutation code.

This continues the library organization and coupling work in #158.

**Description**

Extract packed-bit values into a standalone `bit_array` module that
depends only on `std`.

- `BitList(.{ .limit = n })` and `BitList(.{ .limit =
bit_array.unlimited })` share one implementation, with the optional
limit resolved at compile time.
- `BitVector(n)` retains inline storage and allocator-free mutation.
- `setAssumeCapacity()` is infallible and asserts its existing-length
precondition; callers use `set()` when growth or recoverable limit
errors are needed.
- `BitListType`, `ProgressiveBitListType`, and `BitVectorType` use the
standalone values. Remove the old SSZ value exports and update callers
directly, without compatibility wrappers. Serialization, hashing, and
tree views remain in SSZ.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation primarily AI-authored, with maintainer-directed API
design.

author: Cayman
subject: refactor(ssz): centralize chunked-leaf mutation bookkeeping (#690)
body:
**Motivation**

The packed SSZ setter currently coordinates copying, dirty tracking,
payload mutation, and hash invalidation through direct access to pool
internals. Move that bookkeeping into scoped operations at the layers
that own it, as part of #158.

**Description**

Centralize chunked-leaf mutation bookkeeping while preserving commit and
snapshot semantics.

- `TreeViewState.editChunkedLeaf` prepares private storage and registers
the pending change.
- `Node.Id.editChunkedLeaf` invokes the packing callback, updates the
valid length, and invalidates the cached root.

The SSZ caller passes its existing packing function directly. All
fallible preparation completes before the callback runs. Shared leaves
are copied on the first write; subsequent pending writes reuse storage
without allocating.

Add coverage for snapshot isolation, repeated writes, hash invalidation,
sparse leaves, length growth, allocation failures, and every supported
basic element type.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation primarily AI-authored.

author: Cayman
subject: perf: stream progressive tree serialization (#686)
body:
**Motivation**

Fixed-element progressive-list tree serialization first materializes the
entire list value, including a node-ID traversal array.

Related to #158.

**Description**

Add `progressive.NodeIterator` and stream directly into the caller's
output. Bound traversal depth, check size arithmetic and output
capacity, expand implicit zero subtrees, and validate the right-spine
terminator. Child serializers keep their own workspace contracts. Share
`chunkCountForLength()` across value and tree paths.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The changes were primarily AI-authored.

author: Cayman
subject: perf: bound progressive merkleization workspace (#685)
body:
**Motivation**

Progressive Merkleization allocates subtree-root storage and a padded
final-subtree buffer; its compile-time-size variant puts the padded
buffer on the stack.

Related to #158.

**Description**

Share a bounded Merkleization helper between the two entry points.
Accumulate progressively sized subtrees and fold a bounded root array
along the right spine. Boundary tests compare against tree roots with
scratch allocation disabled and check that input chunks stay unchanged.

Progressive type hashers still allocate their input chunk arrays.
Migrating those producers is a separate follow-up.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The changes were primarily AI-authored.

author: monem
subject: fix: reject invalid characters in fromHex on nodejs build (#9943)
body:
**Motivation**

`fromHex` has two implementations, selected by the `#bytes` condition in
`packages/utils/package.json`: `browser.js` in browsers, `nodejs.js`
everywhere else. They disagree on invalid input.

The browser build decodes character by character and throws `Invalid hex
character code`. The nodejs build calls `Buffer.from(hex, "hex")`, which
decodes up to the first character it cannot read and returns that
prefix, so an invalid string silently yields a short array:

| input | nodejs | browser |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0xzzzz` | `len=0` | throws |
| `0x0011zz2233` | `len=2` | throws |
| `0xgg` | `len=0` | throws |
| `0x00-1` | `len=1` | throws |

Valid hex is byte for byte identical on both, so only the invalid case
diverges.

`fromHex` has 126 call sites. One is
`packages/api/src/builder/routes.ts`, which parses relay supplied
`parent_hash`, `parent_root` and `pubkey`. A malformed value there
becomes a truncated array rather than an error. The wrong length means
SSZ rejects it downstream, so this is a correctness and consistency
problem rather than a validation bypass, but a caller that only inspects
the returned value gets no signal that its input was garbage.

**Description**

Compare the decoded length against the expected one and throw when they
differ. `Buffer.from` truncating at the first bad character means a
length mismatch is exactly the invalid case, so this is one comparison
and the valid path is untouched.

Tests cover five invalid inputs. Worth knowing for review:
`packages/utils/test/browser` is a symlink to `./unit`, so the single
file runs under both the unit and browser projects and pins the two
implementations to the same behaviour.

**Testing**

Reverting only `nodejs.ts` and keeping the tests fails exactly the 5 new
cases, with the other 56 in the file unaffected.

- `packages/utils` unit suite: 231 passed
- `packages/api` unit suite: 669 passed, this is the heaviest `fromHex`
consumer and includes the builder routes
- `check-types` and `biome check` clean on both changed files

subject: fix(bindings): declare sync-committee index map values as Uint32Array (#706)

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: feat(builder): add Engine payload source (#9958)
body:
## Motivation

The Builder needs a small payload-source boundary before runtime wiring
and slot orchestration are added. The existing Builder package has no
abstraction for preparing a payload through the Engine API and
retrieving the exact payload material later.

## Current behavior

The Builder cannot request or retrieve execution payloads from an
injected Engine client.

## Proposed behavior

Add a package-internal `PayloadSource` contract and an
`EnginePayloadSource` implementation that:

- preserves the relationship between each post-Gloas fork and its
fork-specific payload attributes;
- prepares a payload with forkchoice state, payload attributes, and a
caller-provided logical custody set;
- carries the CL data-column custody set used by the EL for blobpool
sampling, or `null` when the CL provides no custody services, as defined
by [Engine API
`forkchoiceUpdatedV4`](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/amsterdam.md#engine_forkchoiceupdatedv4);
the transport owns bitarray serialization;
- binds the source, fork, and payload ID in the returned handle;
- retrieves the execution payload, blobs bundle, execution requests, and
payload value without rebuilding or narrowing exact-width values;
- accepts a per-request abort signal and forwards it through the
injected Engine boundary;
- rejects source mismatches and incomplete Engine responses with
structured error codes; and
- preserves transport, timeout, and cancellation errors from the
injected Engine boundary.

The injected boundary contains only the two Engine method shapes this
service needs. This avoids adding a dependency from `@lodestar/builder`
to the full `@lodestar/beacon-node` package. Its transport owns
serialization, retries, and request execution. Later orchestration owns
request cancellation, build scheduling, deadlines, stale-result
suppression, and job concurrency.

This is an unwired direct-Engine payload-source boundary extracted from
Nico's proof of concept for independent review. Direct Engine access is
the current implementation baseline. This PR does not choose shared
versus dedicated EL use or ownership of `forkchoiceUpdated`. It does not
change Builder initialization, CLI options, concrete Engine ownership,
payload-attribute production, payload scheduling, bid construction,
storage, publication, selection, or reveal behavior.

## Evidence

- 13 focused payload-source tests, ordinary Builder type-check,
changed-file Biome and diff checks passed on 13 September 2026 after
clarifying custody semantics. The change is documentation only; the
nullable input contract is unchanged.

- Historical validation base: `f22c5ce63e`
- Reviewed head on 2026-09-07: `2d2ff420f3` (source unchanged)
- Architecture reference: [`nflaig/builder` at
`99fd8fa9ad`](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/tree/99fd8fa9ad3a867fced3a5907a68edf3a519c1cd/packages/builder)
- Tracking issue:
[krisoshea-eth/lodestar#59](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar/issues/59)
- The Heze test uses Heze payload attributes with
`inclusionListTransactions`, rather than relabeling a Gloas value.
- A compile-time regression proves that a Heze request cannot be paired
with Gloas payload attributes.
- Consensus-specs #5549 and execution-apis #774 require custody-column
input for post-Gloas `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV4`. This boundary carries
the logical custody set without deciding which future Builder component
derives it or which Engine topology consumes it.

## Downstream validation

The unwired boundary has three isolated downstream artifacts:

- upstream draft
[#9973](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9973) applies
duplicate sharing, job limits, phase deadlines, request cancellation,
and deterministic cleanup; its clean two-file comparison remains in
[fork PR #61](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar/pull/61);
- [payload store PR
#63](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar/pull/63) remains a
broader comparison proposal for
[#9970](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9970). The narrowed,
test-only
[markolazic01/lodestar#9](https://github.com/markolazic01/lodestar/pull/9)
has merged into Marko's branch and is incorporated in #9970. That does
not adopt #63's broader capacity, copying or first-write guarantees;
- the temporary [combined integration
branch](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar/tree/krisoshea/builder-direct-engine-integration)
proves one source result crosses orchestration and storage unchanged,
while the later bid, selection, and reveal services compose on the same
branch. At historical snapshot `6c1aff6c66`, it composed the source,
orchestration, store, bid-policy, bid-ledger, and proposer-preferences
components. That snapshot passed 152 Builder tests, type-check, Biome,
build/import, and diff checks with Node 24.13.0. It predates subsequent
component fixes.

These artifacts validate the contract without adding unresolved Builder
or CLI wiring to this PR.

## Testing

Previously recorded validation with Node 24.13.0 and the repository's
installed dependencies:

- 13 focused payload-source tests
- all 40 Builder unit tests
- Builder package type-check
- Builder package lint
- Builder package build and import check
- `git diff --check`

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used during codebase research, implementation,
drafting, testing, and review. The submitted code and PR text were
reviewed and revised by the author, including manual edits and technical
decisions.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: prune execution payload envelopes with `chain.pruneHistory` (#10105)
body:
`--chain.pruneHistory` deletes finalized blocks older than
`MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` and archived states before the finalized
epoch, but it never touches the execution payload envelope archive. On
gloas the full `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` of every finalized block
stays on disk forever, and since the envelope carries the transactions
and the block access list it is the larger part of what the flag is
meant to remove. This prunes the envelope archive with the same slot
cutoff as the block archive and adds a unit test covering both archives.

author: NC
subject: fix: bound inbound gossipsub RPC frames by max_message_size (#10079)
body:
Lodestar never set gossipsub `maxInboundDataLength`, so inbound RPC
frames were capped at the it-length-prefixed default of 4 MiB.
jvm-libp2p (Teku) merges everything queued for a peer into a single RPC
frame with no size cap, and a burst of 128 data column sidecars from a
block with ~20 blobs exceeds that. On overflow gossipsub removes the
peer from all topics and meshes but leaves the libp2p connection open,
so the peer is never re-added and no gossip flows in either direction.
Observed as a permanent Teku/Lodestar gossip split on a focil-devnet-0
style kurtosis network with blob spam.

Set `maxInboundDataLength` to the spec's
[`max_message_size()`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-beta.0/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#max_message_size),
the same bound Lighthouse (`gossipsub_max_transmit_size`) and Prysm
(`WithMaxMessageSize`) apply to the RPC frame. On mainnet that is
12234442 bytes, or 11.67 MiB.

## Verification

A/B run on kurtosis: one Teku, one patched Lodestar, and one unpatched
`ethpandaops/lodestar:focil-devnet-0` control, all on ethrex, with blob
spam tuned so every Teku block carried 21 blobs.

| | patched | control |
|---|---|---|
| `gossipsub_peer_read_stream_err_count_total` | 0 | 1 |
| gossip peers on `beacon_block` and column subnets | 2 | 1 |
| libp2p connected peers | 2 | 2 |
| inbound gossip absorbed | 221 MB over 8394 frames | 105 MB over 16213
frames |

The control reproduced `InvalidDataLengthError: Message length too long`
and deleted Teku's peer id from gossipsub while the libp2p connection
stayed open. The patched node stayed meshed with Teku for the whole run.

Note that with only one node patched the head-level split is masked,
because the healthy Lodestar relays Teku's blocks to the crippled one.
The error counter is the reliable signal in a mixed topology, not head
divergence.

## Out of scope

- **Recovering from the zombie-peer state.** If an inbound read error
happens for any other reason, the peer is still removed from gossipsub
with the connection left open, and nothing brings it back. Worth fixing,
but it belongs upstream rather than in an override of a private library
method, so it is deliberately not in this PR.
- **A send-side frame cap in jvm-libp2p.** Observed frames were around
5.5 MB against the new 11.67 MiB ceiling, so there is roughly two times
headroom, but Teku does not bound its merged frame at all. To be raised
with the Teku team separately.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: test: raise regression threshold for high-variance noise sendData benchmarks (#10111)
body:
## Motivation

The `network / noise / sendData` benchmarks (`send data - 1000 {N}B
messages`) keep firing false **Performance Alert** regressions on
unrelated commits. A recent example flagged the three largest payloads
with no send-path change:

| Benchmark | Current | Previous | Ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| send data - 1000 4096B messages | 132.58 ms/op | 22.325 ms/op | 5.94 |
| send data - 1000 16384B messages | 453.91 ms/op | 63.498 ms/op | 7.15
|
| send data - 1000 65536B messages | 1.9031 s/op | 275.51 ms/op | 6.91 |

## Root cause

Each run encrypts and streams 1000 messages, allocating up to ~64MB of
short-lived buffers for the 65536B case. On the shared benchmark runner
the measured time is dominated by **GC pauses and event-loop
scheduling**, not the noise send path — so the large sizes swing ~6-7x
run-to-run while the small (low-allocation) sizes stay stable. The
rolling per-commit baseline amplifies this: one noisy run becomes the
baseline and poisons the comparison for the next commit.

This is the same failure mode fixed for the data-availability benchmarks
in #10074, and the observed swing (4-8x, bounded) matches the profile
that PR gated with `threshold: 10` (as opposed to the unbounded ~250x
KZG outliers it left `noThreshold`).

## Change

Set `threshold: 10` on the noise sendData benchmark. Normal
shared-runner variance now passes, while a genuine >10x send-path
regression still fails CI. The numbers are still measured and posted to
the comparison comment as before — only the alert threshold changes.

If 10x proves insufficient (a lucky-fast baseline meeting an
unlucky-slow current can stack multiplicatively), the escalation is
`noThreshold` (report-only), matching the blob-reconstruction benches in
#10074.

---

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: prune cache entries of repeat proposals that are not imported (#10083)
body:
Every block that reaches gossip validation seeds a block input, and on
gloas a payload envelope input, before the checks run, and IGNORE keeps
those entries until finalization or size pruning. Since #9805 only the
first signature-verified repeat proposal of a proposer is imported, so
any further one holds its full block in memory for nothing, and a
proposer can send as many of those as it likes. This drops the entries
of a repeat proposal that is not imported, sync re-downloads the block
if a child or an attestation ever references it. The comment on the
import gate now says what it actually is, the two-root cap in the seen
cache is what bounds full imports over gossip to one alternate.

The dropped entry is removed with the block input cache's single-entry
`remove` rather than `prune`, which follows the parent root and evicts
every cached ancestor. A repeat proposal past the second one never had
its signature verified, so with `prune` any peer could name a cached
block as parent and evict it together with its downloaded data. The
gossip REJECT path had the same walk for blocks that fail signature or
proposer checks and is switched to `remove` as well.

The payload envelope input cache named its single-entry eviction `prune`
too, which reads as if it walked ancestors like the block input cache's.
It is renamed to `remove`, with its metric reason label, and
`pruneBelowParent` stays the ancestor variant.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: chore: log block and bid values in ETH (#10108)
body:
Block production logs print the same quantities in three units. The
info-level `Selected builder block` line formats values as ETH, the
verbose `Produced block with builder bid` line prints the bid in gwei
(`bidValue=101000000`) and the verbose `Produced block`, `Produced
beacon block body`, `Produced block with self-build bid`, `Produced
execution block`, `Produced blinded block` and `Fetched execution
payload ...` lines print wei
(`executionPayloadValue=101000000000000000`). The `Published execution
payload bid` info line and the validator monitor's `Received an
execution payload bid for monitored proposer` line print the bid value
in raw gwei as well. This formats all of them with `prettyWeiToEth` /
`prettyGweiToEth` so every value reads as `0.10100 ETH` like the
selection lines.

author: Nazar Hussain
subject: test: apply FCR attestation steps before the slot tick (#10116)
body:
## Motivation


[consensus-specs#5627](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5627)
moved each slot's past attestation steps after the tick that starts the
slot, turning the nightly spec tests red with 1412 `Invalid confirmed
root` failures.

## Description

Lodestar runs the fast confirmation rule from `forkChoice.updateTime()`,
right after the attestation queue drains, so with the new order that
queue is empty at the tick. The runner now feeds each tick's trailing
attestation steps to fork choice before the tick, where the queue holds
them until it drains.

Test-only, no production code touched.

## Testing

- nightly vectors, `spec-minimal`, all forks: 1428 passed, 8 skipped
- pinned `v1.7.0-beta.0` vectors: 1428 passed, 8 skipped. The only steps
that move there hop the genesis `tick: 0`, which is a no-op.

body:

`CLAUDE.md` pointed at the project guide with a markdown link:


Claude Code only pulls a file into context when the path is
`@`-prefixed. A markdown link is plain text, so `AGENTS.md` was never

generated code broke the comment rules in `AGENTS.md` lines 169-187.

The file also carried a quick reference that duplicated rules

partial copy of the same guide.

## Description

reference entries it did not already cover

author: Nazar Hussain
subject: fix(stf): floor the sync-aggregate proposer penalty and guard phase0 lookups (#705)
body:
**Motivation**

Two sync committee bugs that crash the process instead of returning an
error.

The proposer penalty uses `@max(0, proposer_balance -
sync_participant_reward)`. The balance is unsigned, so the subtraction
underflows before `@max` can clamp it and the node aborts.

Separately, `getValidatorIndices` and `getValidatorIndexMap` panic on a
phase0 state. Both are callable from JavaScript, so a pre-Altair state
kills the host process.

**Description**

Use saturating subtraction for the penalty. Return
`SyncCommitteeCache.Error.SyncCommitteeNotAvailable` instead of
panicking, and map it to the `NO_SYNC_COMMITTEE` error the binding
already throws.

Adds a test for each; both fail against the old code. Tests move to a
sibling `_test.zig` because tidy allows only one inline test block per
module.

Mainnet is green. Minimal is green with #704.

Refs #621, items 44 and 33 (phase0 part).

subject: fix(state-transition): use getReadonly for read-only validator access (#712)

**Motivation**

`validators.get()` then `commit()` rebuilds the branch path for every
touched validator. The withdrawals sweep did this for every sampled
validator on every block, which slowly scatters the validators tree
across the node pool and makes the epoch-transition read pass
(`before_process_epoch`) slower the longer a node runs.

TypeScript implementation.
