author: Nazar Hussain
subject: feat(bindings): implement computeBlockRewards (#709)
body:
**Motivation**

`computeBlockRewards` throws `not implemented`, so the beacon API
block-rewards endpoint fails on the native path. #648 leaves the reward
APIs out of scope.

**Description**

Add a native block-rewards computation and wire it to the binding.
Attestation and sync-aggregate rewards are taken from the
proposer-reward cache when the caller supplies one, otherwise recomputed
on a throwaway clone. Slashing rewards use the fork's whistleblower
quotient.

The binding takes signed block SSZ bytes and a blinded flag, matching
`stateTransition`, and derives the fork from the state rather than
parsing the block prefix. It returns the result synchronously; the
adapter wraps it in the Promise the host interface declares.

Covers `computeBlockRewards` only. `computeAttestationsRewards` and
`computeSyncCommitteeRewards` remain stubs and follow separately.

Refs #621, item 36.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: prune archived states before the finalized epoch with `chain.pruneHistory` (#10106)
body:
`--chain.pruneHistory` is documented to delete all archived states
before the finalized epoch, but the cutoff passed to the state archive
is the finalized epoch number while the archive is keyed by slot, so it
only ever removed states whose slot is below the finalized epoch number,
the first 1/32 of the chain. Since #7427 the states kept by the
frequency archive strategy, one per 1024 epochs, have accumulated
regardless of the flag. This uses the finalized epoch's start slot as
the cutoff, capped at the latest archived state so the anchor state
reloaded on restart is never deleted, since state archiving can trail
finalization by up to 32 epochs. Adds tests for both cases.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: feat: schedule Gloas fork on Sepolia (#10119)
body:
**Motivation**

Schedule the Glamsterdam fork (Gloas on the CL) on Sepolia so operators
can upgrade ahead of activation and Lodestar ships the fork timing in a
release.

**Description**

Sets `GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH` to `353024` in the Sepolia network config,
activating Glamsterdam at:

- Epoch: `353024`
- Slot: `11296768`
- Timestamp: `1791294816` (Tue, 06 Oct 2026, 13:53:36 UTC)

Timing as proposed in ethereum/pm#2205. `1655733600 + 11296768 * 12 =
1791294816`, epoch-aligned with Sepolia genesis.

Hoodi and mainnet timings are still TBD in that proposal, so only
Sepolia is scheduled here.

> [!NOTE]
> The corresponding `eth-clients/sepolia` config update is not merged
yet. Wait for confirmation of the upstream config before merging.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: delete block archive index entries when pruning history (#10110)
body:
`--chain.pruneHistory` removes archived blocks by slot, but the block
archive's root and parent root indexes are only cleaned up by the value
based `remove` paths, so every pruned block leaves its two index keys
behind, about 80 bytes per block, and root lookups for pruned blocks
resolve to a slot that no longer has a value. This adds a range delete
to the block archive that removes the value, slot, root and parent root
entries together. The parent root of each block is the root of the
previous archived block, read from the slot index before it is deleted,
so only the first block of the range and any block following an
unindexed one have their bytes read. The parent root entry keyed by the
last pruned block points at the first kept block and is left in place.
The pruned slot ranges are now included in the debug log.

The state archive is left alone, its root index has not been written
since states are archived with `putBinary` (#6504), so there is nothing
to clean up there. Index entries left behind by pruning runs before this
change are not swept, the fix only guarantees that pruning leaves
nothing behind from now on.

author: lodekeeper-z
subject: fix: isolate binding benchmark suites in separate processes (#708)
body:
Run each binding benchmark file sequentially in a fresh Node process
using the public `--isolate` option from `@chainsafe/benchmark` 2.1.0.
This prevents retained mainnet state and garbage collection from earlier
suites from inflating unrelated native measurements, without changing
the allocating API, deterministic inputs, benchmark IDs, or thresholds.

Use the upstream CLI directly, with no local runner adapter or
internal-module coupling. The framework owns comparison, combined CSV
persistence, the single GitHub report, worker lifecycle, and rejection
of incomplete results. Real CLI integration tests cover isolation,
cancellation, failure handling, persistence, and regression exits.

Start a new `isolated-v1` local history namespace and CI cache identity
so shared-process measurements are not reused as baselines. Dedicated
monitors should enable `--isolate` and select a fresh history profile;
archive existing histories rather than copying them into the new
baseline.

Consumes ChainSafe/benchmark#55.

body:
Builder urls must be ASCII, so a url with an internationalized hostname
like `https://platåberget.dev` is rejected without telling the operator
what to configure instead. The error from `--builder.urls`, the proposer
config file and the keymanager API now suggests the ASCII form, e.g.

data is derived from.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: derive default builder auth data from the url hostname (#10107)
body:
Follows https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/168, an omitted
`auth_data` of a builder entry is now the hostname of its url instead of
the url bytes verbatim, so a trailing slash, an explicit default port or
different casing no longer changes the signed bytes.

buildoor still compares the url verbatim, so the builder-dev kurtosis
setup fails auth until it follows the spec change.

author: Chase Wright
subject: fix: bind IPv6 by default only if the host has a global IPv6 address (#10104)
body:
## Motivation

A fresh v1.48.0 beacon node on sepolia or hoodi that runs in a Docker
container without an IPv6 route finds zero peers. Discovery never sends
a UDP packet.

`parseListenArgs` binds `::` when the user sets neither
`--listenAddress` nor `--listenAddress6`. With an IPv6 socket bound,
`@chainsafe/discv5` contacts every dual-stack ENR over IPv6 and does not
fall back to IPv4 (`getSocketAddressMultiaddrOnENR`, same rule as
sigp/discv5 `DualStack`). In a container without IPv6 connectivity every
send to those peers fails.

Until v1.47.0 the built-in sepolia and hoodi bootnode lists contained
IPv4-only EF bootnodes, which masked this. #10049 replaced them with the
NodeOps fleet, which is dual-stack. The only IPv4-only entry left (a
Teku node) does not answer. The v1.48.0 lists therefore contain no
bootnode a default-configured IPv4-only container can reach. Mainnet
still has IPv4-only bootnodes and is not affected.

Verified on a v4-only Docker host on sepolia with the fleet ENRs as
`--bootnodes`:

| image | flags | result after 90s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v1.48.0 | default | 0 peers, 0 ENRs decoded, 0 UDP packets sent |
| v1.48.0 | `--listenAddress 0.0.0.0` | syncing, hundreds of ENRs
discovered |
| v1.48.0 | `--bootnodes <IPv4-only EF ENR>` | syncing |
| v1.47.0 | default | syncing (built-in IPv4-only EF bootnodes) |

## Description

Bind IPv6 by default only if the host has a global unicast IPv6 address.
`hasGlobalIPv6Address` reads `os.networkInterfaces()` and accepts only
addresses inside the IANA global unicast block `2000::/3`, minus the
special-purpose prefixes allocated inside it that the IANA registry
marks not globally reachable (IETF protocol assignments including
Teredo, 6to4, documentation, SRv6 SIDs), through two `net.BlockList`s.
Everything else (loopback, IPv4-mapped, NAT64, unique-local, link-local,
site-local) falls outside `2000::/3`. An explicit `--listenAddress6`
still forces IPv6 on. An explicit `--listenAddress` still turns the IPv6
default off, as before.

`parseListenArgs` takes the detection result as a second parameter so
tests stay independent of the test host. Adds unit tests, updates the
`--listenAddress6` description and the networking docs.

Validated with an image built from this branch on the same IPv4-only
Docker host: default flags bind IPv4 only
(`bindAddr4=/ip4/0.0.0.0/udp/...`, no `bindAddr6`) and discover peers on
sepolia and hoodi; `--listenAddress6 ::` still binds IPv6 as before.

Lodestar warns at startup when it skips the IPv6 default for this
reason. A persisted ENR loses its `ip6`/`udp6`/`tcp6`/`quic6` fields
when no IPv6 listener is configured and no `--enr.*6` flag is given, so
peers stop dialing a dead IPv6 endpoint and the beacon handler's
`enrUpdate` gate is no longer blocked by a stale `ip6`.

The library-side fix, IPv4-first selection and fast failure on send
errors in `@chainsafe/discv5`, is ChainSafe/discv5#341.

## AI Assistance Disclosure

- [x] External Contributors: I have read the [contributor
guidelines](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/unstable/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-assistance-notice)
and disclosed my usage of AI below.

This PR was written primarily by Claude Code, including the
investigation, the code, the tests and this description. I directed the
work and validated the fix on our own infrastructure. A second model
(Codex) reviewed the diff before submission. Replies in this PR may also

author: Nico Flaig
subject: chore: add builder url to failed preferences submission errors (#10136)
body:
`submitBuilderPreferences` reports a failed entry by index and message,
so the validator client logs the reason but not which of its builders
rejected the submission. One unavailable builder then produces a warning
per submission with nothing to act on:

```
warn: Error submitting builder preferences count=6 - submitBuilderPreferences failed with status 400: Error submitting builder preferences
submitBuilderPreferences failed with status 503: Proposer duties unavailable
```

The builder is already resolved for the verbose log next to it, this
prefixes the failure message with it.

```
submitBuilderPreferences failed with status 400: Error submitting builder preferences
https://builder.example.com: submitBuilderPreferences failed with status 503: Proposer duties unavailable
```

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: keep idle event streams alive (#10133)
body:
The events API only writes to the response when an event is emitted, and
the response headers are sent with the first write. A topic that emits
rarely runs into the idle timeout of whatever sits on the other end,
commonly 60 seconds.

- behind nginx the request for such a topic fails with `504 upstream
timed out while reading response header from upstream`, on the
glamsterdam-devnet-8 nodes a `chain_reorg` subscriber loops on this
~1200 times a day per node
- buildoor reconnects an event stream after 60 seconds without any
bytes, events are not replayed, so everything emitted until it has
reconnected is lost. `proposer_preferences` emits nothing between the
burst at the start of an epoch and the preferences our validator client
submits 8 slots ahead of a proposal, and as 60 seconds is exactly 5
slots the stream is cut in the same moment such a slot aligned
submission arrives. buildoor then answers the bid request with `400 no
proposer preferences cached for slot`, this happened on ~7% of my
proposals and only with the buildoor instances backed by Lodestar, all 6
cases within its log retention have the idle reconnect in the same
second as the submission

This sends the response headers right away and writes a comment line
every 15 seconds, the interval suggested by the
[specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#authoring-notes),
comment lines are ignored by clients. Lighthouse and Grandine send a
comment every 15 seconds, Prysm every 12 and Teku every 30.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: chore: log the value and execution payment of each bid candidate (#10135)
body:
`Builder bid candidate` only prints the counted total, which is `value +
min(execution_payment, max_execution_payment)`. A builder that bids
entirely in `execution_payment` then shows up as `total=0.00000 ETH`
with nothing to say whether it bid nothing or whether the payment is not
counted because the entry has no cap, the raw values are only visible on
chain in blocks the builder won elsewhere. The selection log already
prints `bidValue` and `bidExecutionPayment` for the bid that wins.

```
Builder bid candidate slot=272327, rank=1, source=https://builder.example.com, builder=12058, value=0.00000 ETH, executionPayment=0.01350 ETH, total=0.01350 ETH, boost=3800, boosted=0.51309 ETH, receivedMs=90
```

author: Nico Flaig
subject: chore: update ethspecify mappings (#10126)
body:
`ethspecify check` only verifies that a search string exists, so stale
exceptions and mappings that point at the wrong code go unnoticed. This
audits all specrefs against the pinned pyspec and the source, exceptions
go from 330 to 101.

- map fast confirmation (#8837), it was still excepted as not
implemented
- map pre-gloas `validate_*_gossip` variants, the gloas variants already
pointed at the same validators
- map implemented gloas state transition, fork choice, validator and
builder items, and the gloas light client items
- map pre-gloas helpers that exist inline or under a different name
(`compute_fork_version`, withdrawals helpers, phase0 reward deltas, sync
committee helpers, `*_gindex_at_slot`) and the matching types and
constants
- remove 9 entries whose spec text is identical to the previous fork and
the stale `PartialDataColumnHeader#gloas` exception
- fix wrong targets: `is_data_available#gloas`,
`get_signed_proposer_preferences#gloas`,
`upgrade_lc_bootstrap_to_{capella,deneb,electra}`
- move `CustodyColumnBits#gloas` to exceptions, the previous target is a
column index lookup and custody columns are not sent to the EL
- add second sources where the logic is split, e.g. `get_head`,
`compute_ptc`, `get_attestation_participation_flag_indices#deneb`

Remaining exceptions have no counterpart: heze inclusion lists, partial
data columns, removed merge transition and eth1 voting helpers, spec
tree walks that proto-array replaces, `Seen`, `LatestMessage` and a few
trivial accessors.

`ethspecify process` is a no-op on the result and `ethspecify check`
passes.

author: Chen Kai
subject: fix: always check progressive balances (#10046)
body:
**Motivation**

Keep progressive-balance cache validation observable without making a
non-spec cache invariant able to halt state transition.

**Description**

Progressive target balances are an incremental Lodestar cache used by
fork choice for unrealized justification. The epoch transition already
recomputes the authoritative current and previous target balances.

- Keep the Altair+ consistency check.
- On mismatch, increment
`lodestar_stfn_progressive_balances_mismatches_total` and overwrite the
progressive cache with the freshly recomputed values.
- Do not throw from state transition and do not add logging in the
state-transition library.
- Remove the obsolete opt-in CLI and state-transition option plumbing.

This keeps cache drift visible and self-healing while avoiding a
liveness failure from an auxiliary cache invariant.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

> This PR was written primarily by Codex.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: test: fail gossip spec tests on unexpected errors (#10140)
body:
**Motivation**

The gossip spec runner maps raw `TypeError` and `RangeError` to
`REJECT`, while production returns `IGNORE`. This can make tests
expecting rejection pass for the wrong reason.

**Description**

author: Chen Kai
subject: refactor: write error values as error.Name (#718)
body:
**Motivation**

Error names are global in Zig, so `Error.InvalidNode` and
`error.InvalidNode` resolve to the same value, and the repo used both
spellings. The qualified form carries a cost: it has to be revisited
whenever a value moves between sets, and it reads as though the set,
rather than the function's return type, decides which errors can arrive.
`zig fmt` has no opinion here, so nothing kept the rejected form out.

```
$ grep -rnE '[A-Za-z_]*Error\.[A-Z]' --include='*.zig' . | wc -l
70
```

**Description**

Rewrites every `Set.Name` error value as `error.Name` and adds a tidy
rule so the qualified form cannot come back.

- Rewrite all three shapes: `BlstError.BadEncoding`, the bare
`Error.InvalidNode`, and the qualified `Node.Error.InvalidNode`.
Declared error sets are untouched and still appear in signatures.
- Drop the now-unused `BlstError` aliases in
`src/bls/signature_test.zig` and the four `test/fuzz/src/fuzz_bls_*.zig`
harnesses.
- Add `tidyErrorValues` to `test/tidy.zig`. It matches an identifier
ending in `Error` (including `Error` itself) followed by a TitleCase
member, so a camelCase call on a namespace that ends in `Error` is not
flagged. It reads the token stream, so comments and string literals
cannot trip it, and it has a rule test asserting the exact diagnostics.
- Document the rule in AGENTS.md `Code style`.

Diagnostic shape:

```
src/persistent_merkle_tree/Node.zig:142: error: `Error.RefCountOverflow` names an error through its set, write `error.RefCountOverflow`
```

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Primarily AI-authored: the mechanical rewrite, the tidy rule, and the
docs change.

subject: fix(stf): self-heal progressive balance drift (#726)
body:
**Motivation**

Port the state-transition behavior from Lodestar PRs #10046 and #10143.
Progressive target balance caches are maintained incrementally and can
drift from the authoritative participation data used during epoch
transition. The Lodestar behavior records the drift and repairs the
cache so fork-choice consumers do not retain stale values.

**Description**

Add non-fatal progressive balance validation and metric attribution to
the Zig state transition.

- `EpochTransitionCache.init`
- Recomputes current and previous unslashed target balances for Altair
and later forks.
- Increments `lodestar_stfn_progressive_balances_mismatches_total` with
`target="current"` or `target="previous"` for each mismatch.
  - Replaces mismatched cache values with the recomputed values.
- State-transition metrics
  - Adds the labeled mismatch counter and its cleanup/init plumbing.
- Regression coverage
- Forces a current-balance mismatch at an epoch boundary and verifies
the labeled metric.

assistance.

author: bing
subject: feat(stf): zero-alloc `processSyncAggregate` (#269)
body:
Introduces a zero-alloc `processSyncAggregate`.

Done by:

separating `intersectValues` in `BitVector` into:

- `intersectValuesAlloc`: the original `intersectValues`.
- `intersectValues`: a new function that takes a `out: [length]T` as a
param.

The maximum size of the `BitVector` is 512, which is negligible on the
stack. We introduce an alloc-free version as a minor optimization.

Then since we know the pubkeys are going to be 512 * 96 = 48KiB worth of
allocations,
we can skip heap allocations and simply use an array for
`participant_buf`.

author: bing
subject: refactor(epoch-cache): make effectiveBalanceIncrementsSet append instead (#721)
body:
**Motivation**

Before this, adding `preset.MAX_PENDING_DEPOSITS_PER_EPOCH` new
validators could copy up to
`preset.MAX_PENDING_DEPOSITS_PER_EPOCH` of
`effective_balance_increments`. This commit adds a fast path that makes
use of the fact that in `beforeEpochTransition()` we clone and init a
new `effective_balance_increments` before processing deposits, which
allow us to extend the private array in place instead of copying.

Beyond that we also rename `effectiveBalanceIncrementsSet` into
`effectiveBalanceIncrementsAppend`
because it was already append-only anyway, and this makes the contract 
much clearer (we can assert `index == old.items.len`), and makes the
conditionals in the
code cleaner too (see `grow` block)

Napkin math:

Each entry is a u16, so the array uses approximately: validator count *
2 bytes.
For mainnet, that's roughly 1,000,000 validators: about 1.907 MiB. 16
full copies move about 1.907 MiB * 16 ~= 30.52MiB

**Description**

Add a fast path that allow us to grow `effective_balance_increments`
in-place
after `beforeEpochTransition()`, when the ref count is 1.

Closes #720

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Local benchmarks + investigation done with fable

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: derive ephemery config from published iteration, not process start time (#10161)
body:
## Motivation

Reported in #10160: with `--network ephemery`, a validator client
refuses to start against its own beacon node when started any meaningful
time after it:

```
Error: Local and remote configs are different
MIN_GENESIS_TIME different value: 1790188665039 != 1790188516030
```

`MIN_GENESIS_TIME` ends up being the **process start time in
milliseconds** (so it differs for every process), and
`/eth/v1/config/spec` reports a **fractional** `DEPOSIT_CHAIN_ID`.

## Root cause

The ephemery config derived its dynamic values from:

```ts
const RESET_INTERVAL_MS = 604800000;
const iteration = Math.floor(Date.now() - baseChainConfig.MIN_GENESIS_TIME) / RESET_INTERVAL_MS;
```

Two compounding bugs:

1. **Misplaced `Math.floor`** — it wraps only the subtraction (already
an integer), then divides, so `iteration` is fractional. That flows
straight into `DEPOSIT_CHAIN_ID` / `DEPOSIT_NETWORK_ID` → fractional
deposit chain id.
2. **ms vs seconds** — `Date.now()` is milliseconds, `MIN_GENESIS_TIME`
is seconds. With the fractional `iteration`, `RESET_INTERVAL_MS *
iteration` reduces to `Date.now() - MIN_GENESIS_TIME`, so
`MIN_GENESIS_TIME = RESET_INTERVAL_MS * iteration +
baseChainConfig.MIN_GENESIS_TIME` collapses to exactly `Date.now()` (ms)
— the process start time.

On top of that the bundled config was stale (see references below):
ephemery's reset interval changed from 7 → **28 days** and
`GENESIS_DELAY` from 300 → **600**, but the config still used `604800000
ms` / `GENESIS_DELAY: 300`.

## Why these values changed (upstream references)

All values are anchored to ephemery-genesis
[`values.env`](https://github.com/ephemery-testnet/ephemery-genesis/blob/a4b5a2ee5c1c40e378edc92f2ccd9938cf9207d0/values.env)
(pinned, iteration 164):

| value | old | new | upstream change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| reset interval | 7d (`604800`) | 28d (`2419200`) |
[`131d330`](https://github.com/ephemery-testnet/ephemery-genesis/commit/131d330aab546ed2564b81be14981776cf8b1e2c)
— "increase reset interval to 28days" (2024-06-28) |
| `GENESIS_DELAY` | `300` | `600` |
[`f761969`](https://github.com/ephemery-testnet/ephemery-genesis/commit/f761969dd0c827af58f6b19c4fce0f5298fe8f65)
— "update genesis generator, new release layout" (2024-06-28) |
| `MIN_GENESIS_TIME` / `CHAIN_ID` | iteration-0 base | iteration 164
(`1790276400` / `39438164`) | current `values.env` (advances by one each
reset) |

Ephemery periodically resets (EIP-6916); `values.env` publishes each new
iteration. Lodestar bundles a base and rolls it forward, so the base
only needs to stay within the current reset cadence rather than be
bumped every iteration.

## Description

- Rebase the bundled base to the current published iteration
(`values.env` iteration 164) and fix `GENESIS_DELAY` `300 → 600`.
- Recompute the iteration in **whole seconds** with a correctly-placed
`Math.floor` and the 28-day interval.
- `values.env` stages the *next* iteration ahead of its activation, so
resolve the iteration **active at `nowMs`** (the most recent reset
at/before now) rather than clamping forward-only — a node started before
the staged iteration activates still derives the live iteration.
- Extract `getEphemeryChainConfig(nowMs)` so the time-dependent
derivation is deterministic and unit-tested
(`packages/config/test/unit/networks.test.ts`).

Every process within an iteration now computes identical whole-second
values, which is what the VC↔BN params check requires.

## Verification

Reproduced through the actual failing path (`assertEqualParams`,
`validator.ts:372 → params.ts:95` in the stack trace) with the
reporter's exact process start times:

```
OLD -> Local and remote configs are different | MIN_GENESIS_TIME different value: 1790188665039 != 1790188516030
FIX -> BN.MIN_GENESIS_TIME=1787857200 VC.MIN_GENESIS_TIME=1787857200 DEPOSIT_CHAIN_ID=39438163 (assertEqualParams OK)
```

The fix derives the **live** iteration 163 values
(`MIN_GENESIS_TIME=1787857200`, `genesis_time=1787857800`,
`DEPOSIT_CHAIN_ID=39438163`) — matching the reporter's synced beacon
node — so a BN and a VC started ~149s apart agree and the VC connects.
Local: config unit tests green, `tsc` + biome clean.

Closes #10160

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: validate slot and epoch values on slashing protection import (#10166)
body:
Slot and epoch values of an EIP-3076 interchange file were parsed with
`parseInt` without any range check. Values of `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`
or more are either stored truncated (`18446744073709551615` becomes slot
or epoch 0) or are invisible to the range scans of the slashing
protection DB, so the imported lower bound is lost and the export writes
different values back out. Values close to 2^64 also make the min-span
update on import loop forever since `epoch - 1 === epoch`. Malformed
strings like `12abc` or `1.5` were silently accepted as well.

- parse slot and epoch values strictly as decimal uints below
`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, otherwise reject the import with
`ERR_INTERCHANGE_INVALID_VALUE` before anything is written to the DB
- add unit tests for accepted and rejected values

Not exploitable in practice, an import requires the keymanager API token
or an operator importing an untrusted file, and a file with valid low
values already lowers the lower bound the same way (a later import may
lower it for a complete database, see `should_succeed_complete` in the
v5.3.0 interchange tests). Real slots and epochs are bounded by the
clock, the largest value in the EIP-3076 test vectors is 1201.

Validation

- the new unit tests fail without this change (9 of 11) and pass with it
- ran the affected scenarios through
`SlashingProtection.importInterchange`, which the keymanager API and
`slashing-protection import` both use, before and after this change

| scenario | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| block floor at slot 5000, then import slot `2^64 - 1` | import
succeeds, slot 4000 is signed, export shows slot `"0"` | import
rejected, slot 4000 still refused, export unchanged |
| empty DB, import slot `2^53 - 1` | import succeeds, the record is
invisible to range scans | import rejected, nothing written |
| attestation floor at epoch 500, then import epoch `2^64 - 1` | import
succeeds, attestation (10, 20) is signed | import rejected, (10, 20)
still refused |
| empty DB, import attestation `(2^64 - 1, 2^64 - 1)` | import never
completes | import rejected immediately |

- EIP-3076 interchange tests pass

Target epochs below `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` that are far in the future
can still make the import run practically forever, this is addressed
separately in #10170.

author: Chen Kai
subject: perf: overlap Fulu shuffling with epoch processing (#727)
body:
**Motivation**

Fulu and later epoch transitions prepared the active-validator indices
before `processEpoch`, but built the next shuffling in
`afterProcessEpoch`, after the other epoch steps. Building from an owned
snapshot lets that work overlap the independent epoch processing.

**Description**

Start the next shuffling at the beginning of `processEpoch` with
`std.Io.async`. `processProposerLookahead` awaits the result, and
`EpochCache.afterProcessEpoch` reuses its reference-counted shuffling.

- `ShufflingJob` owns an active-index copy and precomputed attester
seed; its worker does not read the mutable beacon state. Worker errors
propagate, and cache teardown cancels or releases unfinished work.
- `stfn_epoch_shuffling_job_seconds` records successful job build time
on the calling thread after await or cancel. It excludes scheduling, the
input copy, and proposer waiting time.
- `bench_process_epoch` starts shuffling once in each whole or segmented
run. The segmented breakdown records `start_shuffling`; the standalone
synchronous lookahead benchmark releases its shuffling after each timed
iteration and is labeled `proposer_lookahead(sync)`. Its Fulu-and-later
guard matches `processEpoch`.
- Pre-Fulu shuffling keeps its existing synchronous path. `std.Io.async`
may also execute inline when concurrency is unavailable.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The implementation was primarily AI-authored with user-directed design
decisions and review.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: reject slashing protection import of attestations from the future (#10170)
body:
Importing an attestation updates the min-max surround spans, and the
max-span update does one database read for each epoch between the source
and target epoch until it finds an existing span that is large enough.
On the first import for a validator nothing stops it early, so an
interchange file with an attestation like `{"source_epoch": "0",
"target_epoch": "9007199254740990"}` makes the import run practically
forever, collecting span entries in memory until the process runs out of
it. #10166 rejects values close to 2^64 where `epoch - 1 === epoch` made
the loop endless, but values below `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are still
valid.

The keymanager API imports slashing protection data inside the running
validator client, which never responds to the request and keeps growing
memory. There the current epoch is known, and no attestation can have
been signed for a target epoch that has not happened yet.

- `importInterchange` takes an optional `currentEpoch` and rejects the
whole import with `ERR_INTERCHANGE_FUTURE_TARGET_EPOCH` before writing
anything if an attestation has a target epoch more than one epoch after
it, one epoch is allowed for clock disparity with the client the data
was exported from, and before genesis (where the clock's current epoch
is negative) the bound is taken from the genesis epoch so a genesis
attestation can still be imported
- the validator client passes its current epoch for keymanager API
imports

With the current epoch the max-span update is bounded by the number of
epochs since genesis. The `slashing-protection import` command is not
changed, it is run by the operator who can interrupt it, and it does not
always know the genesis time (e.g. custom networks without access to a
beacon node).

Validation

- new unit tests in
`test/unit/slashingProtection/interchange/futureTargetEpoch.test.ts`,
without this change importing target `2^53 - 2` times out after 20s and
target `currentEpoch + 2` is accepted, with it both are rejected and
nothing is written, target `currentEpoch + 1` is still accepted, before
genesis targets 0 and 1 are accepted and 2 is rejected
- confirmed with a validator client process through the keymanager API
(the `startValidatorWithKeyManager` e2e setup), before this change the
import of `(0, 9007199254740990)` did not respond within 20s, with it
the request fails in 14ms with `ERR_INTERCHANGE_FUTURE_TARGET_EPOCH`, a
regular import of `(0, 1)` returns 200 in both cases
- EIP-3076 interchange tests pass (94 tests, the runner does not pass a
current epoch)

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: do not replace recorded slashing protection data on interchange import (#10168)
body:
Importing slashing protection interchange data wrote each block and
attestation with `batchPut`, which replaces whatever was stored for the
same slot or target epoch. A record of a message that was actually
signed could therefore be replaced by an imported record with a
different signing root.

For example, after signing a block with root `A` at slot 100, importing
`{"slot": "100", "signing_root": "<B>"}` stores root `B` for slot 100. A
later request to sign block `B` at slot 100 is then treated as a repeat
of the same block (`SAME_DATA`) and gets signed, which is a double
proposal together with `A`. The same applies to attestations with the
same target epoch (double vote), including an imported attestation with
a different source epoch for a target that is not the latest one (the
existing import check only covers the latest target). This requires
importing interchange data, via the keymanager API or the
`slashing-protection import` command, and a second signing request for
the same slot or target epoch, which the validator client does not make
on its own.

Imported records are now merged with what is already stored, both in the
database and earlier in the same file

- same source epoch and signing root: stored as before, so importing an
export of the same history is a no-op and re-signing the same message
still works
- anything else: stored with a zero signing root, which refuses any
block at that slot or attestation with that target epoch. This is the
same handling as for an imported record without `signing_root`, EIP-3076
requires treating any new message at that slot as slashable in that case
- for attestations the higher source epoch is kept, the import already
requires the latest attestation to have the highest source epoch as
`checkAttestation` relies on it

This adds one database read per imported block and attestation, next to
the reads the min-max surround update already does for each imported
attestation.

Validation

- new unit tests in `test/unit/slashingProtection/import.test.ts`, 4 of
the 7 fail on `unstable` with the conflicting message being signed, the
other 3 cover cases that already worked (import without signing root,
re-signing the same message) and guard the merge logic
- EIP-3076 interchange tests pass with the current runner (v5.1.0, 94
tests) and with the runner from #10167 (v5.3.0, 38 tests)

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: use exact integer division for Electra slashing penalty (#10163)
body:
The Electra correlation penalty per increment was computed with float
division followed by `Math.floor`. Once the numerator exceeds
`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, which takes roughly 3M ETH slashed within the
slashings window, an exact quotient just below an integer can be rounded
up by the division itself, leaving nothing for `Math.floor` to truncate.
The penalty is then 1 Gwei per effective balance increment higher than
the spec and the post-state root diverges from other clients.

- compute the penalty per increment with bigint, same as
`getBuilderPaymentQuorumThreshold`
- add a unit test with a vector that previously rounded up (268437223
instead of 268437222 Gwei per increment)

Not practically exploitable since it needs ~9% of total stake slashed
within 36 days and the division to land in the rounding window (~1 in
37M), but spec tests cannot cover it. Verified with the reporter's
reproduction, on the same SSZ pre-state the post-state root now matches
Prysm. The pre-Electra branch and other float divisions in the state
transition keep their numerators below 2^53 or divide by a power of two.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: harden validator block signing (#10142)
body:
Proposal work from adjacent duty slots can overlap when an earlier block
production request remains pending, per-slot duty deduplication does not
serialize this work. A beacon node could answer the request for slot
`S+1` with a block for slot `S`, and two checks for the same key running
at the same time could both pass the double proposal check before either
block is recorded, since `checkAndInsertBlockProposal` reads and writes
the database in separate steps.

- require produced blocks to match the requested duty slot with a typed
`SLOT_MISMATCH` error, `signBlock` now takes the `dutySlot` (this
replaces the untyped check added in #10169)
- serialize block slashing protection checks and writes per validator,
including interchange block imports so an import cannot race a check for
the same slot
- add regression coverage, align the doppelganger block fixtures with
duty slots and correct a public-key test fixture

Without the serialization the overlap tests fail: two conflicting
proposals for the same slot are both accepted, a lower slot is accepted
after a higher one, and an interchange import racing a check for the
same slot loses the imported block.

author: twoeths
subject: fix: do not remove pending block on failed download (#10137)
body:
**Motivation**

- when we failed to download a block, we remove it immediately and
recreate it again on the next unknown root, see #10018
- that causes UnknownBlockInput sync not to be able to accumulate
preferred peer ids to download from

**Description**

handle similar to pending payloads:
- retain the failed pending block, set it status back to pending
- prune on finalized

so instead of removing block immediately, we keep it up to 2 epochs,
similar to the payload path

this is also part of #10091: we don't want to call
`removeAndDownScoreAllDescendants()` on a failed block download

Closes #10018

author: Nico Flaig
subject: test: apply EIP-3076 interchange test steps in order and update to v5.3.0 (#10167)
body:
The EIP-3076 interchange test runner did not follow the [test
format](https://github.com/eth-clients/slashing-protection-interchange-tests#how-to-run),
which starts each test with an empty database and then, step by step,
imports the interchange and attempts the block and attestation signings,
remembering the ones that succeed, before moving to the next step.

Instead, every step with checks registered a `beforeEach` hook in the
same `describe`, so before every single signing check all hooks ran,
each clearing the database and importing its own step. This means

- every check ran against a database holding only the interchange of the
last step that has checks, steps without checks were never imported
- messages signed by one check were cleared before the next one
- steps with `contains_slashable_data` never ran their checks, and the
expected import failure for them was never exercised
- a `should_succeed: false` import was expected to resolve, which also
never ran since that test has no checks

Changes

- run each test case as a single test that applies all steps in order on
the same database
- a step with slashable data that Lodestar refuses to import as
slashable (`InvalidAttestationError` from the import check, or
`SurroundAttestationError` if the surround is only found while inserting
spans) skips its checks, the format allows clients to refuse such data
and the checks assume it was imported, any other import failure fails
the test. Steps with an expected import failure still run their checks
- update the vectors from v5.1.0 to v5.3.0, which adds 5
multi-interchange tests and `should_succeed_complete` next to
`should_succeed`. Releases after v5.2.0 no longer attach a tarball, so
the source archive of the tag is downloaded instead (38 test files,
identical to `tests/generated` at the tag)
- check signings against `should_succeed` where it is equal to
`should_succeed_complete`, otherwise accept either outcome.
`should_succeed` is the expected outcome for a minimal database and
`should_succeed_complete` for a complete one, Lodestar stores all signed
messages but also enforces the lower bounds of imported data so it sits
in between (e.g. after importing block 40 and then block 50, a complete
database may sign block 45, a minimal one may not)

All 38 vectors pass on current code, so this does not depend on any
other change. Five steps skip their checks because the import is refused
with `ERR_INVALID_ATTESTATION_NEW_SURROUNDS_PREV`
(`duplicate_pubkey_slashable_attestation`,
`single_validator_slashable_attestations_surrounds_existing`,
`single_validator_slashable_attestations_surrounded_by_existing`, and
step 1 of
`multiple_interchanges_single_validator_first_surrounds_second` and
`multiple_interchanges_single_validator_second_surrounds_first`).

To confirm the runner now tests what it is supposed to, I added a
mutation that clears the database on every import (simulating an import
that drops previously imported data). The new runner fails 5
multi-interchange tests, the previous runner with v5.1.0 still passes
all 94 tests. None of the vectors re-sign a conflicting message after a
successful signing within a step, so remembering signed messages is
required by the format but not covered by the current vectors.

The CI cache key for these vectors is the hash of `params.ts`, so the
version bump invalidates it.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: check attestation target epoch and block slot before signing (#10169)
body:
The validator client only checked that attestation data and blocks
received from the beacon node are not for a future epoch or slot. It did
not check that they belong to the duty being performed, so a malicious
or faulty beacon node could get it to sign

- attestation data for the duty slot with an older target epoch (only
`duty.slot === data.slot` and `target.epoch <= currentEpoch` were
checked)
- a block for an older slot during a proposal (only `block.slot <=
currentSlot` was checked)

Neither is valid for the duty, and slashing protection is the only thing
left that prevents such a message from being slashable. That is fine as
long as the slashing protection database has the full history, but not
for history it does not know about, e.g. after an interchange import
that did not include all signed messages, which the EIP-3076 lower
bounds only partially cover.

- reject attestation data where `target.epoch` is not the epoch of
`data.slot`, this also covers aggregates since they go through the same
`validateAttestationDuty`
- only sign a block if its slot equals the proposal slot

Honest data always passes both checks. `process_attestation` requires
`data.target.epoch == compute_epoch_at_slot(data.slot)` (also asserted
in `processAttestationPhase0`), and our beacon node derives the target
epoch from the requested slot. The block service passes the slot it
requested the block for as `currentSlot`, and the block returned for
that request must have that slot.

Validation

- added unit tests to `validatorStore.test.ts` that fail on `unstable`
(both messages get signed) and pass with this change, the existing
validator store and services unit tests pass
- the web3signer e2e test signed attestation data with target epoch 0 at
slot 2375711 (epoch 74240) and aggregates with target epoch 0 at the
start slot of each fork, which is now refused. The fixtures use the
target epoch of the slot, verified locally against web3signer, 7 tests
fail with the old fixtures and all pass with the new ones
- the doppelganger e2e test signs a slot 0 block at the current slot,
updated to sign a block at the current slot. The suite is skipped and
fails on `unstable` for unrelated reasons (timeouts, pre-electra block
production), un-skipped locally the new check no longer shows up in its
failures with the updated fixtures

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: update `earliestAvailableSlot` when pruning history (#10177)
body:
`earliestAvailableSlot` is set once at startup to the anchor state slot
and never updated, so a node with `--chain.pruneHistory` keeps
advertising blocks in `Status` that it has already pruned once it has
been running longer than `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS`. Peers then
request those ranges and get an empty response instead of
`ResourceUnavailable`, since the by range handlers only reject requests
below `earliestAvailableSlot`.

`pruneHistory` now returns the block cutoff slot and the archive store
raises `earliestAvailableSlot` to it after each run. The setter already
triggers a status update.

author: Marko Lazic
subject: feat: de-duplicate execution payload from archived Gloas envelopes (#10089)
body:
**Motivation**

Post-Gloas, every finalized `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` in the
archive carries the full execution payload the EL already stores:
transactions (~194 KB/block at current mainnet sizes), withdrawals and
the block access list (~70 KiB), well over 500 GB/year of redundant CL
disk. Closes #5671 for the Gloas scope; pre-Gloas blocks are unchanged.

Also relates to #9282: this covers the finalized archive; hot-db dedup
and the interop test are follow-ups.

**Description**

- New `SignedExecutionPayloadHeaderEnvelope` in `@lodestar/types`
(gloas): the payload replaced by its header, `transactions`,
`withdrawals` and `blockAccessList` swapped for their roots at the same
field positions, so it hashes identically to the full envelope and the
builder signature verifies against the stored entry. ~1 KB per envelope,
Lodestar-internal, never on the wire.
- `--chain.dedupePayloads` (default `true`): hot→cold migration archives
execution-valid envelopes as header envelopes; still-optimistic ones,
and everything with the flag off, are archived in full as bytes. Both
share one bucket: full envelopes are stored as their hot bytes
untouched, header envelopes behind a `0x00` prefix byte (a full envelope
always starts with `0x64`, its `message` offset), so the flag can be
toggled without resync and entries archived before this change stay
readable.
- Reads rebuild header entries from `engine_getPayloadBodiesByHashV2`
(new, Amsterdam), 32 hashes per call, each body verified against its
stored root with the mismatching field reported, byte-identical to what
was archived. `getParentExecutionRequests` reads the header entry
directly, no EL call.
- By-range: the spec inherits BeaconBlocksByRange v2 semantics
(consecutive, MAY be short), so the stream ends at the first entry the
EL cannot serve (unknown hash, pruned BAL (null or zero-length), body
root mismatch, or an EL failure) and answers `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` if
nothing was served. By-root allows omission, so a mismatched envelope is
left out and the rest served. REST keeps 500 on mismatch. EL down →
`RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` / 503. Misses are logged at debug; they are
peer-triggered.
- No age floor: every header entry is attempted, the EL's BAL retention
is the real limit (spec: MUST serve `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS`, MAY
serve more). Deliberately the opposite of Teku's trim.
- Metrics:
`beacon_payload_envelope_reconstruction_envelopes_total{result=ok|unavailable|mismatch}`,
`…_mismatch_total{field}` and `…_engine_errors_total` (failed
`engine_getPayloadBodiesByHashV2` round-trips), incremented in the
single reconstruction path shared by by-range, by-root and REST. The
`unavailable`/`ok` ratio measures how far past the EL's BAL retention
peers are requesting.

**Known limitations**

- With an EL that prunes BALs at the EIP-7928 floor (~16 days), older
range requests get `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`. Spec-correct on our side;
closing the gap between EL retention and the CL's
`MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` serving requirement is
ethereum/EIPs#12347.
- Envelopes archived in full while the EL was still syncing are never
converted later.
- The header envelope types are Gloas-specific; needs fork-aware types
once EIP-8205's per-fork envelope lands. `headerEnvelope.test.ts` pins
the field layout per fork so this fails loudly.

**Sizing**

| full envelope | header envelope | reduction | saved / yr |
| ------------- | --------------- | --------- | ---------- |
| ~267 KB       | ~1 KB           | >99%      | ~690 GB    |

**Testing**

`headerEnvelope.test.ts`, `envelopeMigration.test.ts`,
`execution.test.ts` and `executionPayloadEnvelopes.test.ts` (real
LevelDB, mocked EL): root equality with the full envelope, field layout
per fork, round-trip, per-field mismatch, migration
header/full/optimistic, byte-identity, batching,
end-at-first-unservable, transient EL error, getter vs p2p mismatch
behaviour, and the peer-facing handler mapping (short response after a
served envelope, `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` on an unservable first entry or
EL outage, by-root omitting a mismatched envelope while serving the
rest).

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: initialize earliestAvailableSlot from retained history on startup (#10185)
body:
## Motivation

On an **in-place restart** (existing DB, not a fresh checkpoint sync),
`earliestAvailableSlot` was re-initialized to the anchor state slot and
only ever raised afterwards (`Math.max` on prune). A node that still
retains finalized history below the anchor then rejects
`beacon_blocks_by_range`, `execution_payload_envelopes_by_range`, and
`data_column_sidecars_by_range` requests for data it actually holds —
the incoming by_range error rate jumps to ~100%.

Observed live on v1.49.0 RC soak nodes: after a restart,
`earliestAvailableSlot` jumped `246560 → 313312` (the finalized anchor)
while the node still retained history back to ~246560, and every
by_range request for that range was rejected with
`RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`. `beacon_blocks_by_range` (never deduped) behaved
identically to the envelope path, confirming it is not dedup-related.

Closes #10181. Part of #7997 (the startup/init "correct location" for
`earliestAvailableSlot`).

## Description

In `ArchiveStore.init()`, after pruning, initialize
`earliestAvailableSlot` from the earliest block still present in the
archive (`db.blockArchive.firstKey()`) instead of leaving it at the
anchor slot set in the constructor. Falls back to the anchor when the
archive is empty (fresh checkpoint sync with nothing below the anchor).
It now runs regardless of `pruneHistory`, so archival nodes also
advertise from their earliest retained block rather than the anchor.

The block-archive floor is the correct single value for all three
by_range handlers:
- `beacon_blocks_by_range` and `execution_payload_envelopes_by_range`
share the block retention floor (envelopes are pruned together with
blocks in `pruneHistory`).
- `data_column_sidecars_by_range` handles slots above the floor with
missing columns gracefully (spec-legal short response, no error — see
`handleColumnSidecarUnavailability`), so the block floor is a safe lower
bound.

Tightening `earliestAvailableSlot` to also track the (usually higher)
data-column retention floor, and lowering it during backfill, is the
DA-window/expiry side of #7997 and is left as follow-up.

## Testing

Added unit tests in `archiveStore.test.ts`:
- `init` lowers `earliestAvailableSlot` from the anchor to the earliest
retained block.
- `init` keeps the anchor when the archive is empty.

author: Cayman
subject: refactor: bound fixed vector hashing (#681)
body:
**Motivation**

Fixed-element vectors reserve hashing scratch proportional to their
declared size on the stack. Large vectors therefore consume large stack
frames even though Merkleization can stream chunks.

Related to #158.

**Description**

Keep direct hashing for at most 64 chunks and use `MerkleAccumulator`
above that bound. Stream packed values and composite roots, and reject
incorrect serialized lengths before reading bytes.

A local ReleaseSafe uint8-vector microbenchmark (20,000 calls per size)
preserved the small-vector timings. Larger samples show the tradeoff:
2,080 bytes took 3.15 us with the previous full-buffer algorithm versus
3.80 us with accumulation; 32,768 bytes took 44.10 us versus 50.63 us.
Workspace no longer grows with vector length. These samples are not a
whole-client throughput prediction.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The changes were primarily AI-authored.

author: Chen Kai
subject: fix: floor attestation reward and penalty values (#10182)
body:
**Motivation**

`computeAttestationsRewards` rounds ideal rewards and penalties to the
nearest Gwei, while the state transition
(`getRewardsAndPenaltiesAltair`) and the consensus spec use integer
division. Any value with a fractional part of 0.5 or more is reported 1
Gwei higher than what is actually applied to balances, so the
per-validator breakdown does not sum to the real balance change.

**Description**

Floor ideal rewards and penalties with the same expression as
`getRewardsAndPenaltiesAltair`.

- `computeIdealAttestationsRewardsAndPenaltiesAltair`: replace both
`Math.round` calls with `Math.floor` and divide by
`activeBalanceByIncrement * WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR` in one step
- `attestationsRewards.test.ts`: check ideal rewards against a `bigint`
reference and check each validator's `head + target + source +
inactivity` against `rewards[i] - penalties[i]` from the state
transition

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: use preallocated buffers in `getBlobsV2` (#10203)
body:
`getBlobs` declares a `buffers` parameter but the implementation never
forwarded it to `getBlobsV2`, so the buffers preallocated by
`GetBlobsTracker` since #8282 were ignored and every `engine_getBlobsV2`
response was decoded into fresh allocations. Forwarding them surfaces a
second issue: the tracker preallocates one buffer per max blobs of the
epoch (#8938) while `getBlobsV2` required exactly one buffer per
requested versioned hash, so any block with fewer blobs than the max
would have thrown `Invalid buffers length` before the request was sent.

- forward `buffers` from `getBlobs` to `getBlobsV2`
- only require at least as many buffers as versioned hashes, the first
entries are used
- add a unit test with more preallocated buffers than requested hashes

author: Chen Kai
subject: refactor(stf): make allocator ownership explicit (#722)
body:
**Motivation**

[#621](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/issues/621) item 45
identified allocator mismatches in state-transition caches. The shared
N-API allocator masks them, but distinct Zig callers can free memory
through the wrong allocator.

**Description**

Make allocator ownership explicit at state-transition cache boundaries.

- `EpochCache` uses its own allocator for cache-owned sync-committee and
effective-balance storage.
- Caller-owned attesting-index results receive the output allocator.
- Borrowed process-global compounding-validator storage retains its
owner allocator and exposes `append(value)` without an allocator
argument.
- `EpochTransitionCache` retains the allocator for its owned lists and
`balances`.
- Regression tests cover distinct allocators, cache growth, and OOM
cleanup.


**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation was primarily AI-authored.

author: Chen Kai
subject: perf: shuffle compact validator positions (#734)
body:
**Motivation**

Epoch shuffling repeatedly swaps `u64` validator indices. Shuffling
`u32` positions reduces the data moved by the swap kernel while
preserving full-width validator indices.

**Benchmark**
The existing `bench_process_epoch` benchmark on Apple M5,
ReleaseSafe/mainnet, measured a roughly 15–17% reduction in segmented
epoch time. The input is the mainnet Fulu state at slot 13,336,576 with
2,178,249 validators and 985,817 active indices. Each case runs 50
iterations; values below are per-run means in milliseconds.

| Case | Existing, runs 1 / 2 | Compact positions, runs 1 / 2 / 3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `epoch_total` | 217.467 / 217.005 | 183.483 / 181.523 / 184.346 |
| `proposer_lookahead`, including async wait | 106.162 / 105.282 |
71.625 / 71.072 / 70.881 |
| Standalone synchronous `proposer_lookahead` | 131.044 / 130.724 |
96.859 / 99.810 / 96.350 |
| `state_root` | 33.047 / 33.096 | 33.009 / 32.888 / 32.915 |

Most of the reduction comes from the lookahead stage, which includes
waiting for shuffling and is not a pure shuffle-kernel measurement.
`epoch_total` includes preparation, epoch steps and final hashing, but
excludes `afterProcessEpoch`, `finalProcessEpoch` and deferred
transition-cache cleanup. These are repeated-snapshot results, not
complete-transition or block-replay timings.

**Description**

`EpochShuffling.init` shuffles identity `u32` positions, then gathers
the original `u64` indices into the existing output. The existing
shuffle length limit is checked before constructing positions; validator
index values are never narrowed. Public fields, committees and ownership
remain unchanged.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation, tests, benchmarking and this description were primarily
authored with OpenAI Codex. Submitted as a draft for human review.

author: Cayman
subject: fix(bindings): make native STF setup and memory ownership safe (#648)
body:
**Motivation**

Lodestar's experimental native STF integration needs explicit
configuration and state ownership across historical workers, reloads,
and garbage collection. This provides the native foundation for
[Lodestar #10014](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10014),
which builds on
[#9632](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9632).

**Description**

- `BeaconConfig` owns a copy of the chain config and genesis validators
root. `BeaconStateView.createFromBytes(bytes, config)` requires it
explicitly; states and descendants retain it independently of the
JavaScript wrapper. Configuration storage and parsing live together,
with no ambient `config.set` or native setup/factory abstraction.
- `BeaconStateView` accepts full and blinded signed blocks, validates
numeric and serialized inputs, preserves SSZ bigint fields, and rejects
Gloas and later transitions. Sync committee lookups include duplicate
validator positions. Canonical `SLOT_DURATION_MS` takes precedence over
deprecated seconds defaults.
- `Number.toU64Exact()` from zapi 4.1.0 validates unsigned integer
inputs. Configuration preserves `Infinity` as the maximum-u64 sentinel
and rejects unsafe finite integers, including blob schedule entries.
- `release()` is idempotent and preserves independently retained
descendants. Active calls retain their resources through JavaScript
getters and callbacks; release requests reject subsequent access
immediately and defer cleanup until active calls return.
- Tree pools, mutable STF caches, validator monitors, and metrics are
isolated per Node.js environment. Pools allocate on first state
construction, and native state allocations are reported to V8, including
getter allocations. Atomic allocation counters account for background
Fulu shuffling.

This supports controlled pre-Gloas fleet testing. Ownership and host
integration requirements are documented beside the owning APIs.
Regressions cover configuration isolation and collection, detached
constructor inputs, callback-triggered release, worker teardown, and
memory pressure.

The earlier devnet validation used native `d7e17aa0` and Lodestar
`e836ad8780`, before this refresh. That three-node Fulu Kurtosis devnet
passed Assertoor stability and proposal checks, matched
native/TypeScript sync duties and historical state, published native
sync contributions, and agreed at slot 777 / finalized epoch 22. The
enclave has been removed. Repeated observer replay hit the two-peer
topology's request limits; checkpoint recovery restored agreement.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

This PR was written primarily by Codex.

subject: refactor: iterate compact proof reconstruction (#684)
body:
**Motivation**

recursively builds nodes after validating the proof depth.

**Description**

subtrees. Validate the descriptor and leaf count before node allocation,
and release every unfinished subtree on failure.

scratch, and every pool-exhaustion point on shorter spines.

`computeAttestationsRewards` always uses

from `3 * 2**24` to `2**24`, and the state transition
(`getRewardsAndPenaltiesAltair`) already selects it by fork. Since
Bellatrix the API reports about one third of the inactivity penalty
actually applied to balances.

**Description**

`getRewardsAndPenaltiesAltair`.

- `computeTotalAttestationsRewardsAltair`: use

author: Chen Kai
subject: fix(bindings): preserve eth1 bigint values (#735)
body:
**Motivation**

Follow up to #730 and the remaining Eth1Data conversion path in [#621,
item 34](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/issues/621). The
`eth1Data` getter returns a bigint deposit count, but `toValue()` still
routes the same field and nested `eth1DataVotes` through signed-number
conversion. Small counts have the wrong JavaScript type, wide counts
lose precision or fail the signed cast, and maximum uint64 becomes
`Infinity`.

**Description**

Centralize bigint field mappings in the binding converter, with no SSZ
or consensus-type changes.

- `bigint_fields` lists container types and field names, preserving
existing mappings from #648 and adding `Eth1Data.deposit_count`. Missing
fields or fields whose native type is not `u64` fail compilation.
- Recursive conversion applies the same mapping to state values and
nested votes. The `eth1Data` getter reuses this converter.
- Binding regressions cover exact high-bit counts, nested votes, getter
consistency, unchanged number/Infinity fields, and unchanged serialized
bytes.

Merged current `main`, including #648's mainnet `toValue()` stack fix.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation was primarily AI-authored with Codex, with independent
AI-assisted review.

author: Nazar Hussain
subject: fix: revert fast confirmation to finalized on error (#10220)
body:
**Motivation**

If the fast confirmation rule throws, the error is logged at debug and
`confirmedRoot` keeps its previous value. After a reorg that root can
sit on the losing branch and still be sent to the EL as `safeBlockHash`.
The spec reverts to the finalized checkpoint in that case.

Seen when the head moves to a sibling at epoch start, its post-state is
not in the block state cache, and there is an equivocator or a skipped
slot. The epoch-start chain safety check then throws on the missing head
state.

**Description**

- On error, set `confirmedRoot` to the finalized checkpoint, count it as
a reset/fallback, and log at warn.
- Notify subscribers outside the rule's try/catch so a notify failure
does not undo a valid root.
- Skip the epoch-start chain safety check when the confirmed block is
already behind or not an ancestor of head, matching the spec's
short-circuit `or`.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: merge attester duties for newly discovered validators (#10213)
body:
`pollBeaconAttestersForEpoch` compared an incremental poll's duty count
with the entire epoch cache size. When `dependentRoot` stayed unchanged,
a delta batch no larger than the cache was discarded, silently dropping
newly-active validators' attester duties.

Merge missing duties unconditionally, retaining selection-proof
generation. Use the cache size increase only for the debug log and
count. The regression test covers one new duty arriving with one or two
duties already cached.

This is the attester-duties sibling of #10197, with the same root cause
confirmed by nflaig in
[issuecomment-5869536530](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10197#issuecomment-5869536530)
and traced by lodekeeper through the full-index and incremental-index
polling paths.

- `pnpm vitest run --project unit
packages/validator/test/unit/services/attestationDuties.test.ts`: all 9

author: Cayman
subject: fix: preserve pending view nodes (#740)
body:
**Motivation**

Part of #158's ownership cleanup. A failed `TreeViewState.commitNodes()`
can let Merkle-tree cleanup reclaim pending nodes that the view still
caches. With a four-slot pool, pushing to a list, failing its commit,
allocating an unrelated leaf, and destroying the view frees that
unrelated leaf. Before the fix, the regression reports:

```text
test:ssz
+- run test ssz 26 pass, 1 fail (27 total)
error: 'tree_view.list_basic_test.test.memory_safety: failed list commit preserves unrelated reused pool slots' failed:
```

Commit also sorts `changed.keys()` directly. When rebuilding fails, maps
large enough to use a hash index retain stale lookup positions,
preventing reliable subsequent edits.

**Description**

Preserve pending nodes and dirty-key lookups across failed commits.

- `commitNodes` temporarily retains replacement nodes through rebuilding
and root publication, then restores exactly those references with
`unrefUnsafe`, including partial acquisition failures.
- `changed.sortUnstable` sorts entries and rebuilds the existing map
index without allocating.
- Add regressions for pool-slot reuse, retry after further edits,
partial retain failure, duplicate replacements, borrowed-root
publication, and dirty-map lookups.

This preserves the existing PMT ownership contract and adds no scratch
allocation. It complements #611's allocator-failure coverage and does
not depend on #724's deep-tree reclamation fix.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation was primarily AI-authored with Codex.

author: Cayman
subject: refactor: retain view roots last (#738)
body:
**Motivation**

Part of #158's ownership cleanup. List and container view initialization
currently retains the input root before the remaining fallible work,
requiring special rollback paths to preserve the caller's ownership.
List initialization also allocates a child-cache entry just to read its
length.

**Description**

Retain the root only after allocation and metadata reads succeed.

- `ListBasicTreeView.init` and `ListCompositeTreeView.init` read
`ST.tree.length` directly, so initialization only allocates the view
itself.
- `ContainerTreeView.init` and `StructContainerTreeView.init` retain the
root as their final fallible operation.
- Remove `deinitAfterInitFailure` and the unused chunk `getLength`
helpers.
- Cover single-allocation initialization, fresh and retained caller
roots on OOM, and reference-overflow cleanup.
- Use `std.testing.checkAllAllocationFailures` for participation
rotation, checking cleanup and participation roots across failures.

The existing allocation-failure work in #611 remains independent.

author: Chen Kai
subject: refactor(stf): replace load-state recursive diff with linear scan (#741)
body:
## Motivation

State loading recursively diffs validator and inactivity-score buffers.
This addresses the recursion part of #621, item 42.

## Description

Replace the recursive binary partition with a linear scan over
fixed-size elements. One whole-buffer `mem.eql` first keeps the
unchanged case on the vectorized path. The binary partition came from
Lodestar TS, where one native `Buffer.compare` over a large range is
cheaper than a JS loop. In Zig the partition only re-compares changed
ranges at every level, so a single linear pass is both simpler and
faster.

- Merge the validator and inactivity-score helpers into
`findModifiedIndices(element_size, ...)`.
- Drop the offset parameter. It only carried recursion state and every
caller passed 0.
- The scan is bounded by the element count, needs no stack, and still
appends indices in ascending order. On OOM, the caller keeps the indices
already appended.
- Tests cover empty, single, dense, sparse and unchanged inputs, zero
allocation for equal inputs, and allocation failures.

The `loadState` binding bench used to load a state onto itself, so the
diff always exited on the first comparison. It now loads the era 01629
state onto the era 01628 seed, which exercises the diff and the rebuild
of modified validators.

Bench (ReleaseSafe, mainnet, `bindings/perf/loadState.test.ts`):

| Case | Binary partition | Linear scan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| native, internal serialize seed | 91.7 ms | 71.2 ms |
| native, prebuilt seedValidatorsBytes | 47.5 ms | 28.0 ms |

The implementation and tests were primarily AI-authored.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: deduplicate and stream execution payload envelopes by root (#10207)
body:
By-root requests reconstructed all archived envelopes before sending a
response, including duplicate roots. A request repeating one archived
root 128 times caused four Engine calls containing 128 copies of the
same hash, followed by 128 body verifications and envelope
serializations.

- Deduplicate roots before lookup so each envelope is reconstructed and
served once.
- Reconstruct and yield batches of at most 32 envelopes
(`MAX_BODIES_PER_REQUEST`), allowing responses to start after the first
batch.
- Preserve a partial response if the EL fails after some envelopes were
served; return `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` if none were served. The by-root
protocol permits partial responses.

Broader reconstruction limits, worker backpressure, and cancellation are
tracked in #10193.

author: Cayman
subject: fix: prune legacy hot data columns on startup (#10223)
body:
**Motivation**

Legacy hot data column sidecars survive startup and are not covered by
archive pruning. A Hoodi audit found 55,680 expired columns across 435
block roots in this bucket, with some blobs still retrievable about 37
days later despite the 4,096-epoch retention window. The legacy archive
bucket was empty.

**Description**

Clear the entire legacy hot column bucket in `pruneHotDb()` using the
existing helper that deletes keys in batches of 1,000. Regression tests
cover empty, 128-entry, and 1,024-entry buckets and verify that archived
sidecars, flat-file columns, and hot blocks remain intact.

**Validation**

- Confirmed the populated-bucket regression cases fail before the fix.
- Passed all 24 tests in `beacon.test.ts`, `dataColumnStore.test.ts`,
and `flatFileStoreUpgrade.test.ts` with `pnpm vitest run --project
unit`.
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm --filter @lodestar/beacon-node check-types`

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

This PR was written primarily by OpenAI Codex, including the
investigation, implementation, tests, and PR description.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: perf: avoid rescanning pruned state history (#10216)
body:
State pruning rescans from slot zero every finalization, repeatedly
loading obsolete state values from LevelDB.

Track the last successfully pruned cutoff and scan only newly eligible
ranges. Skip unchanged cutoffs, reset progress on restart, and retry
failed pruning.

- Validation: 39 archive-store tests, targeted Biome checks, and
beacon-node type checking passed after merging unstable.
- Overnight unstable-sas results at 08:35 UTC on September 30: 124
pruning runs over 13 hours averaged 0.66s, versus 3.99s before
deployment. Logs confirm three new state archive/delete cycles completed
successfully.
- Latest 30-minute beacon RSS averaged 9.60 GB, versus 13.58 GB before
deployment. The node remained synced without another restart; stable-sas
still needs rollout validation.

author: Cayman
subject: refactor: remove unused view reads (#739)
body:
**Motivation**

Part of #158's view API cleanup. The unused bulk view readers and
composite iterator `next()` add ownership choices to the read API: the
bulk reader returns cached child pointers, while `next()` allocates a
child view that the caller must destroy. There are no live monorepo
consumers of these paths.

**Description**

Remove `CompositeChunks.getAllReadonly`, its list/vector wrappers,
composite `ReadonlyIterator.next`, and its sole caller, the otherwise
unused `getActiveValidatorIndices` helper.

Value and root iteration remains available through `nextValue`,
`nextValuePtr`, and `nextRoot`; scalar iteration and individual child
access keep their current behavior.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation was primarily AI-authored with Codex.

author: twoeths
subject: fix: init BeaconStateView from state bytes (#10227)
body:
**Motivation**

- today we depend on `BeaconStateAllForks` before initializing
BeaconStateView. It means that for a native BeaconStateView, it still
depend on a NodeJS implementation of BeaconState
- as a preparation for #9632 cc @spiral-ladder 

**Description**

- after #10200, we can now return `BeaconStateView` from
`initBeaconState()` function. A native state-transition doesn't need the
NodeJS implementation of `BeaconStateAllForks` at all
- simplify the signature of `createBeaconStateView()`, for both NodeJS
and native path, we have:

```typescript
type CreateBeaconStateViewOpts = {
  useNative: boolean;
  config: BeaconConfig;
  stateBytes: Uint8Array;
};
```

Closes #10164

author: twoeths
subject: fix: removeAndDownScoreAllDescendants of unknown sync (#10221)
body:
**Motivation**

- the function was designed to downscore peers and add track bad blocks
but we commented it out for no reason
- it turns out the only flow we should call it is when the
`invalidParentPayload`
- now that if we fail to download block, we keep that pending block
until `pruneFinalized()` so we cannot downscore peer if it's
pre-finalized, because the finalized checkpoint could advance
- on `EXECUTION_ENGINE_INVALID`, we cannot penalize peers because it
could be from an optimistic sync node, as specified in the spec

it means this PR does not change the behavior much compared to
`unstable`, and it explains why we disabled the "reportPeers" part for
so long

**Description**

- restore the original `removeAndDownScoreAllDescendants()` behavior:
track bad blocks, report peers
- only call it with `DroppedItemReason.invalidParentPayload` reason
- extract to a new `removeAndBanAllDescendants()`: similar to
`removeAndDownScoreAllDescendants()` but we don't `reportPeer()` there

Closes #10091

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

- created with the help of Claude

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: track slashing signature domains across forks (#10217)
body:
**Motivation**

Pooled slashings can become invalid across a fork transition, but block
production still selects them, causing the produced block to fail
signature verification. For example, future-slot headers or
future-target attestations signed with the pre-fork domain can be
admitted just before the fork and become invalid immediately afterward.

**Description**

Cache the signature domains used to validate proposer and attester
slashings, then evict entries whose domains differ in the proposal
state. This avoids repeating BLS verification during block production.

Revalidate persisted slashings on startup to rebuild the cache. Also fix
proposer-slashing key decoding and replacement writes so persistence
preserves valid slashings.

Closes #10215

author: twoeths
subject: refactor(cli): init BeaconState (#10200)
body:
**Motivation**

`initBeaconState()` mixes source selection, loading, validation, and
persistence, making it difficult to maintain.

Refactor startup to select a BeaconState serialized bytes and
deserialize exactly once. This also prepares the initialization flow to
return `IBeaconStateView` in a separate PR.

**Description**

- Use source-specific preparation functions and a shared template that
constructs, validates, persists, and logs the selected state.
- Read genesis identity, slot, and active-validator statistics from
serialized bytes
- Make checkpoint downloads return bytes without constructing a state.
- Preserve the main `unstable` behavior

```text
                    initBeaconState()
                            |
                    Validate options
                            |
              Read archived DB bytes once
              and assess weak subjectivity
                            |
                      Can resume DB?
                      /            \
                    yes             no
                     |               |
                Prepare DB     Select source by priority:
                     |           1. checkpointState
                     |           2. checkpointSyncUrl
                     |           3. persisted / unsafe checkpoint
                     |           4. genesis
                     |               |
                     +-------+-------+
                             |
                Selected bytes + callbacks
                             |
                executeStateInitialization()
                             |
                   Deserialize state once
                             |
                        validate()
                             |
                    persist() if needed
                             |
                          log()
                             |
                    Return selected state
```
Behavior changes to note:

- weak subjectivity period check is computed with state bytes, not
BeaconStateAllForks
- DB-loaded anchors are no longer persisted again, including at genesis
slot.
- `ignoreWeakSubjectivityCheck` only bypasses the period check. Supplied
checkpoint root and epoch mismatches always fail.
- Only the selected state is fully deserialized
- API state decoding uses the configured fork at the serialized slot,
rather than response fork metadata.

part of #10164

**Sanity tests**
- when `checkpointSyncUrl` is not defined or no `forceCheckpointSync`

```

```

```

Sep-29 08:08:56.793[]                 ^[[33mwarn^[[39m: Forced syncing from checkpoint even though db state is within weak subjectivity period slot=4037920
```
