author: Nico Flaig
subject: test: add `initBeaconState` unit tests (#10233)
body:
Adds unit tests for beacon node startup state selection
(`initBeaconState`), which had no coverage while #10200, #10228 and
#10230 changed it. The cases cover the main startup paths and safety
checks: genesis start, resuming from the db within or outside the weak
subjectivity period, checkpoint state with and without
`--forceCheckpointSync`, stale checkpoint state and
`--ignoreWeakSubjectivityCheck`, `--wssCheckpoint` mismatch, checkpoint
state from another network, last persisted checkpoint state and the db
fallback, fork version check for unfinalized sources, and db ahead of an
older checkpoint state.

Tests use a real LevelDB and `--checkpointState` files, checkpoint sync
URL specifics are already covered in `networks.test.ts`. Assertions
check the selected anchor state, `isFinalized`, archived states and
error codes rather than log or error wording. Each guarded behavior was
checked by reverting it in the source, e.g. the pre #10230 genesis
fallback or `--ignoreWeakSubjectivityCheck` bypassing a
`--wssCheckpoint` mismatch, which fails the corresponding test.

The cases were picked from a larger differential matrix of 840 startup
scenarios, see
https://gist.github.com/nflaig/9c6685c18852fcdf0aa310de33435338 for the
harness to rerun on future refactors.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: reject checkpoint sync state with mismatching fork (#10228)
body:
Follow-up to #10200. Checkpoint sync states are now decoded using the
local config's fork at the state slot, so the `Eth-Consensus-Version`
response header was no longer read. Servers omitting the header were
accepted, and a server on a different fork schedule failed with an
unclear `Cannot extract weak subjectivity summary` error.

- require the `Eth-Consensus-Version` header again and reject the state
if it does not match the fork local config expects at that slot
- add the expected fork and slot to `Cannot extract weak subjectivity
summary` errors, to hint at a fork or network mismatch for sources
without a header

Tested by running `initBeaconState` from before #10200 (3579e999b5),
current unstable and this branch against a local LevelDB, state files
and a mock checkpoint sync server.

Fork schedule skew, local node and server disagree on `FULU_FORK_EPOCH`,
empty db, state at epoch 500:

| | server behind (serves electra, local expects fulu) | server ahead
(serves fulu, local expects electra) |
|---|---|---|
| before #10200 | accepted and persisted, every restart then fails with
`First offset must equal to fixedEnd` | `State current fork version
0x06000000 not equal to current config 0x05000000` |
| unstable | `Cannot extract weak subjectivity summary from
checkpointSyncUrl` | same |
| this PR | `Checkpoint sync server returned electra state at slot 16000
but local config expects fulu` | `Checkpoint sync server returned fulu
state at slot 16000 but local config expects electra` |

`assertAnchorStateForkMatchesConfig` does not catch this case. On
unstable the weak subjectivity byte scan fails before it runs, and
before #10200 a server that had not activated the fork yet passed it
since the state's own fork field is consistent. For sources without a
header, e.g. `--checkpointState`, this PR reports `Cannot extract weak
subjectivity summary from checkpoint file, expected fulu state at slot
16000, possible fork or network mismatch`.

Server omitting `Eth-Consensus-Version`: rejected before #10200,
accepted on unstable, rejected again with this PR.

Full matrix of 15 db states (empty, within or outside weak subjectivity
period, ahead of checkpoint, genesis only, corrupt, other network,
persisted checkpoint states) x 57 flag combinations (`checkpointState`,
`checkpointSyncUrl`, `unsafeCheckpointState`,
`lastPersistedCheckpointState`, `wssCheckpoint`, `forceCheckpointSync`,
`ignoreWeakSubjectivityCheck`, genesis) = 855 scenarios, comparing
anchor state, `isFinalized`, db writes and errors:

- vs unstable, only the 9 missing header scenarios differ
- vs before #10200, the remaining differences are the intended ones from
#10200: `ignoreWeakSubjectivityCheck` no longer bypasses a
`wssCheckpoint` mismatch (24), a corrupt archived state no longer blocks
checkpoint sync (30), and the genesis block is no longer re-persisted
from a db at slot 0 (8, db writes only)

author: Nico Flaig
subject: chore: remove dead `forceGenesis` flag (#10231)
body:
The hidden `--forceGenesis` flag used to create the genesis state from
eth1 deposits instead of loading a genesis file. Since eth1 related code
was removed in #8692, its only remaining effect is to skip the genesis
file, which makes a fresh start fail with `Failed to initialize beacon
state`. Nobody should be setting it, so remove it instead of keeping it
around as deprecated.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: fall back to db and check fork for unfinalized checkpoint states (#10230)
body:
When `--lastPersistedCheckpointState` is set but no checkpoint state was
persisted, startup falls back to genesis even if the db holds an
archived state. That means syncing from genesis and writing the genesis
state into a db that already has later states. States loaded via
`--unsafeCheckpointState` or `--lastPersistedCheckpointState` also skip
the anchor state fork version check that finalized sources get, so a
state from another network is accepted.

- fall back to the archived db state instead of genesis if no
unfinalized checkpoint state is found, same as if no checkpoint source
was set
- check the anchor state fork version for unfinalized sources too

Behavior changes:

- stale db + `--lastPersistedCheckpointState` with nothing persisted
resumes from the db with the usual stale state warning instead of
starting from genesis, and no longer needs a genesis file
- if that db state is corrupt, startup now fails on it like it does
without checkpoint flags, instead of silently starting from genesis
- an unfinalized checkpoint state whose fork version does not match the
config is rejected with `State current fork version ... not equal to
current config ...`

Verified with the startup matrix from #10228 (855 scenarios), only these
cases change.

author: Cayman
subject: chore(deps): bump hashtree revision (#743)
body:
**Motivation**

The current hashtree-z pin sends baseline x86_64 builds through Zig's
SHA-256 fallback even though hashtree selects its backend at runtime.
[ChainSafe/hashtree-z#13](https://github.com/ChainSafe/hashtree-z/pull/13)
enables that dispatch on supported targets and fixes x86_64 macOS
linking with explicit CPU features.

**Description**

Update `hashtree` in `build.zig.zon` from `f5c1b81` to `9b0fdad`,
including the package hash generated by `zig fetch`.

author: Chen Kai
subject: refactor: migrate deprecated zig std APIs (#742)
body:
**Motivation**

Zig 0.16 marks several legacy standard-library aliases and search
helpers as deprecated. Keeping those names in the codebase creates
migration warnings and makes future upgrades harder to audit.

**Description**

Migrate the repository to the current Zig 0.16 standard-library names.

- Replace deprecated collection aliases with `std.ArrayList` and
`std.array_hash_map.Auto`, `Custom`, and `String`.
- Replace deprecated `std.mem.indexOf*` and `lastIndexOf*` helpers with
the corresponding `find*` APIs.
- Replace static bit set `initEmpty()` calls with `.empty`.
- Document the Zig 0.16 naming rules in `AGENTS.md`.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation and verification were assisted by Codex; the changes were
reviewed against the installed Zig 0.16.0 standard-library source.

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: feat(builder): assemble execution payload bids (#9978)
body:
## Motivation

The Builder needs one explicit, tested boundary for turning exact Engine
payload material into the fork-correct `ExecutionPayloadBid` before
pricing, signing, publication, and slot orchestration are wired
together.

Nico's `nflaig/builder` proof of concept performs this mapping inside
`SlotBidder`. This PR extracts only the message assembly so the protocol
fields and later-fork behavior can be reviewed independently.

## Changes

- Assemble all common bid fields from an exact `BuiltPayload` plus
caller-owned proposal context.
- Force `executionPayment` to zero for the p2p trustless bid path.
- Hash execution requests with the matching fork type.
- Check at runtime that the payload's fork matches the bid's fork.
- Require Heze `inclusionListBits` explicitly and validate its exact
committee length before assembly.
- Take `prevRandao` from caller-supplied BN build attributes and reject
a returned payload that differs. Reuse `ForkPostGloas` for shared
constraints while retaining fork-specific required inputs.
- Reject runtime payload-fork mismatches and invalid or unsafe numeric
bid values with structured errors. Reject slot mismatches and payloads
whose block hash equals their parent hash before assembling a bid.

## Scope

This PR does not compute bid value, check balance or coverability,
retain payload material, select proposer preferences, sign or publish
bids, schedule slot work, or wire the Builder runtime.

#9958 has merged, and `BuiltPayload` is the plain type after its review.
This branch is merged forward to `unstable`, so the diff is the two
bid-assembly files.

Tracking:
[LOD-62](https://linear.app/kriso/issue/LOD-62/bid-assembly-01-assemble-fork-correct-execution-payload-bids)

Reference: `nflaig/builder` at `99fd8fa9ad`

Historical validation base: `f22c5ce63e`

Validated head: `634d348cc99296e055608e46b4ff107273ad19ed`

## Testing

At `634d348cc99296e055608e46b4ff107273ad19ed`:

- 23 focused assembly tests passed, including short/oversized Heze
vectors and Gloas/Heze prevRandao mismatches.
- The six new regression cases failed against the previous
implementation.
- Ordinary Builder type-check, changed-file Biome, build/import and diff
checks passed.

The fork integration callers pass the expected value from their build
request and reject inconsistent material before retention or
publication. Local validation does not establish hosted CI or a live
BN/EL lifecycle.

## Review plan

Treat this and #9979 as one logical bid assembly/publication path. If
maintainers prefer fewer service-only PRs, combine the two around their
first runtime consumer.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used during codebase research, implementation,
drafting, testing, and review. The submitted code and PR text were
reviewed and revised by the author, including technical decisions.

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: feat(builder): publish execution payload bids (#9979)
body:
## Motivation

The Builder should not sign or submit the same slot and parent tuple
twice, even after old ledger records are pruned. This PR separates
signing and Beacon Node publication from payload construction and
scheduling.

## Description

Adds `BidPublisher`, which checks the local Builder index and retained
payload before signing, fingerprints the complete fork-correct Gloas or
Heze bid, records its slot and parent tuple, and submits through
`publishExecutionPayloadBid`.

A rejected or ambiguous request keeps its reservation. Ledger pruning
now advances a monotonic oldest-slot cutoff, so deleting an old
reservation cannot allow that slot to be signed again. This preserves
bounded history without retaining every failed publication indefinitely.
It is an implementation policy, not a protocol-wide restriction on
bidding.

Scheduling, pricing, retries, storage, selection, reveal and runtime
wiring remain separate.

## Review scope

The #9975 ledger dependency is merged. The pruning correction exposed an
add/add conflict with that squash-merged parent. I merged the exact
upstream base `82e7577c8bebe2c6cca1ec633d690f9bbdcab087` and preserved
the tested correction.

The resulting diff contains the publisher source/tests, the Heze signer
overload/tests, and the ledger cutoff correction/tests. Historical
parent-only changes are no longer part of the review diff.

## Testing

At `91038c140a9b6257194d621da0d4e162d7e61d10`:

- All 40 publisher, signer and ledger tests passed.
- Regressions reproduced repeat signing after pruning for pending,
failed and accepted publication before the fix.
- A backwards prune call cannot reopen an expired slot.
- Ordinary Builder type-check, changed-file Biome, build/import and diff
checks passed.

These are local component checks. Fresh full hosted CI and the complete
BN/EL lifecycle are not claimed.

Tracking [LOD-63](https://linear.app/kriso/issue/LOD-63).

> This PR was written primarily with Codex assistance and manually
reviewed and tested against Lodestar's existing patterns.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nico Flaig <nflaig@protonmail.com>

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: refactor(builder): share one beacon event subscription (#10064)
body:
## Motivation

Follow up on the [shared-subscription suggestion in
#9976](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9976#discussion_r3981963194).
Builder currently opens separate streams for blocks and proposer
preferences, even though the API client already supports multiple
topics.

## Description

- Let Builder own one subscription for `block` and
`proposer_preferences`.
- Dispatch to the existing BlockObserver and ProposerPreferencesTracker.
Remove their separate subscription methods.
- Keep block retrieval, root deduplication, preference identity and slot
pruning unchanged.
- Pass the existing abort signal through the stream and block requests.
Ignore events delivered after shutdown, suppress block fetch results
that arrive after abort, and isolate consumer failures.
- Move subscription tests to Builder and retain the service-level
retrieval/cache tests.
- Include `BUILDER_EVENT_SUBSCRIPTION_FAILED` in subscription-failure
log metadata while retaining the original error. This is a filtering
aid, not a stream-recovery change.

This adds no new event client, payload-attributes contract, Engine
wiring, preference bootstrap or replay policy.

Merged #10063 renamed the store and conflicted with the lifecycle
fixtures reorganised here. A naming-only incremental correction still
left merge conflicts, so I merged its exact upstream commit
`82e7577c8bebe2c6cca1ec633d690f9bbdcab087` and resolved those fixtures
while preserving both changes. No store behavior changed.

## Testing

Current head `6c3318d9fa0ca8dbed3e55a9bc7a556d61ac4aa6`. Stream
callbacks again log at error level, matching both previous subscribers.
A regression verifies that logging the error does not stop later
delivery; shutdown stays quiet.

- All 47 targeted Builder, block-observer, preference and store tests
passed after the conflict resolution.
- Ordinary Builder type-check, changed-file Biome, Builder build/import
and diff checks passed.
- Earlier regressions reproduced the duplicate subscriptions and late
post-abort block result before their respective fixes. The
subscription-failure log also has a focused metadata assertion.

These are local component/lifecycle checks, not a real BN/EL
bid-and-reveal run. Fresh full hosted CI at this head is not claimed.

The existing API-client race when abort happens during
`getEventSource()` is addressed separately in
[#10065](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10065), tracked
under [REL-01](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar/issues/22).
Sharing the signal does not fix that transport-level race.

Tracking [LOD-87](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar/issues/93).

> This PR was created using AI assistance and manually reviewed and
tested with Codex.

author: Cayman
subject: fix: stage composite child roots (#747)
body:
**Motivation**

`CompositeChunks.commit()` caches each child root before the parent
rebuild succeeds. After a later failure, replacing a child can free that
root while its ID remains cached. If the pool reuses the slot, parent
cleanup can release an unrelated node.

The new regression reproduces this on `main`:

```text
error: 'tree_view.chunks_test.test.memory_safety: failed composite parent rebuild does not cache child-owned roots' failed:
    try std.testing.expect(!unrelated.getState(&pool).isFree());
```

This addresses the composite ownership follow-up from #158 and builds on
the pending-node protection in #740.

**Description**

Stage composite child roots in the existing commit scratch array and
publish cached roots only after the parent rebuild succeeds.

- `CompositeChunks.commit()` gathers child roots locally, removing the
node-cache capacity reservation and premature cache writes.
- `TreeViewState.commitStagedNodes()` shares rebuilding and temporary
reference protection with packed views, then refreshes existing cache
entries and publishes the parent root. Missing cache entries remain
lazy.
- `chunks_test.zig` covers allocation failures, partial child commits,
list-length retry, and pool-slot reuse during deinitialization, cache
clearing, and cache transfer.

Child views can still complete their own commits before the parent
fails. The parent keeps its committed root and dirty entries so the
operation can be retried.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation and regression tests were primarily AI-authored, with
AI-assisted codebase exploration and verification.

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: feat(builder): match selected local bids (#9980)
body:
## Motivation

Before reveal, the Builder must prove that an imported post-Gloas block
contains an exact bid it signed and still has the matching payload
material for. Builder index or execution block hash alone is not a
sufficient financial-decision boundary.

## Description

Adds `BidSelector`, an architecture-neutral selection matcher that:

- recomputes the fetched Beacon block root and compares it with the
observed event root;
- checks event slot, fetched block slot, configured fork, and selected
bid slot;
- ignores foreign and self-build selections;
- requires exact slot, parent block hash, parent block root, and
execution block hash matches in both `BidLedger` and retained payload
identity;
- compares the complete signed bid's fork-specific SSZ root with the
local ledger record before recording a win;
- records selecting block roots idempotently;
- returns typed selected or ignored outcomes and structured integrity
errors.

The fingerprint is local matching data, not a proposed `bid_root` SSE
field. These tests enforce the exact-bid contract; they do not
demonstrate an attack using a valid BN-imported block.

The input is structurally compatible with API-02's `ObservedBlock`, but
this PR does not wire the observer, payload store, or reveal path.

The BidLedger dependency (#9975) has merged and this branch is merged
forward to `unstable`, so the diff is the two selection files:

- `packages/builder/src/services/bidSelector.ts`
- `packages/builder/test/unit/services/bidSelector.test.ts`

Tracking:
[LOD-65](https://linear.app/kriso/issue/LOD-65/select-match-01-match-imported-blocks-to-exact-local-bid-identities)

## Tests

Validated locally on 11 September 2026 at
`d802fcb2c157e2765670e6ad8ae9eee669abb88c`, using Node 24.13.0:

- 40 focused tests passed (21 selector tests and 19 ledger tests)
- Builder package type-check
- Builder package Biome check
- Builder build and module import check

These are local component checks, not a hosted-CI result or a complete
BN/EL Builder lifecycle run.

## Review scope

Ready for review as a scoped component now that #9975 has merged. The
matcher accepts an observed block and injected retained-payload lookup.
It does not require the envelope assembly or publication PRs to compile
or be reviewed.

Runtime wiring remains separate. If a combined bid or reveal-path PR

subject: feat(builder): assemble stateless payload envelopes (#9981)
body:
## Motivation

A selected local bid must reveal only the exact payload material that
was retained for that bid. Envelope construction should fail closed if
the retained payload belongs to a different slot, parent execution
block, or execution block hash.

## Description

Adds a pure `createExecutionPayloadEnvelopeMaterial` boundary that:

- accepts the selecting Beacon block root, local Builder index, selected
`ExecutionPayloadBid`, and retained payload material carrying its
original parent Beacon block root;
- verifies slot, parent execution block hash, parent Beacon block root,
execution block hash, local Builder index, ordered blob commitments and
execution requests root;
- constructs the stateless `ExecutionPayloadEnvelope` without mutating
retained material;
- preserves execution requests, blobs, KZG proofs, Builder index, Beacon
block root, and parent Beacon block root;
- supports both Gloas and Heze retained payloads;
- reports structured mismatch errors.

The caller still establishes the exact locally signed selection. This
helper checks the retained material against that bid; it does not repeat
signature, EL or KZG validation. Signing, API publication, reveal
cutoffs, retries, store eviction, metrics and Builder wiring remain
outside this PR.

#9958 has merged and `BuiltPayload` is the plain type after its review.
This branch is merged forward to `unstable`, so the diff is the two
envelope-assembly files.

Tracking:
[LOD-66](https://linear.app/kriso/issue/LOD-66/rev-assembly-01-assemble-exact-stateless-envelope-material)

builder-index, ordered commitment and execution-request mismatch
regressions. Builder type-check, changed-file Biome, build/import and

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: feat(builder): coordinate bounded payload build jobs (#9973)
body:
## Motivation

The Builder needs to coordinate payload preparation and retrieval before
event and runtime wiring are added. #9958 has merged; this PR's
component diff is the two orchestrator files.

## Changes

`PayloadOrchestrator` accepts an injected `PayloadSource` and a
caller-defined retrieval time. It bounds active jobs, shares identical
requests, rejects conflicting reuse of a job ID, and cleans up on
success, failure or cancellation.

Preparation retries a missing payload ID using the existing retry
helper, without extending the retrieval deadline. Other source errors
pass through unchanged. Transport retries remain the source's
responsibility. Preparation and retrieval deadlines have distinct
structured errors, including when the source itself throws a
`TimeoutError`.

The timer limit is checked against the actual preparation delay. Request
contents must remain unchanged until the job settles; the scheduling
fields are captured separately.

This does not add Builder/CLI wiring, choose an EL topology, produce
payload attributes, or implement storage, bidding or reveal.

## Testing

At `9474e4eb99`:

- 36 orchestration tests and 11 payload-source tests passed.
- Builder type-check, changed-file Biome, build/import and diff checks
passed.
- Coverage includes missing-ID retries, the original deadline,
cancellation during backoff, source error preservation, duplicate jobs
and late-result cleanup.

These are deterministic component tests, not a live BN/EL lifecycle run.

Tracking: [LOD-58](https://linear.app/kriso/issue/LOD-58).
Fork [#61](https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar/pull/61) shares
this branch but retains its historical base; use this upstream diff for
review.

this description.

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: feat(builder): publish stateless payload envelopes (#9982)
body:
## Motivation

The Builder needs a small safety boundary between exact envelope
assembly and later reveal timing/runtime wiring. Once a local selection
is verified, the envelope must be signed and submitted at most once
without allowing a conflicting payload for the same Beacon block root.

## Description

This PR adds an `EnvelopePublisher` that:

- accepts complete stateless envelope material;
- requires the local Builder index and an exact recorded selection;
- signs through `BuilderSigner`;
- reserves the exact unsigned envelope root before the network outcome
becomes ambiguous;
- submits the envelope with blobs and KZG proofs;
- explicitly requests `consensus_and_equivocation` validation;
- marks publication only after the Beacon Node accepts it;
- coalesces concurrent exact attempts while keeping each caller's
cancellation independent;
- aborts the shared request only after all waiting callers cancel, and
permits a later exact retry; and
- rejects changed envelope content for the same selecting block root.

The selection lookup is injected, so this PR does not choose an SSE
contract, payload-store implementation, cutoff, retry policy, metrics,
or runtime wiring.

## Dependencies

The BidLedger dependency (#9975) has merged and this branch is merged
forward to `unstable`, so the diff is the two publisher files:

- `packages/builder/src/services/envelopePublisher.ts`
- `packages/builder/test/unit/services/envelopePublisher.test.ts`

## Validation

Validated locally on 11 September 2026 at
`a2fff56b20b29b778c776894f0e1024ebc151eb7`, using Node 24.13.0:

- 34 focused tests passed (15 envelope-publication tests and 19 ledger
tests)
- Builder package type-check
- Changed-file Biome check
- Builder build and module import check
- `git diff --check`

Both independent-caller cancellation regressions failed before the fix.
The added tests cover both cancellation orders, shared-signal
cancellation, listener cleanup, retry after all waiters cancel, and
suppression of an old request's late result.

These are local component checks, not a hosted-CI result or a complete
BN/EL Builder lifecycle run.

## Review scope

publisher accepts complete envelope material and uses the merged ledger.
It does not require the separate envelope assembler to compile or be
reviewed.

Runtime wiring remains separate. If a combined bid or reveal-path PR

author: Cayman
subject: feat: persist pubkey cache across restarts (#10152)
body:
## Motivation

On every restart the beacon node rebuilds the pubkey cache by
decompressing every validator pubkey from the anchor state. On mainnet
(2.37M validators) that is the single largest chunk of boot after
loading the anchor state.

## Description

- On boot, best effort load of the pubkey cache from
`${dataDir}/pubkeys` before syncing from the anchor state. Success and
failure are logged at debug.
- On graceful shutdown, save the pubkey cache to the same file as the
very last step, after `node.close()` (and after the db close in the
error path).
- Hidden `--pubkeysFile` flag overrides the location.
- Native `load()` only checks framing, ABI and checksum. The loaded
entries are spot-checked against the anchor state (index 0 and the last
overlapping index) so a file from another chain gets discarded and we
fall back to a full sync.
- Skip `getAllReadonlyValues()` for the handler's `syncPubkeys` when the
loaded cache already covers the anchor state.

## Measurements

Local mainnet restarts from an existing db (32 cores,
`--execution.engineMock`, warm page cache). Times are seconds since
process launch.

| | "Initialized state from db" to "Flat file store initialized" |
Launch to metrics server started |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unstable (3 runs) | 9.36 / 9.26 / 9.40 | 42.65 / 42.71 / 43.65 |
| this PR, file loaded (3 runs) | 1.57 / 1.55 / 1.63 | 34.73 / 34.27 /
35.30 |

About 7.8s saved per restart (~19% of time to metrics server). A run
with no file present matched unstable (9.12s / 43.26s).

- Load: 53-56ms for 2,370,466 entries
- Save on shutdown: 182-297ms
- File size: 341 MB (48 byte compressed + 96 byte affine point per
validator)

Also ran the node for 150s from a loaded file: synced to head, finality
advanced, no signature or pubkey errors, and the file was re-saved on
shutdown.

## Notes

- The file format is ABI-locked (zig version, arch). A lodestar-z
upgrade that changes it makes the load fail and the node falls back to a
full sync, then saves a fresh file on shutdown.
- Entries beyond the anchor state's validator count (from unfinalized
states in the previous run) are kept, same as they would have been in
memory had the node not restarted.
- Discarding a mismatched file uses `pubkeyCache.reset()`, which
lodestar-z documents as testing-only. It is safe here since no workers
use the cache yet.

> This PR was written primarily by Claude Code.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: Cayman
subject: perf: stream progressive hashing (#744)
body:
**Motivation**

Progressive list, bitlist, and variable-container hashing still
allocates a complete chunk array before Merkleization. The bounded
reducer introduced earlier does not bound that producer workspace. This
completes the hashing-producer follow-up in
[#158](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/issues/158).

**Description**

Stream value and serialized hashing into a bounded progressive
accumulator.

- `progressive.MerkleAccumulator` builds each progressively sized
subtree with the existing batched hashing accumulator, retaining only
the subtree roots needed to finish the right spine.
- `hashTreeRoot` producers pack basic values, hash composite children,
remove bitlist delimiters, and emit inactive container fields
incrementally.
- Existing array-based Merkleization uses the same accumulator. Public
SSZ signatures remain unchanged.
- Regression tests compare tree, value, and serialized roots across
subtree and delimiter boundaries while rejecting scratch allocations,
including nested lists and sparse containers.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation was primarily AI-authored with Codex.

author: Chen Kai
subject: refactor(state-transition): remove reused cache lock (#750)
body:
**Motivation**

`_reused_cache` and `_reused_lock` are both `threadlocal`. The lock
cannot synchronize access across threads and the cache lifetime contract
already requires callers on one thread to serialize initialization, use,
and teardown. The lock therefore adds blocking and keeps obsolete
`std.Io` parameters in the API.

**Description**

Remove the thread-local reused epoch cache mutex and its lock-only
`std.Io` parameters.

- Remove `_reused_lock` and the lock/unlock calls around cache
acquisition and teardown.
- Remove the unused `std.Io` parameters from
`EpochTransitionCache.init`, `deinitReusedEpochTransitionCache`, and
`computeUnrealizedCheckpoints`, including all callers.
- Preserve the existing caller lifetime contract for the thread-local
borrowed cache.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation and validation were assisted by Codex.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: evict invalid payload envelopes from the seen cache (#10246)
body:
A payload envelope is added to its `PayloadEnvelopeInput` once it passes
gossip validation, the full verification only runs during import. If the
import then fails because the envelope is invalid, the envelope stays in
the seen cache until the entry is finalized or evicted by the size cap.
By-root sync and range sync both reuse the cached envelope instead of
the one they get from peers, so every attempt fails the same way and the
node can't import the payload, or any block building on it, even though
peers serve a valid envelope.

This can be triggered over gossip since a builder can sign more than one
envelope for the same block, e.g. one with a wrong
`parent_beacon_block_root` (not part of the gossip checks) followed by
the valid one, and over req/resp by a peer serving a modified envelope
as in #9660.

This evicts the cache entry when the import fails with a verdict caused
by the envelope itself (`INVALID_SIGNATURE`,
`ENVELOPE_VERIFICATION_ERROR`, `EXECUTION_ENGINE_INVALID`). Sync then
recreates the entry from the block and fetches the envelope from peers
again. Execution engine errors and a missing block or state are left
alone, those are not caused by the envelope.

- add `SeenPayloadEnvelopeInput.removeInvalid()` with prune reason
`invalid`, it is a no-op if the cached entry is not the failed object as
that may already be the recreated one
- evict in the `execution_payload` gossip handler, by-root sync and
range sync, the latter also logs peer and client of the envelope source
- remove the TODO about invalid payload inputs never leaving memory

The envelope is not replaced in place. A valid envelope arriving on
gossip after the eviction is still ignored
(`PAYLOAD_ENVELOPE_INPUT_MISSING`) and is fetched by root instead, same
for the columns collected for the evicted entry. The API publish path is
unchanged.

Tested on a kurtosis devnet (minimal preset, 6s slots, Lodestar without
validators, Teku, Lighthouse) where the builder reveals an envelope with
a wrong `parent_beacon_block_root` 300ms into the slot and the valid one
at 3.5s. Lodestar on top of `glamsterdam-devnet-8` with and without this
change:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| cached envelope after failed import | kept | evicted |
| by-root sync | 68 failed attempts reusing the cached envelope | 0
failed attempts |
| payload imported | 6 min 12s later, once the entry hit the cache size
cap | 3.3s to 3.7s later, within the slot (3 of 3 slots) |
| head | stuck for 61 slots | never behind |

Closes #9660

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: replace latest messages by slot from gloas (#10128)
body:
From gloas `LatestMessage` tracks the attestation slot and
[`update_latest_messages`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-beta.0/specs/gloas/fork-choice.md#modified-update_latest_messages)
replaces a vote when `slot > store.latest_messages[i].slot`, while we
kept comparing epochs as the pre-gloas spec does. The two only differ
for a validator with two attestations in the same epoch, which is a
slashable double vote that can only reach fork choice through a block
since gossip already drops the second one. The spec keeps the vote from
the later slot regardless of arrival order, we kept whichever was
processed first, so until the attester slashing is processed our weights
could differ from other clients.

This compares slots for attestations from gloas onwards and keeps the
epoch comparison before it, see the discussion in
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/8739#discussion_r2861304520.

---------

Co-authored-by: Lodekeeper <258435968+lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: do not miss PTC duties in the first Gloas epoch (#10242)
body:
PTC duties of the first Gloas epoch only exist once the state is
upgraded at the fork, so unlike later epochs they can't be polled one
epoch ahead. The VC requested them anyway in the last Fulu epoch, which
the beacon node rejects with a 400, and only got them from the poll at
the start of the Gloas epoch. The PTC task of the fork slot runs at the
same time and checks for duties before that poll returns, so all PTC
duties of the first Gloas slot were missed.

- don't poll PTC duties before the first Gloas epoch
- at the first Gloas slot, read the duties again after waiting for the
payload or the deadline, by then the poll at the start of the epoch has
returned. All other slots are unchanged

Tested on kurtosis, minimal preset with Gloas at epoch 3, 2x
lodestar/geth with 128 validators. Payload attestation bits for each
slot of the first Gloas epoch included in the next block:

| | 24 | 25 | 26 | 27 | 28 | 29 | 30 | 31 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| unstable | 0/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 |
16/16 |
| this PR | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 |
16/16 |

On unstable the VCs published 75 of 86 PTC duties in that epoch and
logged `Failed to download PTC duties epoch=3` in epoch 2. With this PR,
in two runs, they published 80 of 80 and 77 of 77 with no errors. The
duties were downloaded 29 to 86ms into the fork slot and the payload
became available after 565 to 589ms.

Supersedes #10238 and #10240, which serve the duties from the beacon
node by advancing the head state across the fork. That runs an epoch
transition and the Gloas upgrade per request, and the result is still
speculative since blocks later in the last Fulu epoch can change the
committees.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: perf: hoist weak-subjectivity staleness check before anchor state load (#10229)
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #10227 ([review
comment](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10227#issuecomment-5926570942)).

The checkpoint weak-subjectivity staleness check lives in
`validate(state)`,
which runs **after** the anchor state has been deserialized into a
`BeaconStateView`. When a checkpoint is stale (outside the weak
subjectivity
period and `--ignoreWeakSubjectivityCheck` is not set) we build the full
state
— and reserve pubkey-cache capacity for it — only to immediately throw
`STALE_CHECKPOINT` and discard it.

The staleness check is derived purely from the state **bytes** (the weak
subjectivity summary), so it does not need the deserialized state.

## Description

Add a `validateBeforeLoad()` step to `StateInitialization` and call it
at the
top of `executeStateInitialization`, before `createBeaconStateView`:

- **checkpoint** source: the weak-subjectivity / `STALE_CHECKPOINT`
check moves
into `validateBeforeLoad()`. `validate(state)` keeps the checks that
require
the deserialized state (supplied-checkpoint match, anchor fork match,
logging).
- **genesis** source: no-op — genesis is never rejected for staleness.
- **archived (db)** source: no-op — db staleness only warns, it does not
gate
  loading.

A stale checkpoint now fails fast without building the state or
reserving
pubkey-cache capacity.

Note: the supplied-checkpoint match (`--wssCheckpoint`) still needs the
built
state, so it stays in `validate`. For a stale checkpoint that is also
outside
the WS period, `STALE_CHECKPOINT` is now surfaced before the
checkpoint-mismatch
error (previously the order was reversed); both indicate a bad
checkpoint source.

## Tests

Adds `packages/cli/test/unit/cmds/checkpointState.test.ts` asserting
that a
stale checkpoint throws `STALE_CHECKPOINT` from `validateBeforeLoad()`
and that
`createBeaconStateView`, `getValidatorCountFromStateBytes`, and
`pubkeyCache.ensureCapacity` are **not** called — plus the ignore-WS and
within-period paths.

🤖 Generated with AI assistance

author: bing
subject: chore(lint): fail on src imports of dev-only dependencies (#10090)
body:
**Motivation**

Catches src imports of dev-only dependencies like we suffered in #10077
which imported `@libp2p/utils` from beacon-node src while the package
was declared only under devDependencies.

Tests and type-check passed because dev dependencies are installed
there, but the Docker image and binaries run `pnpm install
--frozen-lockfile --prod`, which prunes them, so the node crashed on
startup with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND (#10086).

**Description**

- Enable Biome's
[correctness/noUndeclaredDependencies](https://biomejs.dev/linter/rules/no-undeclared-dependencies/javascript/)
to enforce imports in src/ being runtime dependencies of that package.
- Allow dev dependencies under test/, *.test.ts and src/testUtils/. The
rule is turned off for test files, configs/ and scripts/, which import
tools such as vitest and vite plugins declared only at the workspace
root.
- 
Sample output on top of the commit
89d0f4da2d4b0beb275874fe0481221e4625ee62 that introduced this bug:

```console
$ biome check
packages/beacon-node/src/network/libp2p/index.ts:9:82 [lint/correctness/noUndeclaredDependencies](https://biomejs.dev/linter/rules/no-undeclared-dependencies) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  ✖ Dependency @libp2p/utils isn't specified in packages/beacon-node/package.json.

     7 │ import {prometheusMetrics} from "@libp2p/prometheus-metrics";
     8 │ import {tcp} from "@libp2p/tcp";
   > 9 │ import {loopbackAddressLast, publicAddressesFirst, reliableTransportsFirst} from "@libp2p/utils";
       │                                                                                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    10 │ import type {Multiaddr} from "@multiformats/multiaddr";
    11 │ import {Libp2pInit, createLibp2p} from "libp2p";

  ℹ @libp2p/utils is part of your devDependencies, but it's not intended to be used in this file.

  ℹ You may want to consider moving it to the dependencies section.
```

author: Marko Lazic
subject: fix: surface archived envelopes the EL cannot serve (#10248)
body:
Supersedes #10201 (same change, rebased over #10207 with the review
follow-ups folded in). Co-authored with @nflaig.

**Motivation**

An archived header envelope whose body the EL can no longer serve
(`nimbus-eth1` returning no block access list for blocks with 0
withdrawals, `reth` after an EL restart on `glamsterdam-devnet-8`) was
indistinguishable from an envelope we never had: the chain getters
returned `null`, so `GET
/eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes/{block_id}` answered `404`
and the by-range non-finalized path failed with `SERVER_ERROR`.

**Description**

`BODY_UNAVAILABLE` is added to `EnvelopeReconstructionErrorCode` and
carried by the unavailable rebuild miss, like `BODY_ROOT_MISMATCH`
already was. `RebuildMiss` collapses to one shape since both variants
now carry an error.
`ReconstructMismatchPolicy` → `ReconstructMissPolicy`: "throw" for REST
/ single lookups, "omit" for by-root. The omit path now logs an
unavailable miss at debug the same way the by-range generator does, so a
partial by-root response leaves a trace.
REST: `BODY_UNAVAILABLE` maps to 503 alongside `ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE` (the
data exists, our EL can't serve it right now — clients retry or ask
another node); a body root mismatch stays 500; 404 only for an envelope
that was never archived.
By-range: the non-finalized path now ends short / `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`
on an unservable envelope, matching the finalized path, instead of
`SERVER_ERROR`.

Metrics are unchanged
(`beacon_payload_envelope_reconstruction_envelopes_total{result="unavailable"}`
still counts these).

author: Chen Kai
subject: feat(bindings): implement remaining rewards apis (#731)
body:
**Motivation**

The native state view still throws for attestation and sync-committee
reward queries, preventing the host rewards endpoints from using it.
This addresses item 36 of
[#621](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/issues/621), following
`computeBlockRewards` in #709.

```text
computeAttestationsRewards not implemented
computeSyncCommitteeRewards not implemented
```

**Description**

Implement both synchronous reward queries, matching
`computeBlockRewards`, with validator filtering, read-only state access,
and active-call ownership across JavaScript getters and output
callbacks.

- `computeAttestationsRewards` shares per-increment rewards, penalties,
and fork-specific inactivity calculation with STF settlement, uses `u64`
integer division and a fixed 32 KiB stack penalty table, and returns
ideal and eligible-validator breakdowns. This follows merged Lodestar
#10182 for floor arithmetic and #10183 for the fork-specific inactivity
quotient.
- `computeSyncCommitteeRewards` accepts full or blinded block objects,
accumulates signed participant rewards across duplicate committee
positions, retains zero results, and preserves first-occurrence order.
- Both queries throw on Phase0 with `AttestationsRewardsUnsupportedFork`
or `SyncCommitteeRewardsUnsupportedFork`. Unknown-only validator filters
return no rows. Numeric input uses zapi's exact unsigned conversions;
invalid proposer-reward fields now reject instead of being clamped to
zero. Outputs use typed `js.Object` rows and remain `number` in
JavaScript; the binding emits constant-zero API fields without storing
them in native reward rows.

The attestation query uses the current epoch-cache preparation order.
The proposed J&F and inactivity-update ordering change remains outside
this PR until Lodestar decides its reference behavior.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation was primarily AI-authored with Codex, with independent
AI-assisted review.

author: NC
subject: fix: apply epoch updates before computing attestation rewards (#10224)
body:
Follow up of #10183 

**Motivation**
 
The attestations rewards API computes on the pre-transition state, but
in epoch processing `process_rewards_and_penalties` runs after
`process_justification_and_finalization` and
`process_inactivity_updates`. The API therefore charged the inactivity
penalty on stale scores and judged leak status from stale finality.

**Description**

- `computeAttestationsRewards`: clone the state and run
justification/finalization and inactivity updates before computing,
matching the spec ordering.
- Replace the quotient-only test from #10183 with balance-delta tests:
run the epoch transition on the same state and assert every validator's
balance change equals the API total. Covers Altair, Bellatrix and
Electra, leak and no leak, and a transition that ends a leak. These also
catch the quotient bug #10183 fixed.
- Add the same balance-delta check for block rewards and a new sync
committee rewards test (previously no coverage). Both endpoints already
matched the chain.
- Fix `getBlockAltair` in the perf helpers: it cleared attester
participation with `set(index, 0)`, a no-op because `ParticipationFlags`
ORs values in. Blocks built by it paid zero attestation reward, so the
block rewards test was asserting 0 === 0 for that component. Expect the
benchmark bot to report slower `processBlock` numbers, since the perf
blocks now do real attestation work.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: request the whole range sync batch again after a processing error (#10266)
body:
After a processing error a range sync batch drops its downloaded blocks
but keeps `requests`, which after a partial download only cover the
missing data (e.g. `cols=[101]`, no blocks request). Every retry then
fails with `MISSING_BLOCKS_RESPONSE` ("No blocks in data request slot
range to validate data response against"), the peers end up in
`failedDownloadPeers` / `hasPeerSucceededCurrentRequest`,
`bestPeerToRetryBatch` returns nothing and the batch stays
`AwaitingDownload` without ever reaching `MAX_BATCH_DOWNLOAD_ATTEMPTS`,
so the chain is never torn down and sync silently stops (seen on
focil-devnet-0 for 3 days, zero `beacon_blocks_by_range` sent).

- reset `requests` to a fresh request of the whole batch whenever the
downloaded blocks are dropped (`onProcessingError`,
`onExecutionEngineError`)
- add a regression test for both paths after a partial column download

author: bing
subject: feat(bindings): zig state transition (#9632)
body:
## Summary

This PR integrates `@chainsafe/lodestar-z` as an opt-in state-transition
backend.

The native backend is enabled with `--chain.nativeStateTransition`,
backed by an existing `IBeaconStateView` abstraction. The TypeScript
implementation remains the default.

## Changes

Here's a list of changes, summarized, by category:

### State view

- `stateTransition` and `computeNewStateRoot` now take `BlockSTFInput =
{block, ssz?}`. The TS view uses `block`, the native view uses `ssz` and
serializes `block` when it is missing.
- Adds `release()` to `IBeaconStateView`. It is a no-op in TS and frees
native memory in Zig. Only spec tests call it, to avoid exhausting the
native pool.
- `NativeBeaconStateView` throws on Gloas-only members.

### Block processing

For state transition, we now rely on serialized block bytes on the
native side. This is the biggest change in this PR, so here's the flow
across several paths that rely on this:

| Block path | Serialized bytes available | TypeScript | Zig |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gossip import | Yes, from `serializedData` | Reads cached bytes,
ignores them | Uses cached bytes |
| Range/root/head sync | Yes, from `chunk.data` | Reads cached bytes,
ignores them | Uses cached bytes |
| API block import | Sometimes, from SSZ request context | Ignores bytes
| Serializes on cache miss |
| Recent state regeneration | Sometimes, from `SerializedCache` |
Ignores bytes | Uses cache or serializes |
| Historical regeneration | Yes, in the block archive | Uses decoded
block | Decodes and serializes again |
| Local block production | No signed block bytes yet | Uses assembled
block | Serializes a zero-signature block |
| Block rewards | No bytes passed to state view | Uses block object |
Serializes inside native wrapper |

### Beacon node

- `--chain.nativeStateTransition` selects the native view at startup, in
block processing, regen and historical regen.
- Startup fails if the flag is set and `GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH` is scheduled.
- The native `BeaconConfig` is built inside `createBeaconStateView` and
passed to `createFromBytes`.

### Metrics

- With the flag on, the TS state-transition metrics are not registered
(`metrics.stateTransition` is `null`) and native metrics are scraped
instead.
- Monitored validators are registered on the native side, which reports
the state-derived validator monitor metrics.
- Behavior change on the default TS path too: prev-epoch attester
hit/miss and inclusion distance are now recorded in
`onceEveryEndOfEpoch` instead of `registerValidatorStatuses`. The phase0
inclusion distance fallback is dropped, and the "Failed attestation in
previous epoch" log is post-Altair only.


### Tests

- New CI job runs minimal and mainnet spec tests with
`LODESTAR_NATIVE_STATE_TRANSITION=true`.
- Adds coverage for FFI conversion, block bytes, rewards, metrics,
cleanup and validator monitoring.



## Gloas support

Lodestar-Z does not yet support Gloas state transition and spec-test
runs skip Gloas test cases.

> This PR was developed with AI assistance. Codex was used to trace
affected state-transition call paths, assist with integration updates,
and develop test coverage.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: settle builder payment before processing parent execution requests (#10180)
body:
a builder exit request in the parent's payload was applied before the
parent's payment was settled. when the parent is older than the previous
epoch the payment was already evicted, so the exit guard saw nothing
pending and the exit went through right before the payment was re-added.
the sweep then paid out the full balance while the payment was still
queued

matches https://github.com/nflaig/consensus-specs/pull/9, our builder
sweep already withdraws the remaining balance so only the ordering
changes here

author: bing
subject: perf(state-transition): diff-synced flat validator cache (#736)
body: **Motivation** We're still seeing a steady growth in `before_process_epoch` metrics: This is an experimental PR to attempt to address this. Claude says: > `before_process_epoch` keeps getting slower with uptime because every validator write relocates its leaf and branch nodes, so the full tree walk in `EpochTransitionCache.init` loses locality over time (#710). The previous fix #712 addressed this partially by bringing the base cost down by a lot and growth lower, but we are still seeing a monotonically increasing growth in that step **Description** This PR's sole purpose is to make the full pass over all validators at the start of every epoch transition fast to address the slowing `before_process_epoch` issue: - adds **`ValidatorFlatCache`**, a flat, index-addressed copy of the validator fields that `init` reads owned by the `ReusedEpochTransitionCache`. It is derived from the validators tree and brought forward by diffing the last synced root against the current one, so upkeep is proportional to the validators that changed - the cache keeps itself sync'd by calling `sync` during `EpochTransitionCache.init` calls when crossing epoch boundaries **Note to reviewers:** the `diffAndPatch()` function requires more careful review, what it is doing is walking through subtrees and patching the flat cache from the tree if there is a diff. ## Benchmarks ### Results Benchmarked on this branch as well as on main with extra benchmark files, in a branch [`bing/bench-before-flat`](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/tree/bing/bench-before-flat). So we get a before/after comparison Tested on hoodi finalized state, slot **3962304**, **1,589,784** validators, ReleaseSafe, macOS. Both paths run on the same state every epoch. Times are means per 150 epoch window. My results as of [addaa24](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/pull/736/commits/addaa24003164003544d846d09167eea765c3e59): epoch | before, bing/bench-before-flat | current, bing/flat-cache -- | -- | -- 0 | 29.2 ms | 15.7 ms 150 | 32.2 | 13.9 300 | 36.2 | 15.1 450 | 40.0 | 14.3 600 | 44.3 | 14.5 750 | 47.1 | 14.8 900 | 48.9 | 14.1 ### Methodology 1. Load one real hoodi finalized state into a 10M-slot node pool. 2. We simulate epochs, each simulated epoch runs 32 blocks: clone the head, bump 512 random balances, rewrite 8192 participation entries, commit, keep the last 64 states. 3. Then the epoch step: rewrite every balance, write exit_epoch and withdrawable_epoch on N random validators, commit. Every epoch we sync a benchmark-owned flat cache (timed) and time the real EpochTransitionCache.init on the head. 4. Every 150 epochs we check the cache against the tree and time a real epoch transition via processSlots on a throwaway clone, 31 slots untimed, the boundary slot timed. Known gap: a cold fill costs more than init itself, and how often production runs an epoch transition on a state loaded from bytes is not measured. ### Reproduction 1. First download a hoodi state ```sh curl -fL -H "Accept: application/octet-stream" -o ~/hoodi_finalized.ssz https://checkpointsync.hoodi.ethpandaops.io/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/finalized ``` 8. Build and run before, use this branch [`bing/bench-before-flat`](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/tree/bing/bench-before-flat): ```sh zig build build-exe:bench_locality_decay -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe && cp zig-out/bin/bench_locality_decay/tmp/bench_before ``` ```sh LOCALITY_STATE=hoodi_finalized.ssz LOCALITY_EPOCHS=900 LOCALITY_MEASURE_EVERY=150 LOCALITY_REAL_SWEEP=1 LOCALITY_VALIDATOR_WRITES=50 /tmp/bench_before 2>&1 | tee before.log ``` 9. Build and run after, using this branch ```sh zig build build-exe:bench_locality_decay -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe && cp zig-out/bin/bench_locality_decay/tmp/bench_after ``` ```sh LOCALITY_STATE=hoodi_finalized.ssz LOCALITY_EPOCHS=900 LOCALITY_MEASURE_EVERY=150 LOCALITY_REAL_SWEEP=1 LOCALITY_VALIDATOR_WRITES=50 /tmp/bench_after 2>&1 | tee after.log ``` 10. You should look at `init_ms`: ```sh cd ~ && paste -d' ' <(grep -E '^[0-9]+,' before.log | cut -d, -f1,2) <(grep -E '^[0-9]+,' after.log | cut -d, -f2) ``` **AI Assistance Disclosure** debugged, designed and implemented with both claude and codex

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: serve finalized state by root from checkpoint cache (#10273)
body:
**Motivation**

checkpointz with only Lodestar upstreams fails on every finality update.
It fetches the finalized block, then `GET
/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/{block.state_root}`, and Lodestar returns
`500 REGEN_ERROR_NO_SEED_STATE`. The same state works by slot or as
`finalized`.

Repro on mainnet (v1.49.0):

```
GET /eth/v1/beacon/states/finalized/root  -> 0x45a0…aa44, finalized: true
GET /eth/v1/beacon/states/0x45a0…aa44/fork -> {"code":500,"message":"REGEN_ERROR_NO_SEED_STATE"}
```

**Description**

After pruning, the finalized block is the fork choice anchor and has no
ancestors. `regen.getState` only checks the checkpoint state cache for
ancestors, so once the block's post-state has been evicted from the
block state cache there is no seed state and it throws.

`getStateByStateRoot` now checks whether the requested root is the
finalized block's state root and, if so, serves the finalized checkpoint
state from memory if the finalized block is at the epoch start slot (the
checkpoint state is then the block post-state). With a skipped boundary
slot, the checkpoint state is the advanced state with a different root,
so it falls through to the existing path unchanged.

**Testing**

Local `dev` node (minimal preset, 8 interop validators,
`--chain.maxBlockStates 4` so the finalized block's post-state gets
evicted the way it does on mainnet), requesting the finalized block's
state root after each finality update:
- v1.49.0: `/eth/v1/beacon/states/{root}/fork` and
`/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/{root}` both return `500
REGEN_ERROR_NO_SEED_STATE`
- this branch: both return 200 with `finalized: true`, across 4
consecutive finality updates (finalized epochs 2, 3, 4, 6)

Follow-ups, not in this PR:
- genesis state by root still fails (`STATE_NOT_IN_FORKCHOICE`)
- `StateArchiveRepository` only writes the root index in `put`, but
archival and startup use `putBinary`, so archived states can't be looked
up by root

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Analysis and implementation by GPT-6.1 Sol, reviewed by me (lodekeeper,
an AI agent).

---------

Co-authored-by: lodekeeper <lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>

subject: fix: discount empty slot support by fork choice node (#10211)
body:
## Motivation


[consensus-specs#5672](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5672)
fixed `compute_empty_slot_support_discount` to discount the parent
*node* a block extends, not the parent root. Post-gloas a root has

`..._two_consecutive_slots_1` predates #5672 and asserts the pre-fix
root, so it is skipped for `gloas`/`heze` only until the spec-tests pin
bump.

passed, 10 skipped

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: prevent range sync stall when rate limit backoff expires (#10249)
body:
When a peer rate limits us, `SyncChain` arms a timer for the end of the
backoff. The timer callback triggered the batch downloader and then
rescheduled the timer, each reading the clock on its own. If the backoff
expires between the two reads, the downloader still skips the peer and
the reschedule then drops it as expired without arming a new timer.
Nothing triggers the downloader again, so with a single usable peer the
chain stalls until another peer or batch event comes in.

This is also why `Should retry a rate-limited peer after metadata
backoff expires` times out in CI from time to time.

- reschedule before triggering the downloader in the timer callback
- add a test where the backoff expires while the timer callback runs

---------

Co-authored-by: Nazar Hussain <nazarhussain@gmail.com>

author: Cayman
subject: feat: emit PTC quorum changes from fork choice (#10274)
body:
**Motivation**

Refresh of #9284. That PR was closed in favor of #9387, which landed the
blob data availability vote tracking and `shouldBuildOnFull()`. The part
that never landed is making the PTC outcome observable: knowing when the
committee reaches a majority that a payload was present or absent, or
that blob data was available or not.

**Description**

- `ProtoArray.getPtcQuorum(root)` derives the per-field majority
(`true`, `false`, or `null` while neither side has one) from the
existing vote bitarrays. It reads the raw tallies and does not gate on
the payload being locally available, unlike `isPayloadTimely()`, so it
reflects what the committee said rather than what this node holds.
- `ForkChoice.notifyPtcMessages()` compares the quorum state before and
after applying the votes. On a change it increments
`beacon_fork_choice_ptc_quorum_total{vote, result}`, logs at verbose,
and calls the new optional `IForkChoiceStore.notifyPtcQuorum()`.
- The beacon node wires that callback to a new
`ChainEvent.forkChoicePtcQuorum`, following the existing `onJustified` /
`onFinalized` / `onFastConfirmation` pattern.

**Design notes vs. #9284**

- One event instead of two (re @nflaig's question on the original). The
event carries the full `{payloadPresent, blobDataAvailable}` snapshot,
so a block-level PTC attestation that crosses both thresholds at once
yields a single notification, and a consumer interested in one field
just reads it.
- No yea/nay vocabulary (re @ensi321). Fields are named after
`PayloadAttestationData`.
- No cached quorum flag. Votes overwrite per spec, so a majority can be
lost when a member re-votes. A before/after comparison reports every
real transition and adds no per-block state to initialize or prune.
- The `shouldExtendPayload` fix and the `blobDataAvailable` threading
from the original are already on `unstable` via #9387 and #9416.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

> This PR was written primarily by Claude Code.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: retry rate-limited peers after a sync chain restart (#10252)
body:
`stopSyncing()` clears the rate limit backoff timer but `startSyncing()`
only triggers the batch downloader and never arms it again. If a chain
is stopped and restarted while a peer is still in backoff, the peer is
skipped on restart and nothing retries it once the backoff ends. If all
usable peers of the chain are in backoff at that point, the chain stays
idle until another peer or batch event comes in.

This re-arms the timer when the chain is started and adds a test for it.
Related to #10249 but independent of it.

author: Chen Kai
subject: fix: preserve shuffling input ownership (#753)
body:
**Motivation**

Shuffling initialization has inconsistent failure ownership:
[`computeEpochShufflingForFork`](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/blob/8b3dcc0abe7dea809af59469148fa56a43e534ef/src/state_transition/utils/epoch_shuffling.zig#L129-L148)
preserves `active_indices` on error, while `computeEpochShuffling` frees
it. `EpochCache.initEpochShufflingRc` also frees the input if shuffling
construction succeeds but the subsequent RC allocation fails. A caller
that retains cleanup responsibility can therefore free the input twice.

**Description**

Transfer `active_indices` ownership only after the entire shuffling RC
initialization succeeds.

- Split the constructor names into `RefCount.create(allocator,
instance)` for allocation and initialization, and `RefCount.init(self,
allocator, instance)` for infallible initialization of allocator-owned
storage. Update all state-transition, fork-choice, and NAPI callers.
- Allocate the RC wrapper before constructing the shuffling, and keep
failed-input cleanup in scoped caller `errdefer` blocks.
- Add regressions for input retention, `RefCount.create` OOM,
`createFromState` allocation failures, and `afterProcessEpoch` wrapper
OOM. The latter verifies copied-input cleanup and unchanged shuffling
references and decision roots.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

- [x] External Contributors: I have read the [contributor
guidelines](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-assistance-notice)
and disclosed my usage of AI below.

Implementation and regression tests were primarily AI-authored, with an
independent AI ownership review.

author: Chen Kai
subject: fix: prepare state before rewards (#755)
body:
**Motivation**

Attestation rewards use finality and inactivity scores before their
epoch updates, producing incorrect inactivity penalties and suppressing
rewards when finalization ends a leak. Addresses the [review comment on
#731](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/pull/731#discussion_r4184001628),
following [Lodestar
#10224](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10224).

**Description**

`computeAttestationsRewards` commits pending writes, clones the state,
and applies justification/finalization followed by inactivity updates
before computing rewards, preserving the caller's state values.

- Cover leak exit, updated penalties, unchanged input, and repeated
queries.
- Extend allocation-failure coverage for scratch-state and reward
cleanup through the supplied allocator.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation and tests were primarily AI-authored, with independent AI
review.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: report builder circuit breaker as block selection reason (#10254)
body:
While the builder circuit breaker is active, `produceBlockV4` neither
requests builder API bids nor reads the bid pool, but the local block
selection is logged and counted as `builder_no_bid` with the error `No
builder bid available`. If the execution engine also flags the builder
override, it is reported as suspected censorship even though no bid was
considered.

Selecting the local block because of the circuit breaker now has its own
reason `builder_circuit_breaker`, used in the log and in
`beacon_block_production_selection_results_total`.

Before

```
Selected local block: no builder bid block produced reason=builder_no_bid, slot=368273, ..., circuitBreakerActive=true, ..., error=No builder bid available
```

After

```
Selected local block: builder circuit breaker is active reason=builder_circuit_breaker, slot=368273, ..., circuitBreakerActive=true, ...
```

author: Nico Flaig
subject: feat: add endpoint to get proposer preferences (#10255)
body:
Proposer preferences are broadcast once per epoch and the beacon node
keeps the ones it has seen to validate bids, but there is no way to read
them. A builder that subscribes to the `proposer_preferences` event
after they were broadcast, for example after a restart, can't bid for
the affected slots until the next broadcast, which can take up to two
epochs.

This adds `GET /eth/v1/beacon/proposer_preferences` which returns the
signed proposer preferences known by the node, optionally filtered by
`slot`. It lives next to the other endpoints for off-chain Gloas
messages (`execution_payload_bids`, `execution_payload_envelopes`) and
not under `/pool`, which holds operations that are included in blocks.

The endpoint is specified in ethereum/beacon-APIs#659, it is ignored in
the spec conformance test until the pinned spec version includes it.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: serve archived genesis state by root (#10277)
body:
**Motivation**

checkpointz v0.32.0 fetches every state by state root, including genesis
(its genesis loop retries `GET
/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/{genesis_state_root}` every 15s). Lodestar
returns `500 REGEN_ERROR_STATE_NOT_IN_FORKCHOICE` for it, while the same
state by `genesis` / slot 0 works. See ethpandaops/checkpointz#266.

**Description**

Genesis is pruned from fork choice, so regen can't find it, and the
state archive can't look it up by root because archived states are
written without the root index. Nodes initialized from genesis still
have it in the state archive at slot 0.

`getStateByStateRoot` now looks up the genesis block's state root once
(block archive slot 0, cached) and, if the requested root matches,
serves the archived slot 0 state directly. It's a plain DB read, so it
doesn't need `--serveHistoricalState`. Otherwise it falls through
unchanged. Checkpoint-synced nodes don't have the genesis state, so
nothing changes for them.

**Testing**

Local `dev` node (minimal preset, initialized from genesis), after the
first finalizations:
- unstable: `/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/{genesis_state_root}` and
`/eth/v1/beacon/states/{genesis_state_root}/fork` return `500
REGEN_ERROR_STATE_NOT_IN_FORKCHOICE`
- this branch: both return 200, and the SSZ bytes are identical to
`/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/genesis`

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Analysis and first implementation by GPT-6.1 Sol, simplified and
reviewed by me (lodekeeper, an AI agent).

Co-authored-by: lodekeeper <lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Kris O'Shea
subject: test: follow current head slot in sync waits (#10237)
body:
## Motivation

The multifork simulation can time out while waiting for a syncing node
even though that node has moved past the requested slot. `waitForHead`
captures the first head event's slot and keeps checking it on every
later event. If that first event is too early and the requested root was
already imported, neither success condition can fire.

This showed up in #9979's [failed
simulation](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/35157369708/job/109995673162).
The node emitted later heads but the wait kept comparing slot 17 against
slot 23.

## Changes

Check the current event's slot instead. Keep the existing exact-root
success path and listener cleanup. No production code or timeout values
change.

## Testing

- Five local regression probes passed, covering later slots, the
exact-root path, node isolation and listener cleanup. The probes are
kept outside the PR, following the repository's guidance for simulation
utilities.
- Full local Docker multifork simulation rerun on 3 October passed using
the repository's pinned Geth v1.16.7 and Lighthouse unstable-d235f2c
images.
- Ordinary CLI type-check, changed-file Biome and diff checks passed.

This fix is separate from #9979, whose updated branch passed the
simulation without it and has now merged. The earlier failed run
motivated the investigation, but this PR is not needed to unblock bid
publication.

Local simulation success is not a claim that hosted CI or the complete
Gloas Builder lifecycle has passed.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with investigating the failure, implementation, tests and
this description.

author: Chen Kai
subject: test: verify allocation failure coverage with standard checks (#611)
body:
## Motivation

Fixed allocation indexes can silently move away from the intended
cleanup boundary when allocation order changes. Replace suitable tests
with allocation sweeps while retaining their original error-path checks.

## Description

Use `std.testing.checkAllAllocationFailures` for 23 scenarios across
SSZ, fork types, state transition, clock, and BlockStateCache. Retain
explicit target-operation OOM, ownership, rollback, pool-slot,
double-free, and forced resize/remap-failure checks where applicable.

Each replacement was checked against the original test using targeted
negative modifications: 25 comparisons fail under both versions, and the
replacement passes once the normal implementation is restored. The two
EpochShuffling failure stages and both bulk-read cleanup stages were
checked separately.

author: b0a7
subject: fix: honor group validator statuses when filtering by ids (#10261)
body:
## Motivation
`POST/GET /eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/validators` accepts Beacon
API group statuses (`active`, `pending`, `exited`, `withdrawal`) in
addition to fine-grained statuses. When both `ids` and `statuses` were
provided, Lodestar compared against fine-grained status strings only, so
`statuses: ["active"]` never matched `active_ongoing` / `active_exiting`
/ `active_slashed`.
That returns HTTP 200 with an empty `data` array for validators that
exist and are active. Nimbus VC `v26.10.0` looks up indices with
`statuses: ["active"]`, so against Lodestar it never resolves indices /
duties and silently misses attestations.
## Description
- Add `statusMatches()` that treats group statuses as matching their
fine-grained members (via existing `mapToGeneralStatus`)
- Use it on the `ids` + `statuses` path in `getStateValidators` (covers
GET and POST)
- Widen request types with `ValidatorStatusFilter = ValidatorStatus |
GeneralValidatorStatus`
- Add unit tests for group and fine-grained filters with `ids`
The statuses-only path was already correct via `getValidatorsByStatus`.
Builder status filtering is unchanged (builder statuses are already
group-level only).

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: inherit gloas block execution status from the parent variant it builds on (#10268)
body:
Gloas blocks inherited the execution status of the parent's default
(PENDING) variant instead of the variant their bid builds on. If the EL
answered SYNCING/ACCEPTED for the parent payload, the child was still
imported as VALID and `onBlock` propagated VALID to the parent's FULL
variant, without the EL ever validating that payload. This also bypasses
the optimistic head check in block production.

- inherit from the parent variant matching the bid's `parentBlockHash`
(`getBlockHexAndBlockHash`), same lookup already used further down in
`importBlock`
- once a payload turns VALID, validate all PENDING/EMPTY variants
building on it (same `executionPayloadBlockHash`), not only the chain
the validation walked up, so siblings and blocks on a sibling's EMPTY
variant don't stay optimistic
- add `importBlock` and protoArray unit tests


Behavior change: a gloas block whose bid builds on a payload the EL
answered SYNCING or ACCEPTED for is now imported as SYNCING instead of
VALID. Such blocks are reported as execution optimistic, block
production refuses to build on them (same as pre-gloas), and the parent
payload is no longer marked VALID until the EL validates it or a
descendant payload. In the other direction, once a payload turns VALID
every block building on it is validated, not only the chain the
validation walked up.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: prevent unknown block sync stall when rate limit backoff expires (#10250)
body:
Same kind of lost wakeup as #10249, this time in `BlockInputSync`. A
by-root download whose eligible peers are all in rate limit backoff is
deferred and relies on the backoff timer to retry it. Expired backoffs
are dropped whenever they are read, and peer selection, the rate limit
check and the rescheduling each read the clock on their own. If the
backoff expires between two of those reads, either peer selection skips
the peer while the rate limit check already sees no backoff, so the
download fails as no peer available, or the download is deferred while
rescheduling finds nothing left to wait for and arms no timer, or only
one for a later backoff of another peer. The block or payload then stays
pending until some other event or that later timer triggers the search.

- use the same time for peer selection and the rate limit check
- if the backoff a deferred download was waiting for has expired,
trigger the search right away instead of dropping or delaying the retry,
for both block and payload downloads
- add tests that move the backoff expiry across every clock read around
the retry timer

subject: test: forward progressive list limits in spec type replacement (#10081)

The progressive branches predate the ssz `limit` option, so the limits

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: reject range sync envelopes whose block hash does not match the bid (#10251)
body:
Range sync caches an envelope served by a peer as soon as its
`beacon_block_root` matches the block at that slot, nothing else is
checked before `addPayloadEnvelope`. The envelope is only verified when
the payload is imported, and #10246 evicts it from the seen cache if
that fails. But `assertLinearChainSegment` runs first and tracks the
execution chain by the envelope's `payload.block_hash`. An envelope with
a wrong hash makes the next block look like it builds on an unknown
payload, the segment fails with `NON_LINEAR_PAYLOAD_ROOTS` before the
import is reached, and the cached envelope is never evicted. Every retry
of the batch reuses it and fails the same way, so one peer serving a
single bad envelope stalls range sync until the cache entry is evicted
by the size cap or finalization, same as #9660. No builder signature is
needed for this.

This rejects the envelope while validating the response if
`payload.block_hash` does not match the block's bid, so it never reaches
the cache, and the peer is reported like for a wrong
`beacon_block_root`. The same check applies to the dangling parent
envelope. There a wrong hash does not break linearity, it fails at
import, but the eviction then removes the parent's cache entry which
range sync cannot recreate, and every retry fails on the missing entry.
Gossip and by-root sync already check the block hash before caching.

- add `INVALID_ENVELOPE_BLOCK_HASH` to
`validateEnvelopesByRangeResponse`, checked against the bid of the
downloaded or cached block
- carry the parent bid's `block_hash` in `ParentPayloadCommitments` for
the dangling parent envelope
