author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: recreate the dangling parent payload entry in range sync (#10311)
body:
The first batch of a sync chain downloads the payload of the block
before the batch by root if its first block builds on that block's FULL
variant, that is the head when the chain was created, in practice the
checkpoint anchor when the epoch-start slot was skipped. The envelope is
attached to the parent's existing `PayloadEnvelopeInput`. If it is
invalid in a way only the import catches (bad signature, wrong
`prev_randao`, ...), #10246 evicts that entry and nothing recreates it:
the anchor entry is seeded once from the anchor state, its block body is
not in the db, and `cacheByRangeResponses` only creates entries for
blocks of the batch. Every retry then fails with a generic `Missing
PayloadEnvelopeInput` error, which is not attributed to the peer, until
`MAX_DOWNLOAD_ATTEMPTS` tears the sync chain down, and the next chain
starts with the same first batch. The node stays stuck until a restart.
The cache cap evicts the same entry without any invalid envelope once
the look-ahead batches fill it up.

The sync chain now captures the head block (root, slot, proposer and
bid) instead of only its bid, which is enough to recreate the entry via
`addFromBid` when it is missing. Carrying the head root also lets
`shouldDownloadParentEnvelope` require the first block's `parent_root`
to match it, so the parent payload is only ever validated against the
bid of the block it belongs to.

- recreate the dangling parent `PayloadEnvelopeInput` from the head's
bid if it is missing from the seen cache
- only download the parent payload if the first block's `parent_root` is
the head block
- reject a parent envelope whose `payload.slot_number` does not match
the parent's slot, it was keyed under the wrong slot and failed the
batch with `PARENT_PAYLOAD_UNKNOWN` instead
- validate the parent's columns against the parent's slot instead of the
slot claimed by the first column

Follow-up to #10251.

author: NC
subject: chore: update consensus specs to v1.7.0-beta.4 (#10314)
body:
**Blocked by #10312 (FOCIL).** This bump skips every Heze spec test, and
#10312 un-skips the Heze `on_inclusion_list` and `gossip_inclusion_list`
suites, which pass at beta.3 but need the new Heze SSZ shapes at beta.4.
Merge FOCIL first, then this PR is rebased and its specrefs regenerated
on top.

Update spec tests and specrefs to
[v1.7.0-beta.4](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/releases/tag/v1.7.0-beta.4),
following the beta.3 bump in #10280.

### Consensus change

ethereum/consensus-specs#5719 moves the Gloas builder pending payment
clearing from `process_proposer_slashing` into `slash_validator`. A
proposer could previously get itself slashed through an attester
slashing first, which made the later proposer slashing invalid and left
the builder paying for the equivocated block. Now every slashing of a
proposer clears all of its `builder_pending_payments` entries, and the
Gloas `process_proposer_slashing` override is gone. This changes Gloas
state roots whenever a slashed proposer has a pending payment, so it
should ship in a coordinated release with the other clients.

### Heze tests skipped (temporary)

v1.7.0-beta.4 adds EIP-8015 (ethereum/consensus-specs#5655), which
removes `eth1_data`, `eth1_data_votes`, `eth1_deposit_index` and
`deposit_requests_start_index` from the Heze `BeaconState` and
`eth1_data` and `deposits` from the Heze `BeaconBlockBody`, and EIP-8365
(ethereum/consensus-specs#5713). Lodestar does not implement either yet,
so no Heze vector carrying a state or a block deserializes. All Heze
suites are skipped in `specTestIterator.ts` except `ssz_static` for
containers EIP-8015 does not touch. The skip carries a TODO and will be
lifted in the EIP-8015 and EIP-8365 PRs. The matching specrefs entries
are recorded as exceptions.

### Other changes

- ethereum/consensus-specs#5679 (slashed validators excluded from
`calculate_committee_fraction` and `compute_proposer_score`) needs no
code: fork choice justified balances and the fast confirmation total
active balance already zero slashed validators.
- ethereum/consensus-specs#5710 replaces `SLOT_DURATION_SCHEDULE` with
`SLOT_DURATION_MS_EIP8198`; EIP-8198 is not implemented, so the new key
joins `MIN_BLOB_DATA_RETENTION_MS` in the config sync ignore list.
- ethereum/consensus-specs#5721 (inclusion list domain from the list's
own slot) is already handled in #10312.
- Removed the stale `process_proposer_slashing#gloas` specref, refreshed
the builder README badge.

### Validation

- Gloas `operations/proposer_slashing` and `attester_slashing`, and the
new `sanity/blocks` slashing cases
(`builder_payment_removed_when_proposer_slashes_itself`,
`invalid_proposer_and_attester_slashings_same_validator`,
`proposer_and_attester_slashings_partial_overlap`) on both presets.
- Full `sanity`, `fast_confirmation`, `fork_choice` (includes the new
`get_head` cases) on minimal: 2,483 passed.
- Heze `ssz_static`: 8,840 passed, state and block containers skipped as
intended.
- Config sync e2e test, `check-types` for state-transition, beacon-node
and config, biome, prettier, and `ethspecify check` (1,231 refs valid).
- Full fork choice compliance run against the beta.4 comptest vectors:
10,304 passed, 0 failed (about 1h45m locally).

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: resubmit proposal preferences after the beacon node resynced (#10326)
body:
Proposer and builder preferences are submitted once per proposal and
tracked per dependent root on the validator client, while the beacon
node keeps them in memory only. A beacon node restart between the
submission and the proposal loses them and peers do not re-gossip
preferences they already know, so bids for the proposal are ignored and
the proposer falls back to a local payload.

The syncing status tracker already detects this case, a restarted beacon
node fails the status poll or reports syncing until it is back at head.
The preferences service now resets its submission tracking when the
tracker reports the node as resynced and submits everything within the
window again. The beacon node ignores preferences it still has.

Addresses the beacon node restart part of #9920. Failover to a second
beacon node that never received the preferences is not covered, the
status poll goes through the same fallback client.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: cancel req/resp bridge iterators when the consumer returns early (#10304)
body:
With the network worker (default), req/resp iterators are bridged
between threads as events. If the consumer stops early (`break`,
`return()`), only its local pending entry is dropped. The other thread
is never told and keeps iterating its source to the end, posting every
item across the thread boundary just to be dropped on arrival.

For outgoing requests the main thread stops after `maxResponses` chunks
or on the first invalid chunk, but the worker keeps decompressing and
copying whatever the peer sends until the stream is closed or
`RESP_TIMEOUT` (10s) fires. The early exit path in `sendRequest` (close,
`closeRead`, scheduled abort) only runs without the worker. For incoming
requests the main thread handler keeps reading from the db after the
remote reset the stream.

- the caller's `return()` emits a cancel event for the request id
- the handler keeps the iterator per request id and calls `return()` on
it, this runs the source's `finally` and for outgoing requests the
graceful close in `sendRequest`
- at most one more item is produced after the cancel since `return()`
queues behind the in-flight `next()`

This also releases the self rate limiter slot and roundtrip timer of an
outgoing request once the consumer is done instead of when the stream
ends.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: feat: honor executiononly builder selection post-gloas (#10309)
body:
**Motivation**

There is no way to opt out of p2p bids post-Gloas. `--builder.selection
executiononly` is currently normalized to `executionalways` (boost
factor 0), which prefers the local payload but still falls back to a p2p
or builder API bid if local production fails or is delayed.

**Description**

Revive `executiononly` post-Gloas as strictly local-only, matching its
pre-Gloas semantics:

- The validator client no longer maps `executiononly` to
`executionalways` post-Gloas.
- When producing a Gloas block with `executiononly`, the validator
client sends no builder entries and sets the top-level `minBid` (which
only applies to p2p bids) to `2**64 - 1`. The beacon node therefore
never selects a bid. If the local payload fails or is not produced in
time, the block is proposed without an execution payload instead of
using a bid (requires the dummy bid fallback that is implemented
separately, without it the proposal is missed).
- As a safety net, the validator client refuses to sign a block that
commits to a non-self-build bid when `executiononly` is configured, same
as the pre-Gloas check on `executionPayloadSource`.
- The validator client refuses to start if `executiononly` is configured
together with `builders` in the same config (CLI args / default config
or a per-key config).
- `executiononly` validators also skip builder preferences submission
(existing check that was previously unreachable post-Gloas).

A per-key builder boost factor set through the standard builder config
(keymanager API / proposer settings) still takes precedence over the
selection alias, as before.

Operators who want to keep builder API bids but drop p2p bids can still
do that with a high global `minBid` and per-builder `min_bid` overrides.

---------

Co-authored-by: lodekeeper <lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Nico Flaig <nflaig@protonmail.com>

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: retry proposer preferences submission on error response (#10317)
body:
The response of `submitProposerPreferences` is not asserted, so an error
response is treated as a successful submission and the slots are marked
as submitted. A beacon node that rejects the preferences, e.g. because
it has not seen the dependent root of the duties yet, leaves the
proposal without preferences until the proposer shuffling dependent root
shifts. The api client only throws on network errors, the submission is
now retried on the next slot for error responses as well, same as for
builder preferences.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: refactor: combine proposer and builder preferences services (#10319)
body:
`ProposerPreferencesService` and `BuilderPreferencesService` share the
same structure, both submit ahead of upcoming proposals using the same
submission window, track submissions per epoch keyed by the proposer
shuffling dependent root and resubmit when it shifts. They only differ
in what they sign and where they submit.

Combine them into `ProposalPreferencesService` with one duty window and
dependent root tracking. The proposer and builder submissions are still
tracked separately since they succeed or fail independently, a failed
submission of one is retried on the next slot without resubmitting the
other. No behavioral change otherwise.

Closes #9919

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: send a zero commit in engine_getClientVersionV1 when git data is missing (#10324)
body:
`getLodestarClientVersion` falls back to an empty commit when the build
has no git data (`.git-data.json` with `"commit": ""`, which a Docker
build from a worktree or an install without a `.git` directory
produces). The engine client then sends `commit: "0x"` in
`engine_getClientVersionV1`, which is not a valid value: the
[spec](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/identification.md#clientversionv1)
defines `commit` as `DATA, 4 bytes`. Nimbus-eth1 rejects it with `-32602
Parameter [version] of type 'ClientVersionV1' could not be decoded`, the
other ELs happen to accept it.

- fall back to `00000000` when the commit is missing, so every consumer
gets 8 hex characters
- the default graffiti becomes `LS0000` instead of a bare `LS` for such
builds, and `/eth/v2/node/version` reports `0x00000000` instead of `0x`
- release images carry git data and are not affected

Found while testing #10204 against Nimbus-eth1, see #10322 for the state
flap the rejected call causes, which is a separate change.

subject: fix: align beacon api with v5.0.0-beta.0 (#10302)
body:
Update the spec tests to [Beacon APIs
v5.0.0-beta.0](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/releases/tag/v5.0.0-beta.0).

- Enable previously skipped operations and events, and update existing

- Select pending deposit, partial withdrawal and consolidation types by

author: Nazar Hussain
subject: test: upgrade geth and nethermind in sim tests (#10308)
body:
**Motivation**

Sim tests were pinned to Nethermind 1.18.2 because of a genesis hash
mismatch with Geth (NethermindEth/nethermind#6683). That issue was
closed as stale, not fixed, so I retested.

The mismatch was on our side: our Nethermind chainspec only enabled
Shanghai while the Geth genesis has Cancun and Prague at genesis.
Nethermind 1.18.2 and 2.1.0 now produce the same hash for the same
chainspec.

**Description**

- Bump `GETH_DOCKER_IMAGE` to `v1.17.7` and `NETHERMIND_DOCKER_IMAGE` to
`2.1.0`
- Run Nethermind again on multifork nodes 2-4 (as before #6540)
- Nethermind chainspec: add Cancun/Prague transitions, blob schedule and
`depositContractAddress` (required by Nethermind 2.x when EIP-6110 is
on)
- Add Prague system contracts (EIP-4788, 2935, 7002, 7251) to genesis
alloc. Geth 1.17 rejects `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3` with `empty system
contract: no code at 0x...7002` without them, Nethermind 2.1.0 throws a
NullReferenceException. Bytecode taken from geth
`params/protocol_params.go`
- Drop the Geth `--mine` flag, removed in Geth 1.17 (no-op post-merge)

**Testing**

- Genesis hash matches across Geth 1.16.7, Geth 1.17.7 and Nethermind
2.1.0 (`0xa5c701...36f2`)
- All 4 sim tests pass locally (macOS arm64): multifork, endpoints,
backup eth provider, mixed clients
- Multifork: finalized with 0 assertion errors, Nethermind-backed nodes
proposed blocks with no RPC errors, range/checkpoint/unknown-block sync
passed

**Notes**

- EL genesis has no `osakaTime`, so the EL stays on Prague after Fulu in
the endpoints sim. Pre-existing, left for a follow-up
- The `admin_addPeer` skip for Nethermind in `network.ts`
(NethermindEth/nethermind#4876) is likely no longer needed, left
untouched

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: handle partial failures when submitting proposal preferences (#10325)
body:
When some of the submitted proposer or builder preferences are rejected,
the beacon node responds with an `IndexedErrorMessage` listing the
failed entries by index. The validator client treated this as a failure
of the whole batch, nothing was marked as submitted and all entries were
sent again on the next slot, including the ones the beacon node had
accepted.

- expose the per-index `failures` of an error response on the client
`ApiError`
- mark the accepted proposer and builder preferences as submitted and
only retry the rejected ones, a proposal is retried with all its
builders if one of them rejected the entry
- log each rejected entry with its slot instead of the joined failure
messages
- fix `mockApiErrorResponse` which never set the response body

Follow-up to #10319, addresses the partial failure handling mentioned in
#9920.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: feat: stop calling `prepareBeaconProposer` from gloas (#10337)
body:
From Gloas the beacon node takes the proposer's fee recipient from the
signed proposer preferences and derives the validators using it from the
committee subscriptions, see #10336. `prepare_beacon_proposer` is
deprecated from Gloas in beacon APIs
[#608](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/608) and beacon
nodes may remove it, so the validator client stops calling it once the
epoch is in Gloas, same as `register_validator`. The last pre-Gloas
submission keeps the proposer cache warm through the fork.

Requires a beacon node with #10336, without it an older beacon node
loses custody derivation and local proposer detection for the validators
of this client.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: feat: stop depending on prepare_beacon_proposer for custody and gloas payloads (#10336)
body:
Beacon APIs [#608](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/608)
asks beacon nodes to derive the set of validators using the node from
`beacon_committee_subscriptions`, to size the custody group count, and
makes signed proposer preferences the source of the proposer's fee
recipient and gas limit from Gloas on. Lodestar derived both from
`prepare_beacon_proposer`, which is deprecated from Gloas and may be
dropped by validator clients, only the gas limit already came from the
pool.

- track the validators of `beacon_committee_subscriptions` in the
proposer cache without fee recipient, the union of both sources feeds
the custody group count and the local proposer detection in
`prepareNextSlot`
- resolve the fee recipient of a local Gloas payload from the requested
one, then the pooled proposer preferences, then the proposer cache, for
block production and for the payload attributes prepared a slot ahead
- share the pooled preferences lookup between the fee recipient and the
target gas limit
- use the attached validator set for the two other local proposer checks
as well, pooling gossip payload attestations for the next proposal and
the proposer boost fcU override, both looked for a registered fee
recipient
- track the subscribing validators regardless of the sync state, the
subscription itself does not fail if the tracking does

`prepare_beacon_proposer` stays supported, it remains the per-validator
fee recipient source pre-Gloas and the fallback after. The validator
client keeps calling it for now, dropping the call post-Gloas is a
follow-up once beacon nodes with this change are released.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: feat: persist proposer preferences across beacon node restarts (#10327)
body:
The beacon node keeps the proposer preferences it validated in memory
only. After a restart the pool is empty and peers do not re-gossip
preferences they already know, so bids for the affected slots are
ignored at gossip validation, for the local proposer and for every other
proposer, until the next epoch's preferences arrive.

Persist the pool the same way as the op pool, written on shutdown and
restored on startup, dropping entries whose proposal slot has passed.
Entries were validated before they were persisted and lookups are keyed
by the dependent root of their branch, so nothing needs to be
re-validated on load.

- add a `ProposerPreferencesRepository` keyed by proposal slot and
dependent root
- persist the pool in `persistToDisk` and restore it in `loadFromDisk`
- move `persistDiff` to the op pool utils to share it

A resubmission after a restart now hits the already-known check, the
restored entry is neither republished on gossip nor emitted as
`proposer_preferences` event. Peers already have the message and ignore
duplicates, and the event is defined as received and validated, which a
restored entry was not. A builder whose event stream dropped with the
restart resyncs via `GET /eth/v1/beacon/proposer_preferences`, which the
restored pool now serves for all proposers instead of only the node's
own validators.

Addresses the beacon node side of #9920, the validator client side is
#10326. A crash skips `persistToDisk`, same as for the op pool.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: feat: support engine api over REST with SSZ encoding (#10204)
body:
Implements the REST engine API with SSZ encoded bodies from
[execution-apis#793](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/refactor.md)
next to the existing JSON-RPC transport. The transport is picked per
execution client connection from `GET /engine/v1/capabilities`, so nodes
on an execution client without the REST API keep working unchanged, and
the REST API is used by default where it is advertised.

- add the engine API wire containers, composed from the consensus
payload types with `Optional[T]` encoded as `List[T, 1]`
- split `ExecutionEngineHttp` into a JSON-RPC and a REST transport
behind `IEngineTransport`, the engine keeps the request queue, engine
state, payload id cache and result handling
- probe the capabilities once per connection and again after a
disconnect. In `auto` mode an execution client without the REST API (a
4xx other than 401, 403, 408 or 429) or with a capabilities document
that cannot be parsed selects JSON-RPC until it reconnects, the latter
with a warning. Timeouts, 408, 429 and 5xx use JSON-RPC and probe again
after 12 seconds, 401 and 403 stay errors. Forks and `/blobs/vN`
revisions that are not advertised stay on JSON-RPC, and a fork rejected
with `unsupported-fork` despite being advertised falls back to JSON-RPC
until reconnect
- REST is only negotiated with a single execution URL, multiple URLs
keep JSON-RPC and its fallback across URLs. `ssz` requires a single URL
and never falls back, `json-rpc` never probes
- validate the blob versioned hashes of the payload's type-3
transactions against the beacon commitments before submitting over REST,
since the envelope has no `expected_blob_versioned_hashes` and the EL
can no longer run that check. JSON-RPC keeps delegating it to the EL
- honor the advertised request limits, oversized requests fail locally
and are not split
- add `--execution.engineApi auto|ssz|json-rpc` (default `auto`) and the
`lodestar_execution_engine_api_requests_total{transport}` counter, the
REST client reports the same per-route client metrics including the
request and response bytes from #10195. Transport selection and
fallbacks are logged at debug level
- decode `/blobs/v2` responses as views into the response body instead
of copying, the response is all-or-nothing so every byte is needed,
`/blobs/v1` keeps copies since partial responses carry zero-filled
entries
- send `X-Engine-Client-Version` as the JSON `ClientVersionV1` object
since the spec does not pin a format and that is what Nethermind parses
- malformed SSZ or JSON on a 2xx response and HTTP errors are classified
as engine errors, only transport failures mark the execution client
offline

The client speaks HTTP/1.1 only, neither reth nor Nethermind negotiates
h2c on the cleartext engine port today. Left for follow-ups: HTTP/2,
`/blobs/v3` and `/blobs/v4`, `custody_columns` on forkchoice updates,
and the `bogota` header value once
[execution-apis#920](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/920)
lands. Heze stays on JSON-RPC in `auto` mode until then.

Verified on kurtosis devnets (minimal preset, blob spam), see the
interop reports in the comments for the per-route numbers:

- reth `v2.7.0` and `main`: everything over REST including `/blobs/v2`,
blobs resolved into data columns on a non-supernode, fulu at genesis and
an electra to fulu transition with the blob revision switching at the
fork boundary
- Nethermind `master` after
[NethermindEth/nethermind#14302](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/14302):
same two scenarios, everything over REST. Before the fix every
forkchoice update with payload attributes was rejected with
`unsupported-fork` on chainspec networks
([NethermindEth/nethermind#14006](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/issues/14006))
and the per-fork fallback kept the node proposing over JSON-RPC
- geth and Nethermind 1.38.0: `404` on capabilities, JSON-RPC for the
whole run

Supersedes #10155.

---------

Co-authored-by: Cayman <caymannava@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Nazar Hussain <nazarhussain@gmail.com>

author: Nico Flaig
subject: ci: add nightly engine API interop run against latest execution client images (#10333)
body:
Turns the engine API interop matrix from #10323 into a nightly workflow
so interop problems with execution clients show up the day they land,
instead of when someone runs a devnet by hand. Every execution client
runs against the published `chainsafe/lodestar:next` image on its own
two-node kurtosis devnet (minimal preset, blob spam, one non-supernode
that has to fetch blobs from its EL, one supernode), and a job fails on
anything that looks like an engine API problem, with the logs attached
for whoever digs in.

- one job per client, geth, Nethermind, reth, Besu, Erigon, ethrex and
Nimbus-eth1, on their default-branch images rebuilt nightly by
ethpandaops. Tags float on purpose and are resolved to their digest at
the registry before every run, since the runners pull through registry
mirrors that kept serving an older manifest for `next`; the summary row
records the digest and Lodestar version that were judged. The Lodestar
image can be overridden through `workflow_dispatch`
- two scenarios per job: fulu at genesis with the second EL restarted
once finality is reached (finality has to advance again and the
transport has to be rediscovered, judged from the moment node 2 reports
its EL back in sync), and fulu at genesis with gloas at epoch 2 (fork
switch, amsterdam payloads and attributes, archived envelopes rebuilt
from EL bodies)
- the verdict is computed from Lodestar's own metrics and logs after the
first finalized epoch, so startup noise is ignored: no engine request
errors (the capabilities probe aside), only `VALID` payload and
forkchoice results, no warnings or errors from the execution module, no
REST to JSON-RPC fallback once REST was negotiated, a build with the
REST transport must use it when the EL advertises it, no missed slots,
blobs included and `getBlobs` exercised, and in gloas the head on the
gloas fork with envelopes rebuilt through the EL
- every run uploads the kurtosis args, both CL and EL logs, the metrics
snapshots, the capabilities document and a `result.json` plus a summary
table row in the job summary
- runs nightly at 04:00 UTC and on dispatch only

Verified in CI while the PR carried a temporary `pull_request` trigger:
run
[37949390461](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/37949390461)
on the merged #10204 code passes all seven clients in both scenarios,
reth and Nethermind over SSZ for every request. Locally also checked the
fail path with a warning and a fallback line injected after the judged
window, which fails and names both lines.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: refactor: clean up attached validators tracking (#10338)
body:
Follow-up to #10336 for the review comments after the merge.

- resolve the fee recipient of a local payload and its source in one
function instead of nested ternaries, shared by the pre- and post-gloas
paths
- rename `touch` to `track`, it returns whether the validator is new so
the custody update no longer compares the index count before and after,
and it refreshes the existing entry instead of replacing it
- log a failed tracking of attached validators at warn

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: keep proposer boost root for the payload tiebreak when boost is withheld (#10339)
body:
In gloas, `should_extend_payload` reads `store.proposer_boost_root`
whether or not `should_apply_proposer_boost` applies the boost weight.
When the boost is withheld, `updateHead()` only runs the
`applyScoreChanges()` pass with `proposerBoost: null` and the payload
tiebreak derived its root from that argument. For a previous slot block
with a known but not timely payload this prefers the FULL variant over
the EMPTY variant the boosted block extends, so the head stops at the
parent's FULL variant instead of following the boosted block. The
re-application in `validateLatestHash()` replays the previously applied
boost and has the same gap.

The tiebreak root is now tracked in `ProtoArray` apart from the applied
boost and passed explicitly from the withheld pass. The
`should_apply_proposer_boost_withheld` spec vector never imports a
payload for the parent so it does not reach the tiebreak, hence the unit
test.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: feat: track validators that submit proposer preferences as attached (#10340)
body:
Since #10336 the validators using a beacon node are known from their
committee subscriptions. Signed proposer preferences submitted through
`POST /eth/v1/validator/proposer_preferences` are a second, more
targeted signal: the message is signed by the validator, validated
against the proposer lookahead and arrives ahead of the exact slot
`prepareNextSlot` prepares for. The validator client also resubmits them
once the beacon node is back after a restart (#10326), which tracks the
upcoming proposer again at the same time.

Track the validators of preferences that pass validation or are already
known, the latter because a pool restored on startup (#10327) makes a
resubmission known. Rejected messages and preferences received over
gossip are not tracked, they say nothing about which node a validator
uses.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: feat: reject proposer data and validator registrations from gloas (#10341)
body:
`prepare_beacon_proposer` and `register_validator` are deprecated from
Gloas in beacon APIs
[#608](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/608), signed
proposer preferences and builder preferences replace them and beacon
nodes may remove the endpoints. Beacon APIs
[#435](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/issues/435) is the reason
to actually do that: proposer data is unsigned, so anyone who can reach
the beacon node api can set the fee recipient of any validator, while a
signed preference can only come from the validator itself.

Both endpoints respond with 410 once the clock is in Gloas, with a
message naming the replacement endpoint, so validator clients that still
call them notice. Pre-Gloas is unchanged.

Follow-up to #10336 and #10337.

author: bing
subject: fix: reset pendingDeposits with the fork's list type at genesis (#10353)
body:
**Motivation**

From gloas pendingDeposits is a progressive list, so resetting it with
the electra list type at genesis leaves a subtree whose root disagrees
with the serialized state.

**Description**

Reset it with the fork's own type and assert that genesis roots survive
a serialize/deserialize round trip from electra onwards.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Fable found this while implementing eip-8015

author: b0a7
subject: fix: do not treat hex block ids as slots in getBlockRoot fast path (#10352)
body:
**Motivation**

The Beacon API block_id for getBlockRoot is one of "head", "genesis",
"finalized", a decimal slot, or a hex-encoded block root with a 0x
prefix (beacon-APIs v5.0.0-beta.0). A 0x string is a block root, but
getBlockRoot parsed it as a slot number instead. When that number was a
recent slot, the handler returned the historical root for that slot and
never loaded the requested block.

**Description**

0x block ids now skip the slot shortcut and are loaded as roots. Decimal
slot strings, numeric slots, and 'head' still use the shortcut.

The new unit test requests a root of 0x followed by 31 zero bytes and 05
while the head is at slot 10. The old code treated that id as slot 5. It
now returns the root of the loaded block. The same file also covers
'head', a recent slot, a normal root, and a slot older than the
historical-root window.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: refactor: make slot timing fork-aware to prepare for slot duration changes (#10138)
body:
Prepares slot timing for EIP-8198 quick slots, extracted from #9933.
Slot durations and deadlines go through fork config, and clocks use
computed slot boundaries.

Timers use the fork of the slot they run in, including preparation,
proposer-duty lookahead, payload polling, reconstruction,
validator-monitor thresholds, and notifier logging. Regression tests
cover shorter and longer slot durations across fork boundaries.

All forks still return `SLOT_DURATION_MS`; actual duration changes
remain in #9933. On non-12-second networks, block-production timeouts
and cutoffs, the reprocessing guard, and light-client rate-limit windows
now scale with slot duration.

---------

Co-authored-by: Cayman <caymannava@gmail.com>

author: Nico Flaig
subject: perf: expose sync committee indices (#768)
body:
**Motivation**

Block import only needs the current sync-committee validator indices for
monitoring. The existing getter also converts the native committee map
into a JavaScript `Map` and position arrays.

**Description**

Expose `currentSyncCommitteeValidatorIndices` as an owned `Uint32Array`,
preserving committee order and duplicate positions. Keep the full getter
for callers that need the map. The returned array remains usable after
state release.

Lodestar caller: https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10350.

The included benchmark measures each uncached binding call for a
512-position committee:

| Unique validators | Full cache | Indices only |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | 63.8 µs | 2.3 µs |
| 512 | 168.3 µs | 1.7 µs |

Measured locally with Node 24.13.0, Zig 0.16.0 ReleaseSafe and an
i7-1360P. These are getter timings, not end-to-end block-import timings.

Validation: all 429 binding tests passed, including ordering, mutation
isolation, release and pre-Altair errors. ReleaseSafe mainnet build,
source formatting, tidy and lint passed.

author: bing
subject: fix(beacon-node): derive the sync aggregate size from the preset in serialized block offsets (#10334)
body:
**Motivation**

We were using hardcoded 160 instead of the `SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE` const
which is wrong in minimal preset.

**Description**

Use the const.

subject: chore: fix Builder API queries per slot panel (#10357)

subject: perf: allocate once when serializing execution requests (#10356)

**Motivation**

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: include commit in block timing (#767)
body:
**Motivation**

The native process-block histogram stops before commit, while the
TypeScript histogram includes it. This gives the timings different
scopes in the [devnet
profile](https://gist.github.com/nflaig/faa742d2f8107e885a698a6db9501a56).

**Description**

Include successful commit in the total block timer, retain the separate
commit timer, and record proposer reward metrics afterward. State-root
verification stays outside the block timer.

Validation: minimal state-transition suite and mainnet
state-transition/proposer-reward binding tests passed. Tidy, lint and
tracked-source formatting passed.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: perf: avoid importing sync committee maps (#10350)
body:
Block import only needs sync-committee validator indices for monitoring,
but the native state view currently also builds the full JavaScript
committee map.

Use a cached indices-only getter. TypeScript states reuse their epoch
cache; native states use the new addon getter when available and fall
back to the full cache with older addons. No dependency update is
required to merge this, but the faster path requires
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/pull/768.

Validation: 33 targeted state-view, block-import and validator-monitor
tests passed; full build, workspace type checks and lint passed. An
integration check also passed with the released 2.0.0 addon, the new
addon and the TypeScript state view.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: feat: implement quick slots EIP-8198 in heze (#10355)
body:
Implements EIP-8198 (quick slots) as part of Heze per
[consensus-specs#5718](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5718),
which folds the eip8198 feature into the fork and derives slot durations
from the fork schedule
([consensus-specs#5710](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5710)).
Builds on the fork-aware slot timing from #10138.

- `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE` (mainnet 10000, minimal 5000) and
`MIN_BLOB_DATA_RETENTION_MS` config values, `getSlotDurationMs(fork)`
returns the heze duration post-heze so all deadline and clock call sites
pick it up
- piecewise timeline helpers per spec (`getSlotDurations`,
`getSlotDurationMsAtEpoch`, `computeTimeAtSlotMs`/`computeTimeAtSlot`,
`computeSlotAtTimeMs`), execution payload timestamps follow it
- rewards priced per spec: base reward and sync participant reward scale
by `duration(epoch) / duration(GENESIS_EPOCH)`, flag deltas and
inactivity penalty priced at the previous epoch, attestation proposer
reward at the attestation's target epoch (new
`baseRewardPerIncrementPrevEpoch` on the epoch cache), inactivity
denominator scales by the squared ratio
- gloas churn limits scale by the duration ratio, bounds applied before
scaling and increment rounding once after
- data column retention preserved in wall-clock terms via
`getBlobDataRetentionStartEpoch` (ByRange/ByRoot validation, pruning,
`isDaOutOfRange`), gossip `seenTTL` uses the largest configured duration

Spec vectors generated from the spec PR head pass (10350/10399 minimal;
the 16 fork_choice failures are a pyspec harness artifact in the
generated vectors, raised on the spec PR, and the 7 random failures are
vectors predating consensus-specs#5719 on the spec PR's base, neither is
a Lodestar issue). Note the pyspec harness never activates the schedule
(`HEZE_FORK_EPOCH` stays `FAR_FUTURE` in config), so all vectors are
generated with the duration unchanged and test configs set
`SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE = SLOT_DURATION_MS` to match; the scaled path is
covered by unit tests and a kurtosis devnet run (gloas genesis, heze at
epoch 3, 6s -> 4s slots: clean fork, no missed blocks, full
participation, finality advancing).

author: bing
subject: feat: verify EIP-8025 execution proofs through ere's C verifier (#760)
body:
Implements https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5639

Add an `ere_verifier` module over ChainSafe/ere.zig, which wraps ere
v0.19.2's prebuilt `libere_verifier_c` (OpenVM, SP1, ZisK, LambdaVM),
and a `proofEngine` N-API namespace.

This standalone PR doesn't really make sense atm but we need to expose
these via napi bindings, after which we will have a `ProofEngine` on
upstream to consume this verifier by calling `verifyExecutionProof` (see
the
[spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/_features/eip8025/beacon-chain.md#execution-proof-verification)).
IIUC all zig needs to know is to verify (and it is the right layer to do
it anyway through FFI with the C library), the rest is handled upstream
for now since that's where gossip happens

author: Chen Kai
subject: perf: vectorize shuffle swap loop (#769)
body:
**Motivation**

`innerShuffleList` does about 45 million conditional swaps for the
mainnet active set (about 1M positions, 90 rounds), one pair at a time.
Each iteration re-checks the source hash window and the decision byte,
so the compiler does not vectorize the loop.

The shuffle is on the epoch critical path: `proposer_lookahead` waits
for the next shuffling, and that wait is the largest single segment of
`bench_process_epoch` on main.

One source byte holds the decisions for eight consecutive pairs, so
those eight swaps can be done as one vector select.

**Benchmark**

`bench_process_epoch` on Apple M5, ReleaseSafe/mainnet. The input is the
mainnet Fulu state at slot 13,336,576 with 2,178,249 validators. Each
run is 50 iterations; values are per-run means in milliseconds. Runs
alternate between the two binaries.

| Case | main, runs 1 / 2 / 3 | This PR, runs 1 / 2 / 3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `epoch_total` | 149.312 / 151.016 / 153.124 | 102.217 / 100.541 /
102.278 |
| `proposer_lookahead`, including async wait | 69.916 / 70.825 / 71.487
| 21.400 / 21.067 / 21.583 |
| Standalone synchronous `proposer_lookahead` | 93.536 / 94.191 / 93.896
| 44.944 / 44.417 / 44.517 |
| `state_root` (unaffected, as a control) | 32.472 / 32.672 / 33.156 |
32.994 / 32.696 / 33.105 |

The other segments are unchanged. `epoch_total` has the same scope as in
#734: it excludes `afterProcessEpoch`, `finalProcessEpoch` and deferred
transition-cache cleanup.

Shuffle kernel alone, `unshuffleList` at 90 rounds, minimum of 21 runs
in milliseconds, same machine:

| Input | main | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `u32`, 16,384 | 1.22 | 0.41 |
| `u32`, 250,000 | 18.5 | 6.1 |
| `u32`, 1,000,000 | 74 to 111 | 25 |
| `u64`, 1,000,000 | 75 | 33 |
| `u32`, 1,000,000, `-mcpu=generic` | 118 | 69 |

Two caveats on the kernel numbers:

- The scalar baseline depends on how the caller is compiled. The same
function measured 74 ms from one harness and 111 ms from another on the
same machine; the table uses the faster harness. The vector version
measured 25 ms from both.
- Release bindings are cross-compiled without `-Dcpu`, so they get the
baseline CPU. There `std.crypto` SHA-256 runs in software and takes
about 50 of the remaining 69 ms. That is a separate issue from this PR.
The `generic` row is aarch64; x86_64 was not run. Its baseline build was
only checked to compile the block to SSE2 instructions.

**Description**

Swap eight pairs per step with `@Vector(8, T)` whenever a whole source
byte of decisions remains. The shuffle output is unchanged.

- `maskedSwapBlock` loads the two 8-element blocks, reverses one so each
pair shares a lane, and selects per lane from the decision byte.
- `swapOrNotPairs` replaces the two per-round loops, which differed only
in their index ranges. It takes the block step when the descending index
is on a byte boundary and at least eight pairs remain, and keeps
`maskedSwap` for the unaligned head and the short tail.
- New tests compare the list shuffle with `ComputeShuffledIndex` for
every list size from 2 to 64 and for sizes around the 256-position
source hash windows. A deliberately stale source hash across a window
boundary is caught only by the second test.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation, tests, benchmarking and this description were primarily
authored with Claude Code. Submitted as a draft for human review.

author: Chen Kai
subject: test: initialize fresh decode outputs (#775)
body:
**Motivation**

The decode contracts clarified in #761 and #771 require callers to
initialize each destination and own cleanup. SSZ benchmarks and several
tests still decode into previously populated values, which does not meet
that contract.

**Description**

- Give the attestation, block, and state benchmarks separate output
storage. Each invocation starts from `default_value` and deinitializes
its result; allocating variants also release the outer struct.
- Rename the former no-allocation variants to `PreallocatedStruct`: only
the outer storage is retained, while decoded fields are allocated and
released each run. Decode timings now include result cleanup.
- Update the existing sanity tests, including progressive bitlists, to
decode into independent outputs with cleanup for owning types.
- Update the fixed-list, byte-list, and bit-list tree-read tests to use
fresh outputs for both populated and zero trees. Retain their allocation
checks by allowing only the output allocation, with no traversal
allocation.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: separate engine response timings (#10349)
body:
JSON-RPC `stream_time` currently includes JSON parsing and omits samples
when body reads, HTTP status checks or parsing fail. Stop the timer
immediately after body consumption, including failures, to match the
REST client.

Add `response_parse_time_seconds{routeId,encoding}` for JSON parsing and
SSZ deserialization, including failed parses. This excludes later value
conversion; empty REST responses produce no parse sample.

Adds deterministic coverage for timing boundaries, failed reads, HTTP
errors, invalid JSON/SSZ and empty responses. All 114 Engine tests, full
workspace type checks and lint pass.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: test: enforce native spec assertions (#10344)
body:
The spec harness checks the TypeScript progressive-balance counter even
when the fixture runs through the native state transition. A native
mismatch can therefore pass unnoticed. Invalid fixtures can also appear
to pass when processing fails because an allocation or native pool is
exhausted.

Require both counters to be registered, capture the native counter's
baseline for each registry and fail if it increases. A registered
counter without label samples is valid; missing registration and
malformed values fail. Propagate native resource failures from
invalid-fixture assertions instead of accepting them as the expected
invalid transition.

All 15 assertion-control tests pass, along with the beacon-node type
check and workspace build using the existing published native
dependency.

author: Chen Kai
subject: refactor: leave decode cleanup to callers (#761)
body:
**Motivation**

Decoders write into a caller-owned `out`; the caller initializes it with
`default_value` and deinitializes it after success or error.
`VariableListType.deserializeFromBytes` and the variable
`VectorType.deserializeFromBytes` also free and reset `out` on error
(added in #598), unlike every other value-path decoder. Came up in the
`out` ownership discussion on #754.

**Description**

Leave failed-decode cleanup to the caller.

- Drop the `errdefer` that deinitialized `out` in both decoders.
- Replace the test that required the decoder to free its output with
list and vector tests for a malformed offset, a malformed element, and
an allocation-failure sweep.
- Move `defer deinit` before the decode in the `loadState` trim scenario
and a few tests.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Primarily AI-authored with Claude Code.

author: Chen Kai
subject: refactor: clarify progressive decode ownership (#771)
body:
**Motivation**

Progressive list and variable progressive container decoders already
construct a private `replacement`, but also deinitialize the destination
before assigning the result. Output cleanup should belong to the caller,
which initializes `out` with `default_value` and defers its
deinitialization.

**Description**

Keep private replacement construction and remove decoder-side cleanup of
caller-owned output.

- `deserializeFromBytes`, `deserializeFromJson`, and `tree.toValue`
document the default-output precondition. Failures clean temporary
results and leave `out` unchanged; success transfers the result to the
caller.
- Adapt existing sanity, malformed-input, and allocation-failure tests
to use default outputs with caller-owned cleanup.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The implementation, tests, and PR description were primarily authored
with OpenAI Codex, with independent AI ownership review.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: perf: decode hex natively in nodejs fromHexInto (#10358)
body:
**Motivation**

Since #10203, `getBlobsV2` decodes responses into the preallocated
buffers through `fromHexInto`. In nodejs that function was re-exported
from the browser implementation, a JS loop that is much slower than
native hex decoding. The allocation savings were outweighed by extra
main-thread time. On our Hoodi nodes, the `getBlobsV2` call duration
(`beacon_engine_getBlobsV2_request_duration_seconds`) went up by ~8-17ms
per call after #10203, while the EL HTTP time stayed flat.

`packages/utils/test/perf/bytes.test.ts`, 128KB blob, node 24:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| nodejs `fromHex(blob)` | 130.8 us/op | 130.8 us/op |
| nodejs `fromHexInto(blob)` | ~1.04 ms/op (browser impl) | 120.3 us/op
|

**Description**

- implement `fromHexInto` for nodejs with `Buffer#write(hex, "hex")`
into the preallocated buffer instead of re-exporting the browser loop
- reject invalid characters by checking the number of bytes written,
`Buffer#write` stops silently at the first invalid character
- cover invalid characters and length mismatch for `fromHexInto` in unit
tests

- [x] External Contributors: I have read the [contributor
guidelines](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/unstable/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-assistance-notice)
and disclosed my usage of AI below.

Investigation, change and PR written by lodekeeper (AI agent), requested
by @nflaig.

author: Matthew Keil
subject: fix: queue column reconstructions in event multiple come in before completion (#10331)
body:
### Motivation

`ColumnReconstructionTracker` gates reconstruction behind one
process-wide `running` flag. If block A holds the flag when a different
block B reaches the 64 column threshold, B's trigger is dropped and
nothing retries it.

A supernode imports B on `hasAllData` with 64 columns, times out waiting
for `hasComputedAllData` in persistence, and archives only the columns
it physically holds. Later gossip columns for B are ignored once it is
in fork choice and `getBlobsV2` is skipped once `hasAllData` flips, so
the gap is never filled and the node cannot serve part of its advertised
custody for that block.

For this bug to come up it needs two roots to reach 64 columns inside
the same ~1-2s window (random delay plus KZG time). With 12s slots that
means one of:

- block A ~10s late, B on time
- equivocation in a single slot, splitting column indices across two
roots
- non-finality with multiple forks, where different proposers build
blocks for the same slot and both roots propagate in full
- an event loop stall near a full slot

### Description

- Track reconstruction in an insertion-ordered map keyed by block root.
A trigger for a root already queued or in flight is a no-op, a new root
waits its turn, and the next root drains when the current attempt
finishes. Concurrency stays at one.
- Remove a root once its attempt finishes so a later column can retry a
failed attempt.
- Move the under-half-columns guard into the tracker and credit time
spent in the queue toward the pre-reconstruction delay.
- Add tracker unit tests covering the dropped second root, dedupe,
single concurrency, draining after a failure, and retry.

author: Chen Kai
subject: feat: add struct progressive container (#777)
body:
**Motivation**

#346 added `StructContainerType`, which stores a fixed container as one
`container_struct` tree node instead of a subtree per field. Progressive
containers (EIP-7688) have no such form: every one builds its spine, one
subtree per group of fields, and the active-fields leaf. In a list that
cost repeats per element.

This adds the missing counterpart at the type layer, next to the
progressive list work in #773.

**Description**

A fixed progressive container can be stored as one tree node, and
progressive field gindices are relative to the type root.

- `StructProgressiveContainerType(ST, active_fields)` wraps
`FixedProgressiveContainerType` and replaces only the `tree` namespace.
- `tree.fromValue` and `tree.deserializeFromBytes` create one
`container_struct` node through `Pool.createContainerStruct`.
- `tree.toValue`, `tree.getValuePtr` and `tree.serializeIntoBytes` read
the stored value.
- Hashing, serialization, JSON and field metadata are the wrapped type's
own declarations, so roots and bytes do not change.
- `WrappedT.toTree` builds the progressive subtree on demand, so proofs
can walk into the node.
- `getFieldGindex` of `FixedProgressiveContainerType` and
`VariableProgressiveContainerType` prepends the step from the type root
to the contents root, where the active fields are mixed in.
- `progressive.subtreeIndex` returns the subtree that holds a chunk. It
returned how many subtrees hold a chunk count, which is one too many for
every chunk that is not first in its subtree.
- `progressive.subtreeCount` is the old loop under the name that matches
it. `getNodes` and `fillWithContentsComptime` call it, so trees and
roots do not change.
  - `progressive.chunkGindex` stays relative to the contents root.

**Bench**

100K validator-shaped elements in a `FixedProgressiveListType`,
`ReleaseFast` on an Apple M-series laptop, mean per run. Measured with a
throwaway bench that is not part of this PR:

| Workload | progressive subtree | struct node |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fromValue | 131 ms | 33.1 ms |
| fromValue + getRoot | 586 ms | 205 ms |
| toValue | 8.58 ms | 2.49 ms |
| serialize | 7.19 ms | 1.21 ms |
| deserialize | 190 ms | 31.4 ms |

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Primarily AI-authored with Claude Code.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: ci: wait for the REST re-probe before judging the engine interop EL restart (#10372)
body:
## Motivation

The 2026-10-13 nightly failed nethermind/fulu with `cl2 after restart: 3
requests fell back to JSON-RPC`
([run](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/38344802096)).
Lodestar behaved as designed. The harness judged too early.

After `docker restart`, the wait loop polls `el_offline`. Node 2 only
notices the EL is gone on its next engine call, so the first poll passes
("back after 12s" is 0s of waiting plus the fixed `sleep 12`). In that
run:

- 04:11:34 EL2 restarted
- 04:11:39 node 2 sees the EL offline, the REST capabilities probe fails
and backs off 12s
- 04:11:41 EL back online
- 04:11:47 `restart` snapshot taken
- 04:11:53 REST re-probe succeeds

The JSON-RPC requests between 04:11:47 and 04:11:53 landed in the judged
window.

## Description

- Wait until node 2 has logged the EL recovery since the restart and,
for Lodestar builds with the REST transport, a new capabilities probe
result, before taking the `restart` snapshot. Drop the fixed `sleep 12`.
- If the EL is in sync but node 2 logged neither within 240s, log it and
judge anyway instead of aborting.
- README: the unjudged restart window now includes the re-probe.

Checked the gate against `cl2.log` from the failing run: it holds until
the 04:11:53 re-probe and passes after it.

> This PR was written with AI assistance.

---------

Co-authored-by: lodekeeper <lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Lodekeeper
subject: test: pin fake clock in prepareNextSlot slot offset test (#10373)
body:
**Motivation**

`prepares at the current slot offset when the next duration is 6000 ms`
in `prepareNextSlot.test.ts` is flaky (about 1% of runs):
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/38387876396/job/115265388997

The scheduler subscribes to a real `Clock` (genesisTime 0) whose fake
timers start at wall time. If a wall time slot boundary for the last
slot of an epoch lands in roughly the first 4s of the test window, the
slot event runs `prepareForNextSlot(wallSlot)`. The test's fork stub
turns that into an altair epoch transition. It sleeps 6000ms * 0.6667
and calls `recomputeForkChoiceHead` before the asserted 8s mark. In the
failing run, wall slot 149324159 (the last slot of its epoch) started at
11:11:48 UTC, while this test was running.

**Description**

Anchor the fake clock to the start of `clockSlot`, which is the same
approach the gloas builder status test in this file already uses. The
real clock then cannot emit a slot event during the test.

Verified locally: seeding the test's fake timers at the CI failure time
(11:11:45.6 UTC) reproduces the failure without this change and passes
with it. A scan over 200 start times gave 7 failures without the change
and 0 with it. The full file passes (13/13) and Biome is clean.

🤖 Generated with AI assistance

author: Nico Flaig
subject: ci: add nightly mixed client interop workflow (#10361)
body:
Runs Lodestar against the default-branch image of every other consensus
client every night, crossed over so both directions of the beacon API
are exercised at once: a Lodestar beacon node drives the other client's
validator client and the other client's beacon node drives a Lodestar
validator client, with a third Lodestar node without validators as the
bootnode. Same idea as the engine API interop run from #10333, so client
pair regressions show up the day they land, with the logs needed to file
an issue on either side.

- one job per client, Lighthouse, Prysm, Teku, Nimbus, Grandine and
Vero, on their default-branch images rebuilt nightly by ethpandaops
(`-minimal` builds where the preset is compiled in). Tags are resolved
to their digest before every run and the summary row records the digests
and versions that were judged. Lodestar runs the published
`chainsafe/lodestar:next`, geth master sits behind every node, both can
be overridden through `workflow_dispatch`. The package has no separate
Grandine validator client and Vero has no beacon node, those two run
with Lodestar on both sides of the affected node
- fulu at genesis with blob spam against both validator nodes, judged
once epoch 4 is finalized. A gloas at epoch 2 scenario is in the script
but not in the workflow yet, it joins once the other clients are ready
for it
- the verdict comes from Lodestar's own metrics and logs after the first
finalized epoch plus the chain as the Lodestar beacon node sees it:
every REST error response of the Lodestar beacon node by route and
status, gossip rejects, req/resp errors and peer drops, errors in its
log; request errors, duty and signing errors, missing publishes and
warnings of the Lodestar validator client; missed slots named with the
proposer's pair, every validator hitting the attestation target in every
judged epoch and each pair hitting the head with at least 90% of its
attestations, sync committee seats filled per block, both beacon nodes
agreeing on finality and staying connected
- every beacon node subscribes to all subnets, with a handful of peers a
message could otherwise not be published at all (the
`submitPoolAttestationsV2 failed` warning in every engine interop run is
exactly that), and the Lodestar beacon node serves historical states so
participation can be read from finalized states
- a failure with a known cause, on either side, is listed in
`known-issues.mjs` with a pattern for the failure text, optionally a log
line that has to confirm it, a note and the issue link. It shows up as a
known issue in the summary row without failing the job, anything else on
the same pair still does, and the entry goes once the fix is in the
image the nightly runs
- every run uploads all container logs, the metrics snapshots and a
`result.json` plus a summary table row

State of the matrix: Lighthouse, Grandine, Nimbus and Teku pass, Prysm
and Vero are green with known issues. Found and filed from the first
runs: Teku ignored the whole subscription message of a peer announcing
more than 200 topics, a Lodestar supernode with all subnets announces
205, so the pair never finalized (Consensys/teku#11482, fixed in
Consensys/teku#11483 the same night); Prysm returns the current epoch's
dependent root for next-epoch proposer duties
(OffchainLabs/prysm#17681); the Nimbus validator client trips its own
doppelganger detection on a block proposal in epoch 0
(status-im/nimbus-eth2#9278, the nightly runs it with detection off
until that is fixed); Vero still requires `SECONDS_PER_SLOT`
(serenita-org/vero#353). On our side: `produceAttestationData` hands out
the next epoch's source after the epoch precompute in the last slot of
an epoch, which is what Prysm's aggregators run into (#10368), liveness
marks last-slot attesters live in the next epoch, which took the Nimbus
VC down after a beacon node restart (#10367), and attester duties for
epoch 1 are rejected before genesis (#10369). The matrix ran on this PR
through a temporary `pull_request` trigger, last run
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/38385107280, removed
before merge as in #10333.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: test: make data column range benchmarks report only (#10377)
body:
**Motivation**

The `dataColumnSidecarsByRange` range benchmarks are the largest source
of false `Performance regression` failures in the Benchmark workflow. Of
the last 17 failed benchmark attempts, 9 are these benches tripping the
10x threshold (from #10074) at 12x to 101x. That includes all 4 attempts
of the v1.50.0 merge back on unstable.

The legacy range benches are bimodal on the shared runner. `8 slots / 1
columns / legacy` normally measures 120-340us over 1.7k-3.3k runs. On
unrelated commits it measures ~11-17ms on every op and converges at
26-44 runs. The very next bench (`8 slots / 8 columns / legacy`, 8x more
data) is back to ~0.7ms. The slow mode only ever hit a legacy bench that
runs right after a flat files bench. No threshold separates that from a
real regression.

It also poisons the rolling baseline. A spiked unstable run is persisted
before the regression check fails, and PRs based on that commit then
report `head state / 8 slots / 1 columns / legacy` at x0.018.

**Description**

Set `noThreshold: true` on the range benches so they are still measured
and reported but no longer gate CI. The two single slot lookup benches
keep `threshold: 10`. They have not tripped in this sample.

🤖 Generated with AI assistance

Co-authored-by: lodekeeper <lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Lodekeeper
subject: perf: avoid array concat when deserializing ENR subnets (#10382)
body:
**Motivation**

`enrSubnets - fastDeserialize 64 bits` is one of the most frequent false
benchmark regressions. Across the 600 failed Benchmark runs since June,
it was flagged in 21 of them at x3.0 to x5.0, most recently on unstable:
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/38464919941/job/115529054217

The 64 bit path builds the result with 8 chained `concat` calls, so each
call allocates 8 intermediate arrays. On CI it measures 632-853ns
normally and 2.2-3.8us when it trips. That makes the "fast" path 2-3x
slower than `ssz BitVector 64 bits` in the same file. The ssz bench
allocates a single array and has never been flagged.

**Description**

Preallocate the result array and copy the cached per-byte bits into it,
the same way `newFilledArray` builds its arrays. Output is unchanged.

Local numbers (5M calls):
- concat: 4914ms, 1629 GC events
- preallocated: 710ms, 318 GC events

`@chainsafe/benchmark` locally, `enrSubnets - fastDeserialize 64 bits`:
~1.1us/op before, ~310ns/op after. ssz BitVector is ~410ns/op.

Unit tests in `enrSubnets.test.ts` pass (11/11).

🤖 Generated with AI assistance

Co-authored-by: lodekeeper <lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Cayman
subject: perf: stream progressive tree construction (#746)
body:
**Motivation**

Progressive tree construction still buffers every child node, and tree
decoding first materializes a complete SSZ value. Those temporary arrays
and values are unnecessary when the destination is already a persistent
tree. This addresses the remaining construction follow-up in
[#158](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/issues/158).

**Description**

Build progressive lists, bitlists, and containers incrementally from
values or serialized bytes.

- `progressive.TreeBuilder` keeps one incremental subtree builder and a
bounded set of completed subtree roots, then assembles the right spine.
It shares tree limits with `NodeIterator`; `appendOwned` takes ownership
on entry, including on error, and requires fresh, unretained roots or
zero nodes.
- `tree.fromValue` appends packed leaves or child roots directly,
including zero nodes for inactive container fields. Fixed progressive
containers retain the error contract required by struct-node
materialization.
- Remove the unused `progressive.fillWithContents` and
`fillWithContentsComptime` helpers.
- `tree.deserializeFromBytes` consumes fixed elements, variable-element
offsets, and bitlist delimiters directly while preserving canonical
boolean and offset validation.
- `Node.SubtreeBuilder` replaces `FillWithContentsIterator` across the
monorepo, naming the existing append/finish API as a builder.
- `SerializedChunkIterator` shares bitlist chunk traversal between
hashing and tree decoding. It borrows full input chunks and copies only
when padding or delimiter removal is needed. `chunk.fromBytes`,
`packBasicChunk`, and standard-library windows share byte padding and
basic-value packing.
- `inactiveFieldCount` computes sparse-container gaps at compile time
for hashing and construction, replacing repeated runtime index
bookkeeping.
- Regression tests prohibit temporary allocator use, sweep pool
exhaustion through partial builds and decoding, and compare 512
deterministic byte-input cases against value decoding. Tests also cover
sparse fields, subtree/delimiter boundaries, unchanged serialized
inputs, and cleanup of inputs rejected after completion or during pool
exhaustion.

`test_case.zig` now checks `OutOfMemory` through retained struct payload
storage. Its previous progressive-decoder probe depended on the scratch
allocation removed here and failed with:

```text
expected error.OutOfMemory, found error.PoolExhausted
```

Broader differences in who cleans up after a failed tree build are
tracked in [#783](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/issues/783).

This PR can merge independently of
[#745](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/pull/745). Refresh the
second PR after merging the first to reconcile shared helper and
test-file edits.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: serialize attestation slashing protection checks per validator (#10303)
body:
This is not a security issue. The overlap below needs `--distributed`,
which is only used by DVT clusters (e.g. Charon). There the validator
client holds a key share, not the full key, and the DVT middleware
aggregates signatures, so the validator client cannot produce a
slashable message on its own. Running full keystores with
`--distributed` makes no sense and nobody does it. The pre-electra case
needs a beacon node serving two duties for one key, and every live
network is past electra. The race is still worth fixing.

The attestation slashing protection check and the write recording the
attestation are separate steps, two checks for the same key running at
the same time both pass before either one is recorded. The validator
clock only waits for a slot's attestation task when skipping slots is
allowed, with `--distributed` (`clock.skipSlots=false`) slot `S+1`
starts while slot `S` is still waiting for attestation data. A beacon
node that serves two duties for one key in an epoch under different
validator indices and releases both responses together gets two
signatures with the same target epoch. Before electra the default config
is exposed as well, two duties with different committee indices sign
different roots in the same slot. Attestation counterpart of #10142.

- serialize attestation checks and writes per validator, including
interchange imports
- checks for keys covered by a running interchange import wait until the
import is done, imports run one after another, this applies to block
proposals as well
- add regression coverage for overlapping checks and imports

Without the serialization the overlap tests fail, a double vote and a
surround vote are accepted next to the attestation they conflict with.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: assert doppelganger safety only for messages counted in liveness (#10396)
body:
**Motivation**

Follow-up to
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10312#discussion_r4278615099.
Doppelganger detection trips on any liveness reported for the validator
while it's unverified. `validatorSeenAtEpoch` counts attestations
(gossip and in blocks), aggregators, payload attestations and block
proposers, so the VC must not publish any of these during detection.
Slashable messages need the check anyway.

Duty services already drop unverified validators (attestation, block and
PTC duties), so the store asserts are a second line of defense. Audit of
the `ValidatorStore` sign methods:

- blocks, attestations, payload attestations: assert, keep
- aggregate and proof: counted in liveness through `seenAggregators` but
had no assert, added
- proposer preferences: not slashable and not counted in liveness,
assert removed
- sync committee messages and contributions, selection proofs, randao,
execution payload envelope, voluntary exit, validator registration,
builder auth: neither slashable nor counted in liveness, no assert

**Description**

- assert doppelganger safety in `signAggregateAndProof`
- drop the assert from `signProposerPreferences`
- unit test for the aggregate case, which fails without the change

🤖 Generated with AI assistance

Co-authored-by: lodekeeper <lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Cayman
subject: perf: stream progressive tree reads (#745)
body:
**Motivation**

Progressive tree reads still allocate complete node-ID arrays, and
variable-list, bitlist, and container sizing or serialization
materializes values just to inspect or copy them. These temporary
allocations remain after the earlier fixed-list serialization work in
[#158](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/issues/158).

**Description**

Read progressive lists, bitlists, and containers directly through
`progressive.NodeIterator`.

- `tree.toValue` follows the fresh, default-initialized output contract
established in [#771](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/pull/771)
and [#775](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/pull/775). It
publishes the value after traversal and terminator validation succeed,
and cleans up partial values on failure. Callers initialize `out` with
`default_value` and own its cleanup.
- `tree.serializeIntoBytes` writes packed bytes and variable offsets
directly, checking output capacity and offset arithmetic.
- `tree.serializedSize` reads child sizes directly; bitlist size comes
from its length leaf.
- Remove the unused `progressive.getNodes` helper.
- Regression tests cover allocation-failure cleanup, unchanged default
outputs on failure, sparse fields, subtree and delimiter boundaries,
malformed terminators, short buffers, and allocation budgets that allow
only materialized output storage.

Builds on the progressive tree construction merged in
[#746](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/pull/746).

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation was primarily AI-authored with Codex.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: skip buffering unknown-root gossip messages from expired slots (#10388)
body:
Follow-up to #10039. The per-slot budget of buffered unknown roots is
keyed by the message slot, and `onClockSlot` only keeps the last
`MAX_UNKNOWN_ROOTS_SLOT_CACHE_SIZE` slots. Messages are accepted up to
32 slots in the past though, so a message from an already expired slot
was still buffered, and each of those slots got its own fresh 5-root
budget until the next tick. The effective bound was ~33 slots x 5 roots
instead of 3 x 5.

Such messages are no longer buffered, for both the block and the payload
await queue. They are still searched so the block or payload can be
recovered, they would have been dropped on the next slot anyway. The
reject metric reason is `expired`.

A unit test that buffers 5 roots for every slot in the accepted range
holds 165 roots before this change and 15 after. The same setup with
`execution_payload` envelopes (5 unknown roots per slot, 3 envelopes per
root, which hits the per-root cap of 2) holds 330 envelopes before and
30 after.

subject: feat: implement FOCIL EIP-7805 in heze (#10312)
body:
Implements FOCIL (EIP-7805) for Heze per consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4
([`specs/heze`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/tree/v1.7.0-beta.4/specs/heze))
and the engine API
[`bogota.md`](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/bogota.md)
(`engine_getInclusionListV1`, `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV5`,
`engine_newPayloadV6`).

- Inclusion list gossip topic, validation and `InclusionListsByIndices`
req/resp responder, with a store that tracks timely vs untimely lists
and the two-message equivocation rule
- Inclusion list transactions passed as payload attributes, the payload
id cache misses when the set changes
- Inclusion list verdict from `newPayload` recorded per block in proto
array, `should_extend_payload` builds on the EMPTY variant of an
unsatisfied payload, verdict exposed in the fork choice dump

gossip, the beacon API and the builder API, bids received before the
inclusion list deadline of `bid.slot - 1` are ignored

publishing, plus the `inclusion_list` event
- Validator client inclusion list duties and service, lists are built
once the slot's payload is imported and published before the deadline

Deviation from beta.4: bid bits are checked against timely lists only,
also by the proposer
(https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5741).

https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5727 is released.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: remove signer from validator store if its index is known (#10386)
body:
`removeSigner` returned early when `indicesService.removeForKey()`
succeeded, so a key with a known validator index was never removed from
`validators`. Keymanager `DELETE /eth/v1/keystores` and `DELETE
/eth/v1/remotekeys` answered `deleted` and removed the key from disk,
but the key stayed loaded, the next index poll found it again and it
kept performing duties. Without doppelganger protection it kept signing,
which can get the validator slashed if the exported slashing protection
is imported into another client. Keys removed from an external signer by
`externalSignerSync` were affected the same way.

The index is now removed and the key is always deleted from
`validators`, with a regression test for a key whose index has been
polled.

Closes #10385

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: isolate selection proof failures per validator (#10387)
body:
Selection proofs are signed one validator after another while polling
attester duties and when getting sync committee duties for a slot, and a
single failure aborted the whole loop. One validator with a failing
signer made every validator on the client miss its attester duties for
the epoch, or its sync committee duties for the slot.

The easiest way to hit this is a remote key the external signer does not
hold, e.g. imported through the keymanager API with the wrong URL, since
`importRemoteKeys` does not check the signer has the key. The selection
proof then fails every epoch and the client stops attesting for all of
its validators. A key removed from the external signer while still in
the sync committee did the same to sync committee duties until the next
duties poll (see #10386).

Errors are now caught and logged per validator, matching how attestation
and sync committee message signing already handle them. A skipped
attester duty is retried on the next poll.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: resolve builder pubkeys in a single pass in getStateBuilders (#10408)
body:
**Motivation**

Looking up builders by pubkey in `getStateBuilders` (`POST
/eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/builders`) scans the whole builder
registry for every requested pubkey. With a large registry this is O(ids
× builders) on the main thread. On glamsterdam-devnet-12 (~24k builders
after a deposit spray) a client polling this endpoint blocked the main
thread for ~17s per request, which made the node miss proposals and fall
behind head.

**Description**

Build a builder pubkey to index map at most once per request (lazily,
only if a pubkey id is requested) and resolve pubkey ids against it.

Micro benchmark, 400 pubkey ids against 24k builders on a tree-backed
builder list:
- linear scan per id: ~6.3s
- single pass map: ~66ms

---------

Co-authored-by: lodekeeper <lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: use the block root for the genesis dependent root fallback (#10409)
body:
The proposer duties endpoint falls back to the genesis block root when
the decision root is not in the state yet, which is the case for
requests served from the slot 0 state on a gloas-at-genesis network (the
lookahead decision slot is slot 0 itself). That fallback hashed the
`SignedBeaconBlock` container instead of the block message, so the
validator client received a dependent root that does not exist in fork
choice and its proposer preferences for epochs 0 and 1 were rejected
with `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENT_ROOT` until the first block was imported.

Seen on the heze-devnet-2 rehearsal (3 Lodestar nodes, gloas at
genesis): duties reported `0x8638…` while the genesis block root is
`0x40a2…`, and every VC logged `Error submitting signed proposer
preferences ... UNKNOWN_DEPENDENT_ROOT` at slots 0 and 1.

- hash the block message, and only read the block from the DB once the
state is past the block roots window, the anchor checkpoint root already
covers the slot 0 state
- unit test for the dependent root at genesis, fails on unstable

A/B on the same kurtosis config (3 Lodestar nodes on ethrex, gloas at
genesis, mainnet preset): with unstable the duties endpoint reported
`0x8638…` at genesis against a genesis root of `0x40a2…`, every VC
logged the error twice and the beacon nodes answered the submissions
with 400. With this branch the duties endpoint reported the genesis
root, all proposer preferences submissions at and after genesis returned
200 and no `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENT_ROOT` was logged.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: feat: add gnosis preset (#791)
body:
**Motivation**

Lodestar with `--chain.nativeStateTransition` fails on gnosis at startup
with `PresetMismatch`. `Preset.gnosis` exists, but there is no gnosis
preset struct or build preset, and `active_preset` can only resolve to
mainnet or minimal, so a gnosis binding cannot be built.

**Description**

Add `PresetGnosis` per the [gnosis
preset](https://github.com/gnosischain/specs/tree/master/consensus/preset/gnosis).
It overrides `SLOTS_PER_EPOCH`, `BASE_REWARD_FACTOR`,
`EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD`, `MAX_WITHDRAWALS_PER_PAYLOAD`,
`MAX_VALIDATORS_PER_WITHDRAWALS_SWEEP` and
`MAX_PENDING_PARTIALS_PER_WITHDRAWALS_SWEEP`, and references
`PresetMainnet` for everything else.

- select the preset by enum, an unknown preset string fails to compile
instead of selecting mainnet
- add the `gnosis` build preset and `prepare-gnosis` script
- set gnosis and chiado `FULU_FORK_EPOCH` and
`MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS` per
[gnosischain/configs](https://github.com/gnosischain/configs)
- build gnosis bindings in CI

Published packages still only contain the mainnet binary. Distributing a
gnosis binary needs zapi support and is left for a follow-up.

Validation: a ReleaseSafe gnosis binding loaded the gnosis finalized
state at slot 30630848 with the canonical root `0x53398c9c…` and
rejected a mainnet `PRESET_BASE`. A gnosis node with the same preset on
2.0.0 and engineMock imported 131 blocks across 10 epoch transitions
with canonical head roots. `test:preset` and `test:config` passed on
mainnet and gnosis; mainnet bindings build, tidy, lint and
tracked-source formatting passed.

author: Nazar Hussain
subject: build: add AFL++ fuzzing image (#787)
body:
**Motivation**

The ChainSafe fuzz platform runs long-lived campaigns from container
images. lodestar-z's AFL++ targets only run on a developer's machine
today, so there is nothing to schedule, and no defined answer to when a
fuzz image is built.

**Description**

Packages every `test/fuzz` target into one image and publishes it to
GHCR on demand.

- `Dockerfile.fuzz`: CI's existing fuzz toolchain in the build stage;
only binaries, `afl-fuzz` and corpora in the runtime stage (221 MB)
- `test/fuzz/docker/run-fuzz.sh`: runs one campaign for `FUZZ_TARGET`
(`ssz-basic` or `ssz_basic`; the platform's names use hyphens), resumes
after restarts, saves crashes, reports status for the platform from the
moment it starts
- `.github/workflows/fuzz-image.yml`: publishing is manual: a maintainer
runs it on `main` once enough good changes have landed (`main` +
`sha-<short>` tags, newest 20 kept). A manual run on another branch
publishes `branch-<name>` instead, to try a branch on the platform
before merging. PRs build and test only
- `test/fuzz/README.md`: container image section; fixes the single-crash
replay command, which aborts without `__AFL_DEFER_FORKSRV=1`

Tested locally: all 13 targets run their first seed, and a campaign runs
under the platform's restrictions (non-root, read-only, no network).
This PR's CI run is the first on amd64.

Tested end to end on the fuzz server (`fuzzer-01`, platform side in
ChainSafe/lodestar-ansible-development#628): a manual run on this branch
published `branch-nh-fuzz-image`; the server pulled it, ran `ssz-basic`
under its restrictions, and on the next publish switched the campaign to
the new image within 5 minutes, resuming its corpus. The
`lodestar-z-fuzz` package is public.

After merging: run the workflow on `main` once, then point the server's
targets at `:main`.
