author: Chen Kai
subject: fix: release failed batch parents (#790)
body:
**Motivation**

When `setNodes` or `setNodesAtDepth` fails partway through a batch,
cleanup can leak subtrees completed by earlier iterations. It also
releases `node_id`, which may be a traversal cursor into the original
tree rather than an owned temporary root. See the [existing
cleanup](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/blob/5fbb0e23a64c9a3e3670135787dd750f573630ec/src/persistent_merkle_tree/Node.zig#L1427).

A separate failure-injection probe against that base reproduced an
incorrect release on `RefCountOverflow`:

```text
expected 105, found 104
FAIL (TestExpectedEqual)
```

**Description**

Release the batch's temporary parents on failure while preserving the
original tree and retained replacement nodes.

- Use an iteration-local `errdefer` for freshly allocated parents and an
outer `errdefer` for pending subtrees.
- Exercise both batch APIs in one table-driven pool-exhaustion test, and
add later-path `InvalidNode` regressions, checking pool occupancy and
original/input node references.


**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation and regression tests were primarily authored with Claude
Code. Codex reviewed the changes, ran independent failure-injection
tests, and prepared this draft PR.

author: lodekeeper-z
subject: feat: add heze timing configuration (#794)
body:
**Motivation**

The native `BeaconConfig` constructor silently ignores `HEZE_FORK_EPOCH`
and `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE` because they are absent from `ChainConfig`.
Extract the configuration portion of
[bfc159a7](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/commit/bfc159a7344291d9da46a0155f2501279219c851)
from #782 so it can land independently of native networking.

**Description**

Add the Heze timing and fork-version fields to `ChainConfig`, its
network defaults, and native configuration validation.

- Keep Heze unscheduled by default. Match [Lodestar's current duration
defaults](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10398): 12 seconds
on mainnet, 6 on minimal, and 5 on Gnosis, rather than the source
commit's provisional values.
- Add `HEZE_FORK_VERSION` with network-specific defaults and optional
merge overrides. Reuse the native four-byte version validation.
- Accept disabled epochs as `Infinity` and reject malformed epoch
values. Require both slot durations to be positive whole seconds, using
the existing constructor error contracts.
- Cover configuration overrides, network defaults, and binding input
boundaries.

This is the configuration foundation only. It does not add Heze fork
activation, piecewise slot/time helpers, consensus reward changes, or
the network branch's gossip-retention policy. Existing slot timing
remains unchanged.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Hermes Agent extracted the existing commit, added the fork-version
configuration requested in review, and authored the tests and this
description. Human review is in progress.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: drop finalized block hash from payload id cache key (#10432)
body:
**Motivation**

On Sepolia, our proposals in the first slot of an epoch are published
about 80ms later than in other slots (3 days of logs: slot 0 p50 603ms
vs 525ms for slots 1-31). Every slot 0 proposal logged
`prepType=Reorged`, every other one `Cached`.

When finalization advances at the epoch boundary, the payload id
prepared by `prepareNextSlot` no longer matches because the cache key
includes `finalizedBlockHash`. `produceBlockBody` then re-sends
forkchoiceUpdated, the EL returns the same payload id, and we wait
`PAYLOAD_GENERATION_TIME_MS` again before `getPayload`.

**Description**

- Drop `finalizedBlockHash` from the payload id cache key. The payload
id only depends on the head block hash and the payload attributes.
Lighthouse keys its cache the same way (`PayloadIdCacheKey
{head_block_hash, payload_attributes}`).
- Add a unit test that a prepared payload id is reused when the
finalized block hash changed.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Investigation, code and tests by lodekeeper (AI).

Co-authored-by: lodekeeper <lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Chen Kai
subject: feat: support progressive ssz views (#793)
body:
**Motivation**

Gloas needs tree views for progressive SSZ types. This replaces #763 and
#773 and provides the SSZ support needed by #764.

**Description**

- Add progressive list and bitlist `TreeView`s, and extend
`ContainerTreeView` for sparse progressive fields. List views support
growth, slicing, and read-only iteration; basic lists can use chunked
leaves.
- Add `TypeOpts.limit` to bound progressive decoding and list growth
without changing Merkle roots.
- Add `ProgressiveByteListType` with hex JSON encoding. YAML and JSON
fixture parsers decode it as bytes.
- Progressive decoders and `tree.toValue` write into `out` in place.
Callers initialize variable outputs with `default_value` and
deinitialize them after success or error, including partially decoded
results.
- Guard container sizes before reading offsets, including direct calls
to `readFieldRanges`. Fix `hasOxPrefix` for empty and one-character
strings.

Consensus fixtures move to `v1.7.0-beta.4`, with the `NewPayloadRequest`
types needed by its static tests. Generic SSZ tests run the new
`ssz-specs` JSON fixtures alongside the existing `alpha.11` YAML cases.
The YAML cases retain malformed-input coverage; consensus releases
stopped shipping them in `alpha.14`.

Remaining work: nested compatible unions (#788, four skipped JSON
cases), generated fixture schemas (#795), and progressive byte-list NAPI
conversion. The basic-list view keeps `cached_leaf` pending Gloas
benchmarks.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Primarily AI-authored with Claude Code, porting #763, #764 and #773.
Review follow-ups by Codex.

author: Nazar Hussain
subject: test: use fake timers instead of Date.now spies (#10440)
body:
**Motivation**

Follow-up to #10434. Most time-dependent tests use `vi.useFakeTimers`,
but a few spied on `Date.now` directly. A `Date.now` spy also ties a
test to the clock the code reads today: if `wrapPromise` moved to
`performance.now()`, its duration tests would fail (`expected 0.03 to be
100`) and need rewriting.

**Description**

- `utils/test/unit/promise.test.ts`: `vi.useFakeTimers({now: 1000})`, a
real `setTimeout` promise and `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(100)` instead
of `Date.now` spies, keeping the exact `durationMs === 100` assertion.
- `beacon-node/test/unit/chain/validatorMonitor.test.ts`:
`vi.useFakeTimers()` with `vi.setSystemTime` for the retain-period
tests.
- `beacon-node/test/unit/executionEngine/restCompatibility.test.ts`:
`vi.useFakeTimers({toFake: ["Date"], now})` with `vi.setSystemTime`.
Only `Date` is faked since these tests talk to a real local HTTP server.
- Real timers are restored in `afterEach`.

Left as is on purpose: the `Date.now` spies in
`sync/range/chain.test.ts` and `sync/unknownBlock.test.ts` change the
returned time between consecutive synchronous reads to test every
clock-read crossing point (#10249, #10250). Fake timers cannot advance
time between two reads in the same tick, so those spies stay.

**Testing**

- `promise.test.ts` 5/5 in Node and Chromium. Firefox not run locally
(browser fails to launch on this machine), CI covers it.
- `validatorMonitor.test.ts` and `restCompatibility.test.ts` 50/50.
- Mutations: dropping the time jump in the prune test, keeping the REST
reprobe jump inside the retry window, and breaking the duration by 1 ms
each fail. The two time jumps whose removal stays green (re-register,
404 remembered) also stay green with the original spies, so no coverage
changes.
- biome, `check-types` for utils and beacon-node.

**Description**

Follow-ups: the `u32` cache optimization is in #797; progressive schema

**Validation**

[Current CI](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/pull/764/checks)

Local ReleaseSafe checks at `3008548b` passed the state-transition,
shuffling and bit-array modules and 1,248 selected beta.4 cases across
minimal and mainnet. Mainnet bindings passed 481 tests, with three
optional fixture skips. Formatting, tidy and lint passed.

<details>
<summary>Historical Plataberget replay benchmark</summary>

Native `33bcbf63` against `2c7a3e1e` with the same pinned host harness:
69 blocks, 85,467 validators, two epoch boundaries and 64 retained
states. Both artifacts used Zig 0.16, ReleaseSafe, mainnet,
`x86_64-linux-gnu.2.31`, `x86_64_v3+sha` and Node 24.13. Two alternating
AB/BA series retained all 12 measured pairs after warmups.

| Metric | Baseline median | Candidate median | Median paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Transition wall time | 2,151.3 ms | 2,170.9 ms | +1.31% |
| Transition CPU time | 2,274.6 ms | 2,296.9 ms | +1.17% |
| Initialization | 752.4 ms | 727.9 ms | -3.46% |
| Peak RSS | 670.02 MiB | 670.12 MiB | +0.023% |

Native epoch time was +2.20%. Transition pair changes ranged from -2.12%
to +6.41%, so small latency differences remain unresolved. All 28

author: Nico Flaig
subject: perf: store shuffling indices as u32 (#797)
body:
**Motivation**

Active and shuffled validator indices occupy `u64` buffers even though
the native pubkey cache and JavaScript index arrays use `u32`. Epoch
shuffling also allocates a positions buffer and maps the result back to
validator indices.

**Description**

Store the native cache indices as `u32` and shuffle them directly. This
halves the index-buffer storage and removes one temporary allocation
from `EpochShuffling.init`.

- use `u32` slices through epoch caches, proposer/sync sampling and the
existing PTC sampler
- widen to `u64` at SSZ boundaries; JavaScript still receives copied
`Uint32Array` values
- give `BitList.intersectValues` explicit result/input element types and
a `[]const Value` parameter, with no `anytype`
- reject more than `maxInt(u32)` validators before constructing the
native caches

This extracts the optimization from #764 following [review
feedback](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/pull/764#discussion_r4324206799),
so its cache/API changes can be reviewed separately. It now targets
`main`. The Zig slice signatures change; SSZ field widths and JavaScript
outputs do not.

Validation at `ea3f1d70` after merging `main`:

- ReleaseSafe state-transition, shuffling and bit-array modules pass on
minimal (253 passed, three existing skips) and mainnet (256 passed),
using an isolated build cache.
- Selected beta.4 proposer lookahead, PTC, sync-committee, attestation,
fork-upgrade and slot tests pass: 656 minimal and 592 mainnet. The 64
mainnet skips correspond to vectors absent from that preset.
- Fresh mainnet ReleaseSafe bindings pass 487 tests, with three optional
execution-proof fixture skips. All 18 tidy checks, formatting and lint
pass; lint retains four existing warnings.

The merge preserves the reviewed 19-file optimization diff and the
serialized transaction compatibility changes from #796.

Historical shuffling benchmark at `1e30c79f` against `2c3baf62`:

Actual `EpochShuffling.init`, mainnet ReleaseSafe, Zig 0.16, native
target on an Intel i7-1360P. Each size uses ABBA process order on one
pinned CPU, two warmups and five measured seeds per process. Each
variant therefore has ten timings from two processes, with the same five
measured seeds repeated. Input preparation, output checks and cleanup
are outside the timed constructor.

| Active validators | Before median | After median | Time change |
Retained allocation MB, before → after | Peak allocation MB, before →
after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 million | 56.67 ms | 45.89 ms | -19.0% | 16.03 → 8.03 | 20.00 → 8.03
|
| 2 million | 123.52 ms | 94.21 ms | -23.7% | 32.03 → 16.03 | 40.00 →
16.03 |

Allocation figures are requested bytes in decimal MB, including the
owned active indices; they are not RSS. The new path uses one fewer
allocation. A/B output hashes match for every seed and size, input and
committee partition checks pass, and tracked live bytes return to zero
after every teardown. Process timings vary, so these results describe
isolated shuffling construction and do not establish whole-epoch or
live-node improvements.

These measurements were collected before this split. The constructor and
sampler implementation is unchanged; the follow-up replaces the BitList
input type and adapts its callers. No new benchmark or live-node
improvement is claimed for this revision.

---------

Co-authored-by: bing <spiralladder@fastmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Chen Kai <281165273grape@gmail.com>

author: Cayman
subject: fix: deduplicate incomplete payload sync at the payload deadline (#10289)
body:
**Motivation**

Gloas columns currently trigger payload sync at the block deadline and
arm one timer per column. An envelope with no arriving columns never
triggers that fallback. Duplicate notifications and overlapping async
work can restart an in-flight payload fetch or import.

**Description**

Schedule one incomplete-payload notification per input at the configured
payload deadline for the input slot's fork, from either envelope or
column gossip. Skip inputs that complete or leave the cache while
waiting. Track scheduled inputs in a WeakSet so notification bookkeeping
does not retain them.

Unknown sync preserves active fetches and imports while recording new
peers. Incomplete-payload events upgrade idle entries and retry failed
work; request/source counters increase only for new roots. Envelope-only
entries still pass through validation before being upgraded.

Check entry identity after reconciliation, download, and processing
awaits so stale completions cannot overwrite or remove replacement
entries. Includes the race protections and adapted regression coverage
from #10347.

Closes #10114

**Validation**

- Gossip-handler, unknown-sync, and byte utility unit tests: 147 passed.
- Ten new retry/race regression cases reproduced failures before the
review fixes.
- Coverage includes Gloas and Heze payload deadlines, envelope-only
arrivals, duplicate notifications during fetch/import, idle retries,
overlapping reconciliation, and prune/re-admit races.
- After merging `unstable` at `7f05c22798`: `pnpm build`, `pnpm lint`,
and `pnpm --filter @lodestar/utils --filter @lodestar/beacon-node
check-types` passed.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

This PR was written primarily by OpenAI Codex.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nico Flaig <nflaig@protonmail.com>

author: Nico Flaig
subject: feat: add flag to disable validation of published execution payload bids (#10429)
body:
The beacon node currently runs full gossip validation on every bid
submitted via `POST /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_bids` before
broadcasting it. This adds latency to the publish path and is redundant
if the API is only used by a trusted local builder which constructs the
bid from the same chain state.

This adds a hidden `--api.disableBidValidation` flag which broadcasts
bids submitted via the API without validating them. Validation stays
enabled by default, skipping it must be an operator decision and not
sender controlled as a public node would otherwise blindly forward
invalid bids and get penalized by peers.

See ethereum/beacon-APIs#668 which makes validation optional in the
spec.

author: Marko Lazic
subject: refactor: use gossip validation for execution payload bids published via api (#10444)
body:
Follow-up to #10429.

With `--api.disableBidValidation` available, builders running in
production are expected to disable validation on the publish path. The
validate-on path is then mainly useful for testing, where the full
gossip rules are what we want to exercise rather than a lenient subset.
This removes `validateApiExecutionPayloadBid` and runs
`validateGossipExecutionPayloadBid` on bids submitted via `POST
/eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_bids` instead.

When validation runs, the bid is now also added to
`executionPayloadBidPool` and reported to the validator monitor,
mirroring the gossip handler. Gossip does not deliver our own published
messages back to us, so without this a proposer on the same node as the
builder never sees the bid in its pool. This matters for single-node
local testing (e.g. kurtosis).

Changes
- `publishExecutionPayloadBid` calls
`validateGossipExecutionPayloadBid`, then adds the bid to the pool and
registers it with the validator monitor using the returned
`proposerIndex`. Nothing is added to the pool when validation is
disabled.
- `validateApiExecutionPayloadBid` and
`RegenCaller.validateApiExecutionPayloadBid` removed.
- New metric
`lodestar_oppool_execution_payload_bid_pool_api_insert_outcome_total`,
same shape as the gossip one.
- Existing validator unit tests ported to
`validateGossipExecutionPayloadBid` (previously the gossip validator had
no direct unit coverage), with additional cases for the gossip-only
IGNORE rules. `mockedBeaconChain` gains `seenExecutionPayloadBids` and
`getParentExecutionRequests`.

Notes
- The pool insert happens inline before broadcast, not deferred to the
next event loop tick like the gossip handler does. There is no
validation result to propagate first on the api path, so deferring is
not needed.
- Reusing the gossip validator means a successfully validated api bid is
recorded in `seenExecutionPayloadBids`, so re-submitting the same bid
via the api is IGNOREd as already known. This matches what would happen
once the bid arrives via gossip anyway.

native portability
- 55 targeted tests covering the wrapper, CLI, execution predicates,
light-client proof persistence and spec assertions

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: check the parent payload before importing a repeat proposal in gloas (#10424)
body:
The gossip handler imports a signature-verified REPEAT_PROPOSAL sibling
into fork choice if its parent is known. That check only looks at the
parent block root, while gossip validation of a gloas block also
requires the parent payload (`bid.parent_block_hash`) to be known. A
gloas sibling whose parent payload has not been seen passes the handler
check, hits PARENT_PAYLOAD_UNKNOWN in block processing, and the default
catch reports the sender with LowToleranceError.

The handler now mirrors the validation check and uses
`getBlockHexAndBlockHash` for gloas blocks, so such a sibling is ignored
without penalty, same as a sibling with an unknown parent block.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: avoid legacy column scans during archiving (#10447)
body:
## Problem

Data columns are written to flat files since #8899, and #10223 clears
the legacy hot-column bucket during startup. The archiver still scans
that bucket for every finalized canonical block. After bulk deletion,
repeated scans over LevelDB tombstones can stall block archiving even
when no columns are migrated.

## Changes

- Remove the obsolete canonical hot-to-cold data-column migration.
- Await compaction of the legacy hot-column range after startup
deletion, including when the bucket is already empty from an earlier
startup.
- Preserve legacy cold-column reads, flat-file storage, retention
pruning, and noncanonical cleanup.

A restart on the fixed build performs the compaction automatically; a
separate manual compaction is not required for this fix. Startup
compaction can take time depending on the existing database.

## Validation

- The regression run failed on the original production code (9 expected
failures); all 39 targeted tests pass with the fix.
- Coverage includes Fulu/Gloas canonical archiving, already-archived
boundary blocks, empty and multi-batch bucket pruning, awaited
compaction, and legacy/flat-file column serving.
- `pnpm lint` passed (1886 files).
- `pnpm check-types` passed across the workspace.
- `pnpm --filter @lodestar/db build` passed.

## Spec compliance

Not applicable: internal database maintenance and removal of an obsolete
migration. No consensus transition or wire-format changes.

Written with AI assistance.

author: Chen Kai
subject: fix: avoid per-validator reads in fast confirmation scans (#10371)
body:
**Motivation**

With `--chain.fastConfirmation` and `--chain.nativeStateTransition` both
enabled, the JS heap grows by hundreds of MB per scanned state.

Fast confirmation runs every slot and three of its scans call
`state.getValidator(i)` for every active validator, only to read
`slashed` and the activation and exit epochs:

- `ensureVoteMaps`
- `getCurrentTargetScore`
- `getNodeSupportBetweenSlots`

On the JS state view this is free: `getReadonly(i).toValue()` returns
the value object the tree node already holds. On `NativeBeaconStateView`
each call crosses the binding, builds a new validator object with two
new byte arrays, and the view keeps it in `cachedValidator` for as long
as the view lives. Views do not share these objects, so every scanned
checkpoint or head state keeps its own full copy.

A Node simulation of the retained shape (objects built in JS, not
through the real binding) for 1M cached validators:

```
retained: Map<index, Validator> x 1M  heapUsed  570.0 MB  external  76.5 MB
retained: Uint16Array x 1M            heapUsed    0.0 MB  external   1.9 MB
```

**Description**

Read scan weights from `getEffectiveBalanceIncrementsZeroInactive()`
instead of reading validators one by one.

That array already zeroes validators that are inactive at the state's
epoch or slashed, which are exactly the conditions the three scans
checked, so the existing zero-weight skip covers them.
`getTotalActiveBalance` already requests the same array for the same
states in the same run, so this adds no new allocation on native views.

- `getZeroInactiveBalances`: new helper, memoized per state in
`FastConfirmationCache.zeroInactiveBalancesByState`. The JS
`BeaconStateView` recomputes the array on every call and
`getNodeSupportBetweenSlots` runs many times per slot, so without the
memo this change would add allocations on the non-native path.
- `ensureVoteMaps`, `getCurrentTargetScore`,
`getNodeSupportBetweenSlots`: drop the `getValidator()` reads.
- `getTotalActiveBalance`: goes through the same helper, which removes
its state/fallback branch.
- `getEquivocationScore`: unchanged. Slashed equivocators still count
there, so it cannot use the zero-inactive balances. Its `getValidator()`
reads sit behind `equivocating.has(i)` and are bounded by the
equivocating set.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The implementation and tests were written with Claude Code.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nazar Hussain <nazarhussain@gmail.com>

author: Chen Kai
subject: perf: select shuffle sha256 at runtime (#774)
body:
**Motivation**

The shuffle and proposer sampling hash a few hundred thousand short
messages per mainnet epoch with `std.crypto` SHA-256, which picks
hardware or portable code at compile time from the target CPU. Release
bindings are built with `-Dtarget` and no `-Dcpu`, so five of the six
targets run the portable code even on CPUs with SHA instructions. Only
aarch64-macos has them in its baseline.

Hardware SHA-256 instructions in a baseline x86_64 build:

```
main: 0
this PR: 32
```

**Description**

Hash the shuffle through blst's runtime-dispatched SHA-256 unless the
target CPU already guarantees SHA instructions.

- `sha256.hash` in the new `src/swap_or_not_shuffle/sha256.zig` calls
`blst_sha256`, or `std.crypto` inline when the target has the SHA
feature (native builds, aarch64-macos)
- the seven `Sha256.hash` call sites in the shuffle use it;
`state_transition` and the bindings already link blst
- CI also runs the shuffle tests with `-Dcpu=baseline`, since the native
test build only compiles the `std.crypto` branch

`bench_process_epoch`, Apple M5, ReleaseSafe mainnet, `-Dcpu=generic`
(the aarch64-linux release baseline), mean ms over three runs:

| Case | main | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `epoch_total` | 241.5 | 152.4 |
| `proposer_lookahead` | 160.8 | 73.4 |
| `state_root` (control) | 32.8 | 32.5 |

`unshuffleList` alone on a baseline build dropped from 153 to 113 ms on
the M5 and from 125 to 97 ms on a Ryzen 5 3600. Native builds are
unchanged.

Review notes:

- `blst_sha256` lives in `blst_aux.h`, which upstream may change; blst
is pinned and the tests fail on an incompatible upgrade.
- x86_64-macos is the only release target where the new path was not
executed (no Intel Mac or CI runner); it uses the same blst routine BLS
hash-to-curve already runs there.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Primarily authored with Claude Code; submitted as a draft for human
review.

author: bing
subject: fix(archive): rework pruning for non-canonical block variants (#10022)
body:
First raised in #9199, see
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/discussions/9199#discussioncomment-18280128
supersedes #10017

**Motivation**

The main issue is that archiveBlocks and indiscriminately pruned
canonical block-level data, and permanently deleted the light client
data.

Post-gloas a block occupies several ProtoArray nodes
(PENDING/EMPTY/FULL) sharing one blockRoot and only one of them is on
the ancestor walk, so getAllAncestorAndNonAncestorBlocks reports the
sibling variants of every canonical block as non-ancestors.
archiveBlocks keyed all deletions by blockRoot, which is fine for
payload-level data (envelopes, data columns: canonical ones were
migrated to the cold DB first) but permanently deleted the light client
witness and header of canonical epoch boundary blocks, which are never
migrated. Bootstrap for any finalized root older than the current
checkpoint then failed with RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

**Description**

We cannot build `nonCanonicalBlockRoots` by directly mapping
`finalizedNonCanonicalBlocks` because that array contains fork-choice
variants, not distinct blocks.

We instead use these intermediate data structures

`canonicalBlockRootHexes`: the set of distinct block roots on canonical
path
`nonCanonicalBlockByRoot`: a map of block root -> `ProtoBlock`
`orphanedPayloadBlocks`: a `[]ProtoBlock`

to get:

1) `nonCanonicalBlocks`, which we can get by filtering for what roots
that are not in `canonicalBlockRootHexes` in `nonCanonicalBlockByRoot`

2) Then anything that is of a FULL variant in the
`finalizedNonCanonicalBlocks` should be pruned by building
`orphanedPayloadBlocks`

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

created with the assistance of fable

author: Chen Kai
subject: perf: speed up sync committee rotation (#778)
body:
**Motivation**

`process_sync_committee_updates` runs once per sync committee period and
is slow when it does. On the mainnet state at slot 13,336,576 (985,824
active validators), sampling the 512 members takes 131 to 143 ms and
reading their pubkeys 7.4 ms.

Since Electra a 32 ETH validator is accepted about once in 64 tries, so
filling 512 seats examines about 29,000 candidates, each computing its
own 90-round shuffled index. The pubkeys are read from the state tree
and uncompressed again, although the pubkey cache already holds them.

**Description**

Sample Electra and later sync committees from one list shuffle, and take
the pubkeys from the pubkey cache. The selected committee is unchanged.

- `computeSyncCommitteeIndicesInto` unshuffles a copy of the active
indices once, then applies the same acceptance rule in the same order.
Inputs outside its range (one random byte, rounds outside 1..255) keep
`getCommitteeIndices`.
- `getCommitteeIndices` and the NAPI `computeSyncCommitteeIndices` write
into caller-owned output instead of allocating a result.
- `getNextSyncCommitteeIndices` uses the new sampler from Electra on.
Earlier forks keep the per-candidate sampler, since acceptance there is
close to certain.
- `getNextSyncCommittee` reads pubkeys with `getPubkeyBytes` and
aggregates with `PubkeyCache.aggregate`. A miss returns
`error.PubkeyNotFound`.
- New `sync_committee_rotation` case in `bench_process_epoch`, which
forces the rotation.

`sync_committee_rotation`, Apple M5, ReleaseSafe, mean of 50 iterations
over three alternating runs:

| Build CPU | main | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `apple_m1` | 137 to 160 ms | 25.0 ms |
| `generic` (software SHA) | 185 to 203 ms | 70.4 to 71.6 ms |

The list shuffle is used whenever it applies, without a cost model. It
only loses when few candidates are rejected, which on mainnet would need
an average effective balance above about 230 ETH. On current active
sets: mainnet 91.9 → 21.1 ms, Hoodi 136.2 → 29.4 ms, Sepolia 3.4 → 0.16
ms.


**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Primarily authored with Claude Code.

author: NC
subject: refactor: carry milliseconds through the fork choice timeliness API (#10455)
body:
## Motivation

Fork choice measured block receive delay, block import delay, and the
time into the proposer's slot in fractional seconds and compared them
against millisecond deadlines by multiplying by 1000. The producers
already had millisecond resolution, so nothing was truncated, but
dividing by 1000 and multiplying back introduces about 50 µs of float
error at Unix-timestamp magnitude. That flips the comparison at the
exact deadline millisecond: at 1667 ms into the slot `isProposingOnTime`
returned false where the spec's `get_time_into_slot_ms(store) <=
get_proposer_reorg_cutoff_ms()` says true.

At 12 s slots every deadline is a whole second and the boundary is never
hit. At 10 s slots the gloas deadlines land on 2500 ms and 7500 ms and
the reorg cutoff on 1667 ms, so exact comparisons matter.

## Description

Pass integer milliseconds end to end and drop the `* 1000` in the
predicates. No deadline value changes.

- `onBlock` takes `receiveDelayMs` and `importDelayMs`.
`getProposerHead`, `predictProposerHead`,
`shouldOverrideForkChoiceUpdate` and the `UpdateAndGetHeadOpt` union
take `msFromSlot`.
- `isBlockReceivedTimely`, `isBlockPtcTimely`, `isBlockImportedTimely`
and `isProposingOnTime` compare milliseconds directly.
- The beacon node computes `receiveDelayMs` as
`Math.round(seenTimestampSec * 1000) - computeTimeAtSlotMs(...)`, and
the import and proposer paths use `clock.msFromSlot`.
- Mocks and both spec runners updated. Vector ticks are whole seconds
per the test format, so the spec tests cannot exercise sub-second cases;
a new `blockTimeliness.test.ts` checks each predicate one millisecond
either side of the 2500 ms and 7500 ms gloas deadlines at a 10 s slot,
and `getProposerHead.test.ts` gains cases exactly at and one millisecond
after the 1667 ms cutoff.

author: NC
subject: fix: floor slot component durations as the spec does (#10456)
body:
## Motivation

`getSlotComponentDurationMs` converts a basis-point fraction of the slot
into milliseconds with `Math.round`. The spec's
`get_slot_component_duration_ms` is `basis_points * SLOT_DURATION_MS //
BASIS_POINTS`, floor division. The two differ whenever the product is
not a whole millisecond.

At 10 s slots every mainnet basis-point value is exact, so nothing
changes. At 12 s slots the product is `bps * 1.2`, and 3333 bps gives
3999.6: the spec floors to 3999 ms, Lodestar rounded to 4000 ms. That is
the pre-gloas attestation and sync message deadline, so a block arriving
at exactly 3999 ms into the slot was timely for Lodestar and late for
the spec. The other mainnet values (1667, 6667, 9167 bps) round and
floor to the same number, and every gloas deadline is a multiple of 500
bps and unaffected.

## Description

Switch to `Math.floor`, with a comment pointing at the pinned spec
function, and pin the values in a config unit test: 3333, 6667, 1667 and
2500 bps at 12 s, and 3333, 1667 and 2500 bps at 10 s.

The minimal preset moves the same deadlines from 2000 to 1999 ms. No
test anywhere pinned the old rounded values; the validator service,
fork-choice, and beacon-node chain, API, unknown-block sync and gossip
processor suites all pass against the rebuilt config package.

Spec test vectors cannot tell round from floor because their ticks are
whole seconds, so the config unit test is the only pin.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: recompute unrealized checkpoints for blocks with slashings (#10467)
body:
**Motivation**

`ForkChoice.onBlock` skips `computeUnrealizedCheckpoints()` for a
same-epoch child whose parent is already justified in the block epoch,
and reuses the parent's unrealized checkpoints instead. That assumes a
child can't have lower unrealized checkpoints than its parent. Slashings
in the child block break that assumption: they lower the unslashed
target balance of the child state, so its unrealized justification can
drop. The spec's `compute_pulled_up_tip` always recomputes.

Lighthouse fixed the same shortcut in
https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/pull/9471.

**Description**

- Only take the reuse path when the block has no proposer or attester
slashings
- Add unit tests: a same-epoch block without slashings keeps the
parent's checkpoints, and one with a proposer or attester slashing
recomputes them

Verified locally: fork-choice unit tests (319 passing, the new ones fail
without the fix), fork_choice minimal spec tests v1.7.0-beta.4 (516
passing), biome and tsc clean.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implemented and tested with AI assistance (lodekeeper).

Co-authored-by: lodekeeper <lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>

[10-23](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/39893885557)
and
[10-24](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/40057373081).
No assertion fails; the single vitest worker runs out of heap near the
end of gloas.

Root cause is in the test harness, not in fork choice.
`forkChoiceTestRunner` builds a fresh `testLogger("executionEngine")`
and a fresh `getMockedBeaconDb()` (which builds its own `testLogger()`)
for every test case:

- Each winston logger registers a `process.on("uncaughtException")`
listener (`handleExceptions: true` on the console transport) that is
never removed. Every CI run, green ones included, prints
`MaxListenersExceededWarning: 11 uncaughtException listeners added to
[process]` seconds after start.
- Each mocked db creates ~88 `vi.fn()` mocks, and vitest keeps every
mock in a module-level registry forever. `clearMocks` only clears call
history.

Measured locally on the altair fork (1472 cases) with forced GC after
every 25 cases:

| Build | Retained growth per case | Projected over 10304 cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| f39fad29a (last green nightly) | 331 KB | 3.3 GB |
| 9cb14e338 (first red nightly) | 373 KB | 3.7 GB |
| this PR | 26 KB | 0.3 GB |

Heap snapshots at case 30 and case 90 confirm that chains, states and
metric registries are released; only the loggers and mocks grow strictly
per case. The suite has run within ~25 min of its timeout since gloas
vectors were enabled on 09-11, already GC-thrashing during gloas. #10022
added six explicit mocks and two automocked repositories to
`getMockedBeaconDb()`, which raised per-case retention by ~11% and
crossed the limit. That PR is not at fault; any change to the mocked db
would have done it.

**Description**

Create the execution engine logger and the mocked db once per module in
`forkChoiceTestRunner`, and the logger once in `mockedBeaconDb`. The
runner never customises the mocks per case and `clearMocks` resets call
history between cases, so sharing one instance is safe.

With this change retained heap stays flat across the altair fork (137 MB
at case 1450 vs 632 MB before) and the fork runs ~18% faster from less
GC pressure. The full suite was not run locally; the next nightly is the
end-to-end check.

Follow-ups, out of scope here:
- A `handleExceptions: false` option for `testLogger` would remove the
listener leak from the ~100 other per-test logger call sites in
beacon-node tests.
- Two `sleep()` calls keep closed chains reachable for 3 to 4 s after
`chain.close()`: the half-slot validator-monitor sleep in
`BeaconChain.onClockSlot` has no abort signal, and
`PersistentCheckpointStateCache` is constructed without one. Bounded,
but it inflates peak memory in the suite.

author: Nazar Hussain
subject: fix: build fuzz harnesses in ReleaseSafe (#805)
body:
The fuzz image and CI's `build-fuzz` job built the harnesses in
`ReleaseFast`, which compiles out `std.debug.assert` and Zig's bounds
and overflow checks. Every SSZ harness checks its round-trip invariant
with `assert`, so those checks never fired: the campaigns could only
find bugs that happen to segfault.

This builds both in ReleaseSafe. `Dockerfile.fuzz` takes `--build-arg
OPTIMIZE=ReleaseFast` for comparisons.

### Verified locally (arm64 image)

- All 13 targets build; every seed in `corpus/` replays clean on both
builds.
- Two bugs planted in `ssz_basic`:

  | input | ReleaseFast | ReleaseSafe |
  |---|---|---|
  | round-trip mismatch | exit 0 | 134, `reached unreachable code` |
| out-of-bounds read | exit 0 | 134, `index out of bounds: index 2, len
2` |

- Throughput under AFL++ (2 min, 1 core): about −22% on SSZ targets, −8%
on `bls_signature`; edges found slightly up.

amd64 is not verified locally (Rosetta crashes in `translate-c` on
`blst.h`); this PR's `build-fuzz` job builds it on amd64.

Once published, fuzz campaigns may report new crashes from invariants
that were silently failing.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: avoid slow LevelDB scans over deleted legacy data column entries (#10460)
body:
**Motivation**

Follow-up to #10447. On `public-hoodi-hzax41-0`, a long-running
supernode, LevelDB scans over legacy data column entries that were
deleted long ago slowed both startup and every archive job:

- Startup stalled about 20 minutes after `Flat file store initialized`.
The reverse lookup in bucket 58 took 712 s and the wipe scan of bucket
57 took 381 s, although both buckets had no live keys. Legacy column
entries deleted while long archive scans held a snapshot had stayed in
the bottom LevelDB level (224.8 GB). `compactRange` never rewrites the
bottom level, so the compaction from #10447 was a no-op there.
- The legacy column prune runs `keys({lt: cutoff})` from the start of
bucket 58 on every archive job. The bucket is not written since flat
files and only shrinks from the front, so every prune walks all deleted
entries LevelDB has not compacted.

**Description**

- At startup, before the first lookup into buckets 57 and 58, check the
size of the hot column bucket plus the pruned part of the legacy column
archive. Above 1 GiB, write a key at each end of the range, compact, and
delete the keys again. That forces the bottom files to be rewritten. On
hoodi-0 the same steps took 475 s once, cut the range from 224.8 GB to
0, and startup went from 20 min to 3 ms
- Add `pruneBefore(slot)` to the legacy data column archive repository.
It resumes from the slot the previous prune ended at, and the first
prune of a process compacts the range it deletes from

author: NC
subject: fix: stop flooring the import-time seen timestamp of a block (#10453)
body:
## Motivation

`processBlocks` stamps a block with the current time when the caller
passes no `seenTimestampSec`, which is the case for unknown-block sync
and range sync. That stamp was floored to a whole second. At 12 s slots
every deadline lands on a whole second, so flooring never changed the
outcome. At 10 s slots `ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS_GLOAS = 2500` becomes 2500
ms, and a block imported at 2.9 s into its slot measures as 2 s and
still counts as timely for proposer boost. The same applies to the PTC
deadline.

## Description

Keep the fractional import time. Stamping at import time is deliberate
for these paths and now says so in a comment: the spec cannot run
`on_block` until the parent is known and records timeliness at that
moment, so for a block that could not be imported on arrival the import
time is the spec's clock. The unknown-block sync delay for already known
proposers relies on the same stamp to deny proposer boost, and now
carries a note to that effect.

Two unit tests pin the fallback to a fractional stubbed time and the
precedence of an explicit opts value.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: use the correct PTC duties dependent root for the Gloas fork epoch (#10468)
body:
The PTC of the Gloas fork epoch is computed by `upgrade_to_gloas` from
effective balances that are updated at the end of the last pre-Gloas
epoch, so blocks of that epoch can still change it. The dependent root
returned for it was the attester decision root two epochs earlier, which
does not cover those blocks. A reorg replacing blocks of the last
pre-Gloas epoch could change the committee without the validator client
noticing, and the fork epoch duties are never polled again after the
start of the epoch.

- the beacon node returns the block root at the last slot before the
fork as the dependent root of the fork epoch PTC duties
- the validator client matches the fork epoch duties against the head
event's current duty dependent root, which carries that root

All other epochs are unchanged. Spec text in
https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/671, see
https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/issues/670 for the analysis.

author: Nazar Hussain
subject: feat(fuzz): add a minimize command for the fuzz platform (#808)
body:
**TL;DR:** the image gets a minimize command, declared in a label. The
fuzz platform will run it on a schedule to keep each campaign's state
small.

## Motivation

A campaign's state on the fuzz platform grows for as long as it runs:
AFL++'s queue, plus `plot_data` and stats, which keep growing even on a
plateaued target. The platform will run each project's minimize command
on a schedule, and will refuse to start a target whose image doesn't
declare one.

## Description

- `test/fuzz/docker/minimize.sh`, declared with the label
`org.chainsafe.fuzz.minimize`. While the campaign is stopped, it:
  - saves any crash not yet in `failures/`;
- runs `afl-cmin` over the queue, the previous corpus and the committed
seeds;
  - swaps the result into `state/corpus` and deletes `state/afl`.

If it fails, the state is left as it was, and it is safe to kill at any
point.
- `run-fuzz.sh` starts from `state/corpus` when it exists. The shared
setup moves to `lib.sh`.
- `afl-cmin` is added to the image.
- CI runs the labelled command after the smoke campaign, then checks
that the next start uses the new corpus.

## Testing

Tested locally on `ssz-lists` under the platform's restrictions: 56
inputs minimized to 35, with edge coverage unchanged (171 before and
after). Also checked the restart, interrupted-swap, failure, no-op and
unsaved-crash cases.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: bound engine getBlobs retries and request blobs before newPayload (#10329)
body:
`GetBlobsTracker` only deduplicated in-flight requests, so every gossip
column that arrived after the EL had answered `null` triggered another
`engine_getBlobsV2` for the same block, about 14 per blob block on a
non-supernode, all with the same answer. It also deferred the request to
the next event loop tick, which let block processing issue `newPayload`
first. Nimbus-eth1 and Nethermind drop a transaction's blobs as soon as
the payload is validated, so on those ELs the request could never
succeed. Sequence from a debug run, Lodestar on the left, Nimbus on the
right:

```
cl 15.191  Call engine api newPayload slot=8
cl 15.194  Trigger getBlobsV2 for block slot=8
el 15.204  POST /engine/v1/payloads
el 15.205  New payload received and validated number=8
el 15.205  POST /engine/v1/blobs/v2 -> 204
el 15.283 .. 15.390  seven more POST /engine/v1/blobs/v2 -> 204
```

- the request is sent synchronously from `triggerGetBlobs`, so it leaves
before `processBlock` reaches the engine
- after a `null` answer or a failed call the block root is retried at
most `MAX_GET_BLOBS_ATTEMPTS` times and only once
`GET_BLOBS_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS` has passed, since the answer only changes
if the EL receives the transactions later. The map of failed attempts is
capped at 64 block roots
- the v1 path gets a `catch` as well, a rejected
`getBlobSidecarsFromExecution` was unhandled before

Closes #10321

---------

Co-authored-by: Lodekeeper <258435968+lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: lodekeeper <lodekeeper@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: treat data availability timeouts of gossip blocks and payloads as unavailable data (#10474)
body:
A gossip block or payload envelope whose data does not arrive within the
availability wait rejects the import with a `TimeoutError`.
`processBlocks` wraps it into `BEACON_CHAIN_ERROR`, which the block
gossip handler treats as a bad block: the relaying peer is downscored
and the error is logged at warn. The envelope handler gets the raw error
and logs it at error level. In both cases BlockInputSync is already
pulling the data and retries the import, so there is nothing to act on
and nothing the peer did wrong.

- the availability waits throw `DATA_UNAVAILABLE` block and payload
errors instead of leaking the `TimeoutError`
- both gossip handlers log it at debug without reporting the peer

Range sync is unchanged, `DATA_UNAVAILABLE` is not peer attributable,
same as the wrapped error before.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: do not prefer an unsatisfied payload as head during its own slot (#10416)
body:
Fork choice only acts on the inclusion list verdict from the next slot
on, through `should_extend_payload`. During the block's own slot
`getPayloadStatusTiebreaker` returns the raw payload status, so the head
stays on the FULL variant of a payload the node already knows it will
not extend. Everything reading the head during that slot gets the wrong
variant: the next slot payload is prepared on FULL and rebuilt at
proposal time, and bids for the next slot are checked against the wrong
parent hash.

Rank such a payload below its EMPTY variant during the block's own slot,
as proposed in https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5769.
Same-slot attestations support the PENDING node, so both variants weigh
zero during that slot and the tiebreaker alone picks the variant. Weight
decides as before once attestations from the next slot exist.

A/B on a kurtosis heze devnet (3 Lodestar nodes on ethrex ddffde4, which
still builds unsatisfied payloads, spamoor): with this change the head
of a block with an unsatisfied payload stays EMPTY through its own slot
(head_v2 stream) and the following proposal reused the prepared payload
built on EMPTY, `prepType=Cached`, 2 of 2. On unstable every such
proposal rebuilt, `prepType=Reorged`, 4 of 4.

Supersedes #10410.

author: bing
subject: fix(api): type historical summaries proof nodes as Bytes32 (#10487)
body:
**Motivation**

The proof returned by getHistoricalSummaries is a Merkle branch of
32-byte nodes, but the response type declared ArrayOf(Bytes8).

JSON responses still carried 32-byte hex because ByteVectorType.toJson
is toHexString(value) which returns the correct length.

Since every consumer reads JSON, the broken paths were never hit: a
client sending Accept: application/octet-stream got a 500 from a
RangeError in serialize, and the typed client threw on fromJson of any
non-empty proof.

The only test mocked an empty proof, which
exercises none of those.

**Description**

- Change the type from `ssz.Bytes8` to `ssz.Bytes32`
- Use a non-empty proof in the test and add a ssz test path

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

fable discovered this and fixed this

author: Nico Flaig
subject: refactor: remove non-spec `none` broadcast validation level (#10500)
body:
`none` is not a beacon-APIs value. It was added in
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/6308 so the unknown block
sync simulation could push a block with an unknown parent through to
`processBlock`, back then the only publish path that emitted
`blockUnknownParent`. Since
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9025 the `consensus` level
emits it before rejecting with `PARENT_BLOCK_UNKNOWN`, so the test no
longer needs it. Nothing else used it, the validator client already
rejects it on the command line.

Keeping it was a footgun, blocks were gossiped before any check ran and
envelopes were imported with the signature marked as verified.

- remove `none` from `BroadcastValidation`, the simulation uses
`consensus` and the unit test `gossip`
- reject unknown levels with a 400 instead of logging a warning and
publishing without validation
- drop the hidden `broadcastValidationStrictness` option, it only
governed that fallback

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: use the envelope's own payload status for `execution_optimistic` (#10484)
body:
`getSignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` returns the `execution_optimistic`
of the block, which for a gloas block is the status of the payload it
builds on (`bid.parent_block_hash`), inherited by the PENDING variant at
import. The envelope is the block's own payload, so a SYNCING envelope
on a VALID parent was served as `execution_optimistic: false`.

The flag now comes from the block's FULL variant, the fork choice node
created when the envelope was imported, and is `false` once finalized.
An unfinalized block without a FULL variant has not imported its
envelope yet and returns 404, the same as block lookups for a block that
is not in fork choice. Before, an envelope still in the input cache was
served with the block's flag.

Related to https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/issues/672.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: return each gloas block once from fork choice block summaries (#10483)
body:
`getBlockSummariesByParentRoot` and `getBlockSummariesAtSlot` return
every proto-array node, for a gloas block that is its PENDING and EMPTY
variant plus FULL once the payload arrived. `getBlockHeaders` pushes a
header per node, so `?parent_root=` returns each gloas child two or
three times and `?slot=` does the same for non-canonical blocks at that
slot.

Both now return one summary per block, the default variant (FULL
pre-gloas, PENDING for gloas). The other caller, `isValidDependentRoot`,
only checks that a child exists and is unaffected.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: fix: keep the engine off an unsatisfied payload at envelope import (#10486)
body:
At envelope import, step 7 sends the envelope's block hash to the
execution engine as forkchoice head whenever the cached head has the
same block root. It does not look at the inclusion list verdict recorded
a few lines earlier, so an unsatisfied payload becomes the engine head
although fork choice does not extend it and the next proposer builds on
the parent payload. The engine builds mempool and inclusion list state
on it until the next forkchoiceUpdated, the prepare call about 6.7s into
the slot on the heze devnet rehearsal, then reorgs.

Skip the update when the payload is recorded as not satisfying the
constraints. `isPayloadInclusionListSatisfied` is true for every
pre-heze payload and for a VALID payload without a verdict, so nothing
else changes. The spec sends no forkchoiceUpdated at envelope import,
this one is a Lodestar optimization behind the
`disableImportExecutionFcU` chain option.

Independent of #10416, which fixes the beacon head for the same slot.

author: Nazar Hussain
subject: chore: use biome for markdown and yaml, drop prettier (#10492)
body:
**Motivation**

[Biome 2.6](https://biomejs.dev/blog/biome-v2-6/) supports Markdown and
YAML. Prettier was only used to format Markdown, so Biome can cover it
and we drop one tool.

**Description**

- Upgrade `@biomejs/biome` to `^2.6.3` and include `**/*.md`, `**/*.yml`
and `**/*.yaml`.
- Markdown formatter set to Prettier's defaults (`lineWidth: 80`,
`proseWrap: "preserve"`), frontmatter parsing enabled for
`.claude/skills`.
- YAML is linted only. The formatter is disabled for now to keep this PR
small.
- Excluded: `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `specrefs/*.yml` (regenerated and diffed
by ethspecify in CI) and `test/fixtures`.
- Remove `prettier`, its config (`.prettierrc.js`, `.prettierignore`),
the `docs:lint` / `docs:lint:fix` scripts and their CI steps. `pnpm
lint` in the Tests workflow runs on every PR and now covers Markdown.
Generated docs are gitignored, so both tools skipped them anyway.
- VS Code uses Biome for Markdown. The Prettier extension is no longer
recommended, and YAML has no default formatter until Biome YAML
formatting is enabled.

Compatibility on our files:

- Markdown: 83 of 86 files identical to Prettier output. Two docs lists
get blank lines around fenced code. `packages/cli/README.md` had a table
without surrounding blank lines, so GitHub rendered the "Append
`--help`" sentence as a table row. Fixed the source.
- YAML: Biome output is identical to Prettier on all 80 files.

Side effects of upgrading from Biome 2.2:

- 37 TS files: 2.6 now sorts exports and changed some line breaking.
Applied with `biome check --write`, ordering and whitespace only.
Verified the runtime module evaluation order (`import` / `export ...
from`) is unchanged in every file.
- New findings on 2.6 fixed in stacked PRs, now merged into this branch:
#10493 (`noFloatingPromises`), #10494 (`noMisusedPromises`), #10495
(`noUnsafeOptionalChaining`), #10496 (`noNonNullAssertedOptionalChain`),
#10497 (`useMathMinMax`). All rules are back at their original level.
- `useMathMinMax` is off for `packages/state-transition/src`. Its fixes
would break bigint operands, which are common there.
- `useImportExtensions` has a false positive on JSON imports through the
`spec-tests-version.json` symlinks (its fix rewrites them to `.js`).
Suppressed on those 4 imports. Fixed one real `.ts` import.
- `@chainsafe/biomejs-config` uses the deprecated
`linter.rules.recommended` key, so Biome prints a deprecation notice.
Needs a fix upstream.

author: Raphina Liu
subject: fix: return 400 when sync committee message validator is not in the sync committee (#10502)
body:
**Motivation**

Lodestar's `POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/sync_committees` returns 200 and
drops a message whose `validator_index` is out of range or not in the
current sync committee. The [beacon-APIs
spec](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/bc3384f9cb1f02169d4fcb81e7da4da329b857ee/apis/beacon/pool/sync_committees.yaml#L9-L11)
requires a 400 with details of which messages failed and why. A message
with an out-of-range index fails the gossip rule `[REJECT] The validator
index is valid`. A message from a validator that is not in the sync
committee fails `[REJECT] The subnet_id is valid for the given
validator`.

**Description**

- Replace the early `return` with `throw new
SyncCommitteeError(GossipAction.REJECT, {code:
VALIDATOR_NOT_IN_SYNC_COMMITTEE, validatorIndex})`. Gossip validation
throws the same error in `validateGossipSyncCommitteeExceptSig`. The
existing `catch` adds the error to the `IndexedError` failures, so the
endpoint returns 400. The handler still adds the valid messages in the
same request to the pool and publishes them.
- Add unit tests for an out-of-range index, a valid validator that is
not in the sync committee, and a request with one invalid and one valid
message. Each test fails without the fix.

Closes #10488

- [ x ] External Contributors: I have read the [contributor
guidelines](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/unstable/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-assistance-notice)
and disclosed my usage of AI below.

This PR was written by me and Claude Code, we human found and reproduced
the bug on a local devnet, then reviewed the change and the tests.

author: twoeths
subject: fix: verify cached envelope signature on publish (#10499)
body:
The publish flow validates the submitted envelope but then imports the
cached `PayloadEnvelopeInput` with `validSignature: true`. If range sync
already cached a different envelope for the same block root before
verifying it, that envelope is imported with its signature marked as
verified and skips the BLS and `executionRequestsRoot` checks at import.

- only pass `validSignature: true` when the cached envelope is the one
this request validated, otherwise the import verifies it
- add tests for the submitted envelope and for an envelope cached by
another source

Rebased onto https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10500, which
removed the `none` level. Every remaining level verifies the submitted
envelope, so the gate is just the identity check.

author: Lodekeeper
subject: fix: retry post-gloas getBlobs after a failed attempt (#10479)
body:
**Motivation**

Follow-up to #10329. Pre-gloas, every gossip data column re-triggers
getBlobs, so a `null` answer is retried up to `MAX_GET_BLOBS_ATTEMPTS`
times. Post-gloas, getBlobs is triggered once per block, from the bid
after block import, so a `null` answer is never retried.

**Description**

- Post-gloas, every failed getBlobsV2 attempt (`null` or a rejected
request) arms the existing trailing retry. That gives the same cap of 3
attempts at least 1 s apart as pre-gloas. Retries stop once the sampled
columns are complete
- Pre-gloas behavior is unchanged
- Remove the TODO at the bid trigger, since the retry now lives in
`GetBlobsTracker`

Retries are not timed to a point in the slot. On glamsterdam-devnet-8
over the last 24h, the post-gloas `null` rate of the single request
depended mostly on the EL: reth 1%, geth, besu and nimbusel about 5%,
erigon 16%, ethrex about 30%, nethermind 61%. That points at EL blob
pool behavior more than at when in the slot we ask, so it doesn't
support picking a slot time yet.

Written with AI assistance (Claude), including the devnet data,
implementation, tests and description.

subject: fix: decode gloas deposit requests without the electra limit (#10515)
body:
**Motivation**

Gloas changes `DepositRequests` to a progressive list without a limit.
Execution requests from the EL are still decoded with the Electra type,
which caps deposits at `MAX_DEPOSIT_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD`, so a Gloas
payload with more deposit requests than that fails to decode.

**Description**

- Decode deposit requests with `ssz.gloas.DepositRequests` from Gloas
on. The wire bytes are the same; only the list limit differs
- Add a test that decodes `MAX_DEPOSIT_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD + 1` deposit
requests for Gloas and still rejects them pre-Gloas

author: Nico Flaig
subject: test: reuse one node pool across Zig spec test cases (#10524)
body:
Every Zig spec test case allocates its own `Node.Pool` sized for the
largest state, 1M nodes for the ssz tests and 10M nodes for the mainnet
state transition tests. At 44 bytes per node that is 44 MB and 440 MB
per case, and safe builds fill the whole buffer on allocation and again
on free. This setup dominates the runtime: ssz_static minimal runs
56,826 cases in ~35 min (~36 ms per case) and mainnet operations runs
2,562 cases in ~20 min (~0.45 s per case), both close to 1 GB/s of pool
churn. The generated sanity, random and finality tests also allocated
the pool before skipping cases that don't exist for the preset.

Cases now share one pool per test binary. A case that leaves nodes
behind drops the pool, so the next case still starts from an empty one.

- add `acquirePool` / `releasePool` to the spec and ssz test case
helpers
- use the shared pool in the ssz cases, the operations, epoch
processing, rewards, fork and transition runners, and the generated
sanity, random and finality tests
- run ssz_static spec tests in ReleaseSafe for both presets

---------

author: Nico Flaig
subject: chore: let Lerna publish the native wrapper package (#10527)
body:
publish-dev has failed on every unstable push since
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10513. zapi published
`@lodestar/native` seconds before `lerna publish from-package` checked
the registry. npm still reported the version as unpublished, so Lerna
ran the wrapper's `prepublishOnly` guard and the job failed. Only the 7
native packages reached npm, and the Docker publish was skipped.

This bumps zapi to 4.3.0 (https://github.com/ChainSafe/zapi/pull/88) and
splits publishing by package type:

- zapi builds and publishes only the platform packages, with
`--skip-existing` so a failed release can be re-run from any point.
- Lerna publishes the wrapper with the other packages. Its `prepack`
script (`zapi prepublish --main-only`) pins the platform packages as
`optionalDependencies`, replacing the throwing guard.

Verified locally with fake artifacts:

- `zapi publish --platforms-only --skip-existing --dry-run` would
publish all 6 platforms for an unpublished version and skips all 6 for
`1.51.0-dev.122e5d5f21`.
- `lerna publish from-package --dry-run` found only
`@lodestar/native@1.50.1` unpublished, ran `prepack`, and the packed
tarball lists all 6 platform `optionalDependencies`.

author: Nico Flaig
subject: chore(ci): key the Zig cache by host glibc and kernel (#10528)
body:
Build takes 2.3 to 3.2 min since
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10513, up from about 1 min.
108 s of that is compiling the native bindings, even when no Zig code
changed.

setup-zig keys its cache by job id only, so the `build` jobs of Tests,
Sim tests and Check docs share one cache and restores pick the newest.
Check docs runs on `ubuntu-latest` (glibc 2.39) and finishes last, while
the other two run on Warp (glibc 2.35). Zig's native target includes the
host glibc and kernel versions, so the Warp builds never hit that cache.
On https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10527, Build restored the
Check docs cache from f2b568e3d0 and recompiled from scratch.

This adds the host glibc and kernel release to the setup-zig cache key,
so jobs only share caches built for a matching host. The build cache key
reuses the same glibc detection.

The first run on this branch starts from empty caches. The effect shows
from the next commit without Zig changes, which should bring Build back
to about 1 min.
